# TIMELINE — The Flat Chronological Index

> **Every notable event in the corpus, sorted on the cosmic clock.** Auto-generated cross-index: each entry links to the file where it is detailed. Hindu chronology is cyclic and often unordered within an age, so sequence inside each period is approximate. Back to the [master index](README.md) · see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for how to use this.

**3493 distinct events** across 9 periods. Current address: 7th (Vaivasvata) Manvantara → 28th Mahāyuga → **Kali Yuga**.

---


## Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation  ·  205 events

*The creation accounts (Vedic, Upaniṣadic, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, Śākta) and the first emanations — catalogued as parallel variants, not a single sequence.*

- **Being wills to become many (Chāndogya cosmogony)** — In the beginning Being alone (Sat) exists; it wills 'May I be many' and emits heat, water and food, from which all forms recombine _(actors: Sat (Being))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2)
- **Birth of Agastya from the Pot** — Mitra and Varuna, aroused at the sight of the apsara Urvashi, spill their seed into a clay pot, from which Agastya (and in some tellings Vasishtha) is born _(actors: Agastya, Mitra, Varuna, Urvashi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Rigveda 7.33; Mahabharata; Puranas)
- **Birth of Aruṇa from the Broken Egg** — Impatient Vinatā cracks one egg early, releasing the half-formed Aruṇa, who curses her to 500 years of slavery and flies up to become Sūrya's charioteer and the red dawn _(actors: Aruṇa, Vinatā, Sūrya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Birth of Brahmā from the navel-lotus** — Brahmā emerges seated on the lotus growing from Viṣṇu's navel as Viṣṇu reclines on Śeṣa in the cosmic ocean at the start of each Kalpa _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Gaṇeśa and the elephant head** — Pārvatī forms a guardian boy from her body-paste; Śiva beheads him for barring the door, then revives him with an elephant's head as Gajānana with first-worship precedence _(actors: Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā, Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Narmadā from Śiva's Sweat** — While Shiva performs tapas on Mount Riksha/Mekala, a drop of his perspiration falls to earth and becomes the maiden Narmada, whom he commands to flow as a sin-destroying river _(actors: Shiva, Narmada)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/narmada-parikrama.md) — (Matsya Purana; Skanda Purana (Reva-khanda))
- **Birth of the Rākṣasas from Brahmā** — As Brahmā recited the Vedas at the dawn of creation he grew hungry, and beings born of his hunger cried 'rakṣāma!' becoming rākṣasas (and those of thirst, yakṣas) _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.5)
- **Birth of Yama and Yami** — Yama and his twin sister Yami are born to Vivasvat/Surya and Saranyu/Sanjna as the primordial mortal pair _(actors: Yama, Yami, Surya, Saranyu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.17; Puranas)
- **Brahma emits the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — At the dawn of the kalpa Brahma produces his first conscious offspring from mind without union, the Prajapatis and first Saptarshis _(actors: Brahma, Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasishtha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Manusmriti 1.34-35; Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Brahma–Vishnu Supremacy Quarrel and Lingodbhava** — Brahma and Vishnu dispute who is supreme, and Shiva manifests as a boundless flaming pillar of light (jyotirlinga) piercing the three worlds to settle the contest _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara Samhita); Linga Purana)
- **Brahmā Creates Mānasarovara from His Mind** — Brahmā forms the lake Mānasa-sarovara out of his consciousness as the abode of his haṃsa mount, manifesting it on earth for the gods' austerities at Kailāsa's foot _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (Skanda Purana, Manasakhanda; Matsya Purana)
- **Brahmā creates the worlds (Brahma Purāṇa sarga)** — Brahmā emerges from the cosmic egg / Viṣṇu's navel-lotus and brings forth the Prajāpatis, the Manus, and the worlds _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Pūrva-bhāga))
- **Brahmā First Sacrifices in Ānandavana (Founding of Kāśī)** — In its origin-myth Kashi is the first light-pillar of creation, the ground where Brahmā first performed sacrifice and the liṅga of light manifested in the grove of bliss _(actors: Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Brahmā Slays the Demon Vajranābha with the Lotus** — Brahma strikes down the asura Vajranabha with the lotus he holds; petals fall to earth at three places and well up as the three Pushkar lakes _(actors: Brahma, Vajranabha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Brahmā's lotus-creation** — The Purāṇas narrate the primary creation (sarga), including Brahmā's emergence and the lotus-creation unfolding the universe at the start of his day _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Padma Purāṇa; Matsya/Vāyu/Viṣṇu Purāṇas)
- **Brahmā's Prakṛṣṭa Yajña at Prayāga** — At the start of creation Brahma performs the supreme prakrsta yajna at the confluence, giving Prayaga its name and making it the cosmic sacrificial altar _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Matsya Purana (Prayaga-mahatmya); Padma Purana)
- **Cosmos emitted from Death/Hunger (Bṛhadāraṇyaka cosmogony)** — In the horse-sacrifice opening, Death (Mṛtyu / Prajāpati / Hunger) appears as the primal reality from which the worlds are emitted _(actors: Mṛtyu/Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.1–1.2)
- **Creation by Vishnu/Vasudeva (sarga)** — Vishnu as material and efficient cause unfolds prakriti and the tattvas, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's emergence in the model Puranic cosmogony _(actors: Vishnu/Vasudeva, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1))
- **Creation of Svayambhuva Manu & Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his body into male and female halves, producing the first human couple and progenitors of mankind _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Manusmriti 1; Vishnu Purana 1; Bhagavata Purana 3-4)
- **Creation, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's day (Vamana)** — The Vamana Purana supplies a sarga account of the cosmic egg (anda) and the unfolding of the elements and the gods at the start of the kalpa _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana)
- **Diggajas Created by Brahmā** — The eight directional world-elephants, headed by Airāvata, are born at creation and ordained by Brahmā to uphold the earth at the quarters and serve as the Dikpālas' mounts _(actors: Brahmā, Aṣṭa-diggaja)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/dikpalas-and-lokapalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8; Mātaṅga-līlā)
- **Hayagrīva recovers the stolen Vedas** — Viṣṇu in his horse-headed Hayagrīva form recovers the Vedas stolen from Brahmā by the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha (or slays the asura Hayagrīva who stole them) _(actors: Hayagrīva (Viṣṇu), Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Hayagrīva Upaniṣad; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Indra Shears the Wings of the Mountains** — In primeval ages winged mountains flew about crushing settlements until Indra cut off their wings with his vajra to fix them in place _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Brahmanda Purana; Kathasaritsagara)
- **Kṛṣṇa divides into male and female (Brahmavaivarta cosmogony)** — The universe issues from Kṛṣṇa as Para-Brahman, who first divides into male (Kṛṣṇa) and female (Rādhā/Prakṛti); Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are produced as functionaries _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Brahma-khaṇḍa))
- **Kaśyapa's progeny seed the beings of the cosmos** — Kaśyapa's unions produce the opposed classes of beings: Ādityas (devas) by Aditi, Daityas by Diti, Dānavas by Danu, Nāgas by Kadrū, and Garuḍa and Aruṇa by Vinatā _(actors: Kaśyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/README.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.6)
- **Liṅgodbhava** — An infinite pillar of fire erupts in the Brahmā-Viṣṇu supremacy quarrel; neither finds its end, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute and origin of the liṅga _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Kūrma Purāṇa, Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Liṅgodbhava — the pillar of fire** — When Brahmā and Viṣṇu quarrel over supremacy, an infinite fiery liṅga erupts; both fail to find its end, Viṣṇu concedes and Brahmā lies and is cursed, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā; Liṅga Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Lingodbhava** — Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite pillar of fire (jyotirlinga) and challenges them to find its ends, establishing the origin of linga-worship _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara-samhita); cf. Linga, Kurma, Vamana, Skanda, Brahmanda, Vayu Puranas)
- **Lingodbhava — rising of the cosmic pillar of light** — Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite blazing jyotirlinga and neither finds its end — Vishnu (as Varaha) admits failure while Brahma lies and is cursed to receive no worship, establishing the linga as supreme _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu (Varaha), the ketaki flower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (Purva-bhaga))
- **Lotus cosmogony (padma-srishti)** — From Vishnu's navel on the cosmic ocean rises a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates the worlds — the myth giving the Padma Purana its name _(actors: Vishnu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Srishti Khanda))
- **Nasadiya Sukta — Hymn of Creation** — Before existence/non-existence, 'That One' (Tad Ekam) breathes windless and arises through tapas, with kama as the first seed of mind — the agnostic origin hymn _(actors: Tad Ekam (That One))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.129)
- **Nasadiya Sukta — the first impulse from That One** — Before existence or non-existence, 'That One' breathes windless by its own impulse; through tapas it arises and kama (desire) becomes the first seed of mind, the agnostic Vedic origin account _(actors: Tad Ekam (That One))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.129)
- **Parvati's Penance and the Sand-Linga at Kanchipuram** — Parvati, having covered Shiva's eyes and plunged the cosmos into darkness, does penance at Kanchi and moulds a sand-linga under a mango tree to worship as Ekambareswarar _(actors: Parvati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Ekambareswarar mahatmya)
- **Pitṛs Beget the Devas, Asuras and Humans** — As primordial demiurges the sevenfold Pitṛ orders precede and beget the three great classes — devas via Agniṣvātta, asuras via Barhiṣad, and humankind/varṇas via the four corporeal orders _(actors: Pitṛs, Devas, Asuras, Humans)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/pitrs-and-ancestors.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Priyavrata Furrows the Earth-Disc into Oceans** — Priyavrata, grandson of Manu Svayambhuva, furrows the lotus-disc Bhu-mandala with his chariot-wheels to make the seven ring-oceans, his seven sons ruling the seven dvipas _(actors: Priyavrata, sons of Priyavrata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.1; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Puruṣa Sacrifice (Puruṣa Sūkta)** — The cosmic person (Puruṣa) is sacrificed, and from his dismembered body the worlds and the four varṇas originate _(actors: Puruṣa, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.90 (Puruṣa Sūkta))
- **Saptarishi emitted as mind-born sons of Brahma** — The original Saptarishi are emitted as manasaputras (mind-born sons) from Brahma to begin procreation, simultaneously titled Prajapatis and seeders of all beings _(actors: Brahma, the Saptarishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Manu Smriti 1.34-35; Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Sarasvati as Vac utters creation** — Sarasvati, who is Vac, the primordial sound/speech, is the means through which Brahma utters creation; she is co-emergent with the spoken cosmos _(actors: Brahma, Sarasvati (Vac))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Vedic/Puranic theology; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Sati's birth as Daksha's daughter** — The Great Goddess incarnates as Sati, daughter of the Prajāpati Daksha, specifically to win Shiva as her husband _(actors: Sati (Adi Shakti), Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda, Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII)
- **Sri emerges from Prajapati** — In an early distribution-of-fortune myth, Sri emerges radiant from Prajapati and the gods seize her many powers (food, sovereignty, beauty) _(actors: Sri, Prajapati, the gods)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **The contest of the faculties (prana-vidya)** — In the recurring Upanishadic parable the senses each leave the body to prove their primacy and the body survives, but it collapses when Prana prepares to depart, proving breath the chief and support of all faculties _(actors: Prana, the senses)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/prana-and-the-vital-airs.md) — (Chandogya Upanishad 5.1; Brihadaranyaka 6.1; Prashna Upanishad 2)
- **The heavens figured as the Śiśumāra (cosmic dolphin)** — The Bhāgavata directs contemplation of the entire stellar sphere (jyotiś-cakra) as the coiled body of a porpoise/dolphin, head bent down, identified as the body of Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva-Kāla _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Kāla/Vāsudeva), Śuka narrating to Parīkṣit)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.4-9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **Ātman creates the worlds (Aitareya cosmogony)** — In the Aitareya Upaniṣad's opening, Ātman alone exists and brings forth the worlds, the cosmic guardians, and the human person _(actors: Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad 1)
- **Varaha lifts the Earth and instructs Bhu-devi** — The Boar avatara Vishnu raises the submerged Earth-goddess Bhu-devi from the cosmic ocean and instructs her, the kalpa-opening frame of the whole Varaha Purana _(actors: Varaha/Vishnu, Bhu-devi/Prithivi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/varaha-purana.md) — (Varaha Purana; cf. Vishnu P., Bhagavata 3, Linga P.)
- **Varaha lifts the submerged Earth** — At the dawn of the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa the Varaha (boar) avatara lifts the submerged Earth, opening the Svayambhuva manvantara and naming the whole Kalpa _(actors: Varaha (Vishnu), Earth)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vishnu Reclines on the Ocean of Milk (Tiruparkadal)** — In the celestial Vyuha state, Vishnu reclines as Kshirabdhinatha on Adishesha upon the Ocean of Milk attended by Lakshmi, the cosmic source from which the Dashavatara descents issue _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi, Adishesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Ardhanārīśvara manifestation** — Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into a single half-male, half-female body, expressing the inseparability of consciousness and energy and enabling sexual generation _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Brahmā, Bhṛṅgi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Ardhanārīśvara — the half-male/half-female form** — Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into one body split down the centre, expressing the inseparability of Śiva (consciousness) and Śakti (energy); in one variant it enables sexual generation when Brahmā's mind-born creation cannot multiply _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Garuḍa** — After five hundred years the second egg bursts and Garuḍa emerges fully formed and blazing like cosmic fire, mistaken for Agni until he diminishes his heat _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Brahman knows itself as 'I am Brahman'** — In the beginning Brahman knows only itself, declaring 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi,' and thereby becomes the All _(actors: Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.10)
- **Brahma's lie and curse over the lingam** — Brahma falsely claims to have found the pillar's top, producing the ketaki flower as false witness; Shiva curses Brahma to receive no worship and rewards the honest Vishnu _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu, ketaki flower, Kamadhenu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara-samhita))
- **Brahma's mind-born daughter and the growth of his heads** — Brahma brings forth Sarasvati from his own mind as a being of dazzling beauty; captivated, he sprouts a face on each side and one upward to never lose sight of her, the origin of his four or five heads _(actors: Brahma, Sarasvati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Brahmā's Yajña and Marriage to Gāyatrī at Pushkar** — To complete his Pushkar fire-sacrifice on time without the delayed Savitri, Brahma marries the local girl Gayatri to sit beside him as ritual wife _(actors: Brahma, Gayatri, Savitri)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Creation of the Prajāpatis and Manus** — Brahmā emanates his mind-born sons (the Kumāras, Saptarṣi, Marīci, Atri, etc.) and the Manus who govern each Manvantara _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Manusmṛti; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Descent of the Sarayu from Vishnu's Foot** — The Sarayu river issues divinely, created from Vishnu's left foot-thumb as the Ganga issued from his right, making it a pada-tirtha of Vishnu _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Skanda Purana, Ayodhya-mahatmya)
- **Dhruva fixed at the tail-tip as the cosmic pivot** — Dhruva the pole star sits at the tip of the dolphin's upraised tail as the immovable point about which the whole heaven revolves, untouched even by pralaya _(actors: Dhruva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.1-4; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **Gangā's Descent on Brahmapurī** — The celestial Gangā falls onto Brahmā's city atop Meru and divides into four cosmic rivers flowing to the four quarters off Meru's flanks _(actors: Gangā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.17)
- **God Bears and Watches the Seer Kapila at the Beginning** — The Lord brings forth and observes the seer Kapila, born at the beginning, an early scriptural reference tying the founding of Samkhya to the cosmic dawn _(actors: Ishvara, Kapila)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/svetashvatara-upanishad.md) — (Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.2)
- **Hamsa Avatara Instructs the Four Kumaras** — Vishnu's swan-avatara Hamsa reveals the doctrine to the four Kumaras, the origin myth of the Kumara/Sanakadi Sampradaya transmitted through Narada to Nimbarka _(actors: Hamsa Bhagavan, the four Kumaras, Narada, Nimbarka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (vedanta.redzambala; Wikipedia)
- **Heti and Praheti, the first rākṣasas** — The two first-born rākṣasa brothers spring at creation; Praheti turns ascetic while Heti founds the dynasty by marrying _(actors: Heti, Praheti)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Hiranyagarbha arises as sole lord** — A golden germ arises in the beginning as the sole lord of all, floating on the primordial waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.121)
- **Hiranyagarbha — the Golden Womb arises** — A golden germ (Hiranyagarbha) arises in the beginning as sole lord, floating on the primeval waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.121)
- **Śiva Vows Never to Leave Kāśī (Avimukta)** — Śiva installs the liberation-giving liṅga at Kashi and binds himself never to abandon the city, making it Avimukta, the never-forsaken zone outside ordinary time and karma _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Kala draws forth the worlds (Kala-sukta)** — In the oldest hymn personifying Time, Kala as a seven-reined horse draws forth the worlds, the waters and even Prajapati, creating heaven and the earths _(actors: Kala (Time))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Atharvaveda 19.53-54)
- **Madhu and Kaiṭabha slain through the Goddess** — At the dawn of creation the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha menace Brahmā on the lotus; Brahmā hymns the Goddess as Yoganidrā, who withdraws from Viṣṇu and wakes him, enabling the demons' slaying _(actors: Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Goddess)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha I)
- **Madhu and Kaitabha arise from Vishnu's ear** — While Vishnu lies in Yoganidra on Shesha at the end of a cosmic cycle, the asuras Madhu and Kaitabha arise from his ears and move to kill Brahma on the navel-lotus _(actors: Madhu, Kaitabha, Vishnu, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Mind-Born Daughters of the Pitṛs** — Each Pitṛ-class generates a mind-born daughter — Menā (mother of Pārvatī and Gaṅgā), Acchodā, Narmadā — seeding the river- and mountain-genealogies of the cosmos _(actors: Vairājas, Menā, Acchodā, Narmadā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/pitrs-and-ancestors.md) — (Vāyu, Brahmāṇḍa, Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Nāsadīya creation-mystery hymn** — The Ṛgvedic creation hymn contemplates the primordial state before being and non-being, framing the cosmos's emergence from neither existence nor non-existence → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.129 (Nāsadīya Sūkta))
- **Parvati's Flood-Embrace of the Earth-Linga** — Shiva looses a flood to wash away Parvati's sand-linga; she embraces it with her whole body to shield it, leaving the imprint of her bangles, and a pleased Shiva marries her at Kanchi _(actors: Parvati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Ekambareswarar mahatmya)
- **Per-Varsha Avatara Worship Established in Jambudvipa** — Each of the nine varshas of Jambudvipa becomes the eternal heaven where a specific avatara (Hayagriva, Matsya, Kurma, Nrsimha, Varaha, Rama, Nara-Narayana) is worshipped by a chief devotee _(actors: avatara forms, Prahlada, Hanuman, Narada)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Bhagavata Purana canto 5.16-19)
- **Prakriti unfolds the 23 evolutes (Samkhya emanation)** — Disturbed from equilibrium by Purusha's mere proximity, Prakriti evolves in fixed sequence into Mahat, ahamkara, manas, the eleven indriyas, the five tanmatras and the five gross elements — the cosmogonic emanation of the manifest world _(actors: Prakriti, Purusha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Samkhya-Karika 3, 22-25, 38)
- **Samjna Flees the Sun and Leaves Chhaya** — Samjna/Saranyu, unable to bear the Sun's heat, flees and leaves her shadow-double Chhaya in her place; Chhaya becomes mother of the future 8th Manu Savarni by Surya _(actors: Samjna/Saranyu; Chhaya; Surya/Vivasvan)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.1)
- **Sati weds Shiva against Daksha's will** — Sati performs tapas to win the ascetic Shiva and marries him, deepening Daksha's resentment of the cremation-ground bridegroom _(actors: Sati, Shiva, Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana, Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4)
- **Surabhi Born from Dakṣa's Belch** — After Dakṣa drinks the churned amṛta, Surabhi is born from his belch, and from her spring the golden Kapilā cows, mothers of the world _(actors: Dakṣa, Surabhi)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Anuśāsana Parva)
- **Surabhi emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka** — The wish-cow Surabhi/Kāmadhenu emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka, grounding cow-worship and the cowherd cosmology _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Surabhi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Brahma-khaṇḍa))
- **The Atharvaveda deifies Prana** — Atharvaveda 11.4 glorifies Prana as a cosmic deity, lord of all that breathes, present in wind, rain, trees and foetus — the earliest extended deification of breath as cosmic power _(actors: Prana)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/prana-and-the-vital-airs.md) — (Atharvaveda 11.4)
- **The failed first creation: the four Kumaras refuse to procreate** — Brahma's first mind-sons, the four Kumaras, choose eternal childhood and celibacy, forcing Brahma to emit the procreating Prajapatis _(actors: Brahma, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12.4-7; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
- **Varaha and Hamsa Seek the Pillar's Ends** — Vishnu descends as the boar Varaha to find the pillar's base and Brahma ascends on his swan to find its top, but neither reaches an end of the infinite linga _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha), Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Vishnu Stations the Dvādaśa Mādhava to Guard the Sangam** — At Brahma's yajna, Vishnu stations himself in twelve Madhava forms around the Prayaga kshetra to perpetually guard the confluence _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Matsya Purana; Padma Purana; Agni Purana)
- **Vāyu Hides Maināka in the Ocean** — Vāyu spirits away his friend Maināka and hides him in the ocean, so Maināka alone among mountains keeps his wings _(actors: Vayu, Mainaka)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Brahmanda Purana; Kathasaritsagara)
- **Yama, the First Mortal to Die** — Yama becomes the first human to die, treading the path to the afterlife and so becoming lord and guide of the dead, welcoming souls to a sunlit Svarga _(actors: Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.14; Atharva Veda 18)
- **Bhairava severs Brahma's fifth head** — Shiva as Mahakala emanates Bhairava, who severs Brahma's arrogant fifth head with a thumbnail and is condemned to wander as Kapalika bearing the skull until released at Kashi _(actors: Bhairava (Shiva), Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Skanda Purana Kashi Khanda)
- **Brahma hymns Yoganidra to wake Vishnu** — Unable to wake Vishnu, Brahma praises the goddess Yoganidra/Mahamaya (the Brahma-stuti), begging her to withdraw so Vishnu can rouse _(actors: Brahma, Yoganidra, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1.73-87)
- **Brahmā and the Śatarūpā incest, cursed by Śiva** — Smitten by the goddess Śatarūpā he created, Brahmā grows extra heads to keep gazing at her, for which Śiva curses him to lack worship, explaining his absence of temples _(actors: Brahmā, Śatarūpā, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Brahmā Purāṇa)
- **Brahma's Lie and Shiva's Curse on Brahma and the Ketaki** — Brahma falsely claims to have reached the summit using a ketaki flower as witness, and an enraged Shiva curses Brahma to have no worship and bars the ketaki flower from his worship while blessing the honest Vishnu _(actors: Brahma, Shiva, Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches the Kumāras in silence** — Śiva as the south-facing supreme guru expounds jñāna, yoga, and śāstra wordlessly through the cinmudrā to the four aged Kumāras, teaching ultimate truth through silence _(actors: Śiva, the four Kumāras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Śaṅkara's Dakṣiṇāmūrti Stotra)
- **Hiranyagarbha golden egg splits into heaven and earth** — The golden womb-egg floats on the primordial waters for a cosmic year before splitting into heaven and earth, the Vedic antecedent of the Puranic Brahmanda _(actors: Hiranyagarbha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahmanda-and-bhuvana-kosha.md) — (Rigveda 10.121; Manusmriti 1.5-13)
- **Lakṣmī Becomes the Badrī Tree to Shelter Vishnu** — While Vishnu does austere tapas exposed to Himalayan cold, Lakshmi transforms into a badri (jujube) tree to shade him, giving Badrinath its name Badri-ka-ashrama _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Badari-mahatmya))
- **Marriage of Heti and Bhayā** — Heti weds Bhayā, sister of Kāla (Time/Death), begetting Vidyutkeśa and continuing the rākṣasa line _(actors: Heti, Bhayā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu** — At the start of the kalpa the fish-avatāra Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu, making the deluge a frame for revelation itself _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa)
- **Prakṛti divides into the five primary goddesses** — On Kṛṣṇa's will Prakṛti divides into Rādhā, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Sāvitrī, each assigned a cosmic office, with all other goddesses their portions _(actors: Prakṛti, Rādhā, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Sāvitrī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Prakṛti-khaṇḍa))
- **Purusha Sukta — creation by cosmic sacrifice** — The gods dismember the cosmic Man Purusha in a primal yajna, and from his parts arise the moon, sun, Indra, Agni, Vayu, the worlds, and the four varnas _(actors: Purusha, the gods)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.90)
- **Sati's self-immolation at the Daksha-yajna** — Publicly humiliated by Daksha, who reviles Shiva at his great sacrifice, Sati renounces her body in yogic fire _(actors: Sati, Daksha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.4, Shiva Purana)
- **Shiva descends into matter (36-tattva emanation)** — In Kashmir Shaiva cosmogony a single divine consciousness Shiva, through Shakti, Sadashiva, Ishvara, Shuddhavidya, then Maya and the five kanchukas, contracts and descends into the individuated soul and the 24 tattvas of matter — the self-display of one consciousness as the universe _(actors: Shiva, Shakti)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Tantraloka; Malinivijaya; Svacchanda Tantra)
- **Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head** — Condemning Brahma's pursuit of his own daughter, Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head _(actors: Shiva, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Soma's abduction of Tara and the Tarakamaya war** — Soma, swollen with pride after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara wife of Brihaspati, sparking the Tarakamaya war until Brahma forces her return; Tara then bears Budha, founder of the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Soma (Candra), Tara, Brihaspati, Shukra, Brahma, Budha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana (adhyaya 24))
- **Surabhi Granted Goloka by Brahmā** — After ten thousand years of austerities to Brahmā at Kailāsa, Surabhi is made a goddess, decreed worthy of universal worship, and granted the cow-heaven Goloka _(actors: Surabhi, Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Anuśāsana Parva)
- **Sāvitrī's Curse on Brahmā** — Finding another woman in her ritual seat, the enraged Savitri curses Brahma to be worshipped nowhere in the universe (and curses the attendant gods), explaining Brahma's near-total absence from temples _(actors: Savitri, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **The anatomy of the figure — planets and asterisms as limbs** — Sun, Moon, the five planets, Rāhu, the Aśvins, the nakṣatras and Nārāyaṇa (as the heart) are mapped onto specific limbs of the dolphin, with variant assignments in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa _(actors: the Navagraha, nakṣatra-deities, Nārāyaṇa, Yama/Mṛtyu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.5-8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **The Kumaras' curse on Jaya and Vijaya** — Barred from Vaikuntha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the Kumaras curse them to three demonic births, engine of three Vishnu avatars _(actors: the four Kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.15-16, 7.1)
- **Viṣṇu speaks the Catuh-sloki to Brahma** — Viṣṇu speaks the four-verse seed of the Bhagavata to Brahma, the cosmogonic teaching treated as the text in miniature _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.9.33-36)
- **Wager of Kadrū and Vinatā; Vinatā Enslaved** — The sisters bet on the color of Uccaiḥśravas's tail; Kadrū's nāga sons blacken it by deceit, Vinatā loses the wager and becomes Kadrū's slave, rooting Garuḍa's hatred of serpents _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, nāgas, Uccaiḥśravas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Yama-Yami Dialogue and Rejected Union** — Yami proposes incestuous union with her twin Yama to propagate humankind, but Yama refuses on grounds of dharma, staging moral restraint winning over desire at humanity's origin _(actors: Yama, Yami)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.10)
- **Atharvan and Angiras Hear the Atharvaveda at the Cosmic Dawn** — By the scripture clock, the rishis Atharvan, Angiras (and Bhrigu) 'hear' the eternal Atharvaveda — the twin streams of healing and aggressive magic — at the dawn of the cosmic order _(actors: Atharvan, Angiras, Bhrigu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/atharvaveda.md) — (Atharvaveda Samhita)
- **Brahma's creation from Garbhodakasayi Viṣṇu** — Brahma emerges and undertakes secondary creation as the tattvas unfold from prakṛti, the cosmogonic core of skandha 3 _(actors: Brahma, Garbhodakasayi Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3)
- **Brahmā's Creative Sacrifice at Brahma Sarovar** — Tradition holds Brahmā performed the cosmic sṛṣṭi-yajña at Brahma Sarovar in Kurukṣetra, the universe created from this very ground _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Kurukshetra-mahatmya tradition)
- **Creation from Vishnu and Lakshmi** — The Garuda Purana's cosmogony makes the manifest world the fruit of the union of Lakshmi-Narayana, anchoring the cosmic time-spine _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/garuda-purana.md) — (Garuda Purana (Purva-khanda))
- **Creation of Night to Heal Yami's Grief** — After Yama's death, the perpetually grieving Yami cannot feel time pass, so the gods create Night to separate the days, healing her sorrow with the coming of tomorrow _(actors: Yami, the gods)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Maitrayani Samhita)
- **Daksha's daughters wed to Kashyapa breed all classes of beings** — Daksha gives 13+ daughters (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Vinata, etc.) to Kashyapa, who become the mothers of devas, asuras, nagas, birds and beasts _(actors: Daksha, Kashyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Vinata)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.21; Bhagavata Purana 6.6; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Eggs emanate from Maha-Vishnu's pores (Causal Ocean)** — On the exhalation of Maha-Vishnu reclining on the Causal Ocean, millions of brahmandas issue from his pores as bubbles, withdrawn again on his inhalation _(actors: Maha-Vishnu (Karanodaka-shayi))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahmanda-and-bhuvana-kosha.md) — (Brahma-samhita 5.47-48)
- **Existence born from non-existence (Brahmanaspati)** — The gods are born, existence arises from non-existence, and Brahmanaspati forges the worlds like a smith, with Daksha and Aditi mutually generated _(actors: Brahmanaspati, the devas, Daksha, Aditi)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.72)
- **Garuḍa's Amṛta-Quest and Battle with the Devas** — To ransom his mother, Garuḍa fights through the devas, a fire-ring, a razor-wheel and serpent-guardians to seize the amṛta from the gods _(actors: Garuḍa, Indra, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Āstīka section)
- **Gāyatrī's Boon and Sāvitrī's Mitigation at Pushkar** — Placated, Savitri softens her curse so Brahma may be worshipped only at Pushkar, and Gayatri blesses the spot to be the king of pilgrimages granting liberation _(actors: Savitri, Gayatri, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Kushmanda creates the cosmos with a smile** — The Navadurga form Kushmanda is said to have created the cosmic egg (Anda) with a smile and to dwell in the sun's core _(actors: Kushmanda)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Kavaca)
- **Nara–Nārāyaṇa Penance at Badarikāśrama** — Vishnu incarnate as the twin sages Nara and Narayana performs eternal penance in the open at Badarikashrama, the eponymous ascetics of the peaks flanking the shrine _(actors: Nara, Narayana (Vishnu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana; Mahabharata tradition)
- **Sacrifice of the Cosmic Purusha** — The thousand-headed Purusha is dismembered by the gods in a primal yajna; from his body arise the cosmos and the four varnas (Brahmana from mouth, Kshatriya from arms, Vaishya from thighs, Shudra from feet), plus moon, sun, Indra, Agni, and Vayu _(actors: the gods, Purusha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.90 (Purusha Sukta))
- **Samkhya-Shaiva creation from the unmanifest linga** — Creation proceeds from the unmanifest linga (avyakta/pradhana) through mahat and the tattvas to the manifest world, with Shiva-Shakti as the ultimate ground _(actors: Shiva, Shakti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (Purva-bhaga))
- **Sat born from Asat (Brahmanaspati account)** — The devas are born and existence arises from non-existence; Brahmanaspati forges the worlds, with Daksha and Aditi mutually generating each other _(actors: Brahmanaspati, Daksha, Aditi)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.72)
- **Shuka's Dharana and the Avatara Catalogue** — Shuka teaches the cosmic-body (Virat-purusha) meditation and recites the locus-classicus list of Vishnu's twenty-two avataras _(actors: Shuka, Parikshit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.1, 2.6, 2.7)
- **Sun, Moon, planets and Saptarṣi tethered to Dhruva by wind-cords** — All celestial bodies are bound to Dhruva by cords of wind (pravaha) and wheel about him like oxen at a central post; the Saptarṣi circumambulate him, generating the kāla-cakra (wheel of time) _(actors: Dhruva, the Saptarṣi, Sun, Moon, the planets)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.1-3; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **Tvaṣṭṛ forges Indra's vajra** — Tvaṣṭṛ, the first smith of the gods, forges Indra's thunderbolt vajra, his signature creation and the weapon that slays Vṛtra _(actors: Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishvakarma-and-tvashtar.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32, 1.61)
- **Vidyutkeśa weds Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā; abandonment of Sukeśa** — Vidyutkeśa marries Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā, daughter of Twilight, who bears a son and abandons the infant on a mountain _(actors: Vidyutkeśa, Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Vishnu beheads Madhu and Kaitabha** — Mahamaya withdraws and Vishnu wakes, battles the demons for 5000 years, tricks them via their own boon, and beheads them on his thighs with his discus _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Mahamaya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Birth of the primordial Pitrs from Brahma** — The classical classes of divine ancestors (Agnishvattas, Barhishads, Somapas, Ajyapas, Sukalins) arise as mind-born sons of Brahma, becoming the primal ancestor-races worshipped above ordinary dead _(actors: Brahma, the divine Pitrs)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/shraddha-and-pitr-rites.md) — (Manusmriti 3.194-201; Vishnu, Vayu, Brahmanda Puranas)
- **Daksha's 27 daughters wed to Candra become the nakshatras** — Daksha gives 27 daughters to the Moon as the lunar mansions; the Moon's neglect of all but Rohini brings Daksha's curse causing the lunar phases _(actors: Daksha, Candra (Soma), Rohini, the 27 nakshatras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana 6.6, 9.14)
- **Emanation of innumerable universes from Maha-Vishnu's breath** — Universes (brahmandas) issue like bubbles from the pores of Maha-Vishnu with each exhalation, each sealed in seven concentric layers and birthing its own Brahma _(actors: Maha-Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.5, 3.11; Brahma Samhita 5.11-13)
- **Śiva and Pārvatī bless Sukeśa** — The abandoned infant Sukeśa is found and blessed by Śiva and Pārvatī, granted immortality, eternal youth and a flying city, becoming the patriarch of the Laṅkā kings _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Sukeśa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Liṅgodbhava — the Infinite Pillar of Fire** — When Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy, Shiva appears as an infinite column of fire whose ends neither god can find; Vishnu as Varaha digs down and Brahma as a swan flies up, and the column cools into the Arunachala hill _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu (Varaha))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Arunachaleswarar / Skanda Purana mahatmya)
- **Prajapati creates by tapas and self-multiplication** — Prajapati, alone and desiring to be many, performs tapas and emits the worlds, creatures and Vedas, becoming exhausted and reconstituted by sacrifice _(actors: Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana; Taittiriya Brahmana)
- **Prajapati creates by tapas / self-multiplication** — Prajapati, alone and afraid, desires to be many, performs tapas and emits the worlds, creatures, and Vedas, becoming exhausted and reconstituted by sacrifice _(actors: Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana, Taittiriya Brahmana)
- **That One Arises Through Tapas and Kama (Nasadiya creation)** — Before being and non-being, 'That One' breathes windless by its own impulse; through tapas it arises and kama (desire) becomes the first seed of mind — the agnostic Vedic cosmogony _(actors: Tad Ekam (That One))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.129 (Nasadiya Sukta))
- **The Ṛbhus split Tvaṣṭṛ's cup into four** — The artisan-elf Ṛbhus split Tvaṣṭṛ's single soma-cup (camasa) into four, a feat earning them divine status and provoking Tvaṣṭṛ's jealousy _(actors: the Ṛbhus, Tvaṣṭṛ)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishvakarma-and-tvashtar.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.20, 4.33)
- **The Hamsa-avatara teaches the Four Kumaras** — In the namesake passage, Vishnu as a swan instructs the Four Kumaras on the three gunas and the discrimination of Self from matter, wisdom Krishna re-transmits _(actors: Vishnu (Hamsa), Sanaka, Sananda, Sanatana, Sanat-kumara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.13)
- **The Śiśumāra-dhāraṇā and closing mantra** — Bhāgavata 5.23 prescribes a daily meditation visualising the dolphin-form as Vāsudeva-Kāla, with a thrice-daily namaskāra mantra said to dissolve the day's sins _(actors: the meditator/devotee, Vāsudeva-Kāla)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.8-9)
- **Viṣṇu Digs the Cakra-Puṣkariṇī; Śiva Drops His Earring** — Viṣṇu digs the Maṇikarṇikā kuṇḍa with his discus in primal devotion and Śiva, trembling with delight, drops his jewelled earring (maṇi-karṇikā) into it, naming the great cremation-ground _(actors: Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda; varanasiguru.com)
- **Viṣṇu's Boon and Garuḍa Becomes His Mount** — Impressed in the amṛta-flight, Viṣṇu grants Garuḍa immortality without drinking the nectar and a perch above him, setting him on his banner and making him his vāhana _(actors: Garuḍa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Yami Becomes the River Yamuna** — In Puranic tradition Yami's grief at Yama's death transforms her into the sacred river Yamuna _(actors: Yami/Yamuna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Puranas)
- **Alignment of Dhruva, Meru and the lokas** — The Śiśumāra-cakra occupies the starry region above the planetary spheres and Mount Meru, with Dhruva as the celestial pole directly above the Meru world-axis, all contained within the one Brahmāṇḍa _(actors: Dhruva, Mount Meru, the lokas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.20-23; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.8-9)
- **Atman splits into male and female** — In the beginning the Self alone, lonely, desires a second and splits into husband and wife, from whose union all beings arise through name and form _(actors: Atman/Self)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4)
- **Atman splits into male and female (Upanishadic monism)** — The lonely Self (Atman) desires a second, splits into husband and wife, and from their union all beings arise through name and form _(actors: Atman/Brahman)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4)
- **Birth of the eight diggajas from Brahmā's chanting** — Per the Mātaṅgalīlā, Airāvata and the seven other world-elephants spring from Brahmā chanting hymns over Garuḍa's eggshell, forming the aṣṭa-diggaja that uphold the quarters of space _(actors: Brahmā, Airāvata)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mātaṅgalīlā; Amarakośa)
- **Daksha's sons renounce; Narada is cursed** — Narada dissuades Daksha's Haryashva and Shabalashva sons from procreating; the enraged Daksha curses Narada to wander eternally _(actors: Daksha, Narada, the Haryashvas, the Shabalashvas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.5; Vishnu Purana)
- **Genesis of the Shakti Pithas** — Vishnu's Sudarshana Chakra dismembers Sati's corpse as the grief-stricken Shiva dances; each landing-spot of a body-part becomes a Shakti Pitha _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu, Sati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Devi-Bhagavata VII, Kalika Purana, Mahabhagavata Purana, Pithanirnaya)
- **Kardama Weds Devahuti** — The prajapati Kardama performs tapas, marries Svayambhuva Manu's daughter Devahuti, builds an aerial palace, and fathers nine daughters and a son who is Vishnu _(actors: Kardama, Devahuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.21-24)
- **Origin of Chitragupta from Brahma's Body** — Chitragupta springs from the body (kaya) of Brahma to keep the master-ledger of every being's deeds when Yama could not track them all _(actors: Chitragupta, Brahma, Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Garuda Purana; Padma Purana; Kayastha tradition)
- **Sukeśa weds Devavatī; birth of Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī** — Sukeśa marries Devavatī and fathers the celebrated triad Mālyavān, Sumālī and Mālī, the great rākṣasa kings _(actors: Sukeśa, Devavatī, Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **The Golden Womb (Hiranyagarbha) Arises** — A golden germ/egg arises as the sole lord of creation, sustaining heaven and earth, named in the final verse as Prajapati — the seed of the later cosmic egg and Brahma _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.121 (Hiranyagarbha Sukta))
- **The Kuśa-Grass Trick and the Serpents' Forked Tongues** — Garuḍa delivers the amṛta to the nāgas to free Vinatā but sets it on kuśa grass; while they bathe Indra snatches it back, and the nāgas licking the grass split their tongues — the aetiology of the forked tongue _(actors: Garuḍa, Indra, nāgas, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Unfolding of the cosmic egg (Adi-Sāṅkhya cosmogony)** — From the unmanifest Pradhāna arise mahat, ahaṃkāra, the tanmātras and gross elements, condensing into the golden cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) within which Brahmā fashions the worlds _(actors: Brahmā, Pradhāna)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmanda-purana.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Prakriyā/Anuṣaṅga pādas))
- **Vishnu Appears as an Old Man to Sage Nārada at Vridha Badri** — Vishnu appears in the form of an old man to sage Narada during his penance at Animath, where the current Badrinath idol carved by Vishvakarma was first worshipped _(actors: Vishnu, Narada, Vishvakarma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Badari-mahatmya))
- **Vāyu breaks the peak of Meru to form Laṅkā** — Incited by Nārada and after Garuḍa abandons his shielding post, Vāyu shears off the summit of Mount Meru and hurls it into the southern ocean, where it becomes the three-peaked Trikūṭa island of Laṅkā _(actors: Vāyu, Nārada, Garuḍa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Purāṇic tradition)
- **Brahmā composes the Daṇḍanīti and the first king is instituted** — In primeval anarchy men appeal to Brahmā, who composes a vast treatise on polity; Śiva abridges it and the first king is installed to wield the rod of punishment _(actors: Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.59)
- **Kapila's Teaching to Devahuti** — Vishnu incarnate as the sage Kapila instructs his mother Devahuti in Sankhya, bhakti-yoga, and liberation, and she attains moksha _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **Lotus-born Brahma from Vishnu's navel** — During pralaya Vishnu reclines on Shesha on the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma, the delegated creator _(actors: Vishnu (Narayana), Brahma, Shesha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8, Vishnu Purana)
- **Parvati's rebirth and tapas to win Shiva** — Sati reincarnates as Parvati, daughter of Himavan, and undertakes ferocious austerities (Aparna) to win the meditating Shiva, passing his Brahmin-disguise test _(actors: Parvati, Himavan, Shiva, Narada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Parvati Khanda, Kumarasambhava 1-5, Devi-Bhagavata)
- **Vishnu reclines on Shesha and projects Brahma** — During the cosmic night Vishnu reclines on the serpent Shesha upon the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma the delegated creator _(actors: Vishnu (Narayana), Shesha, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8; Vishnu Purana; Matsya Purana)
- **Viśvakarmā builds Laṅkā** — At the brothers' request the divine architect Viśvakarmā raises the golden city of Laṅkā on Mount Trikūṭa for the first rākṣasa masters _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Brahma born from the navel-lotus of Vishnu** — Within each cosmic egg, Vishnu reclines on the Garbhodaka womb-ocean and from his navel-lotus is born Brahma, who then builds the dvipas and lokas _(actors: Vishnu (Garbhodaka-shayi), Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahmanda-and-bhuvana-kosha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8; Brahma-samhita 5.51)
- **Devi slays Madhu and Kaitabha (Prathama-carita)** — The Goddess as Yoganidra/Mahamaya rouses Vishnu from cosmic sleep to slay the demons Madhu and Kaitabha who threatened Brahma _(actors: Mahakali (Devi), Vishnu, Brahma, Madhu, Kaitabha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana (Devi Mahatmya ch. 1))
- **Garuḍa wins the amṛta to free his mother Vinatā** — Garuḍa, son of Kaśyapa and Vinatā, wins the amṛta from Indra to ransom his enslaved mother, whereupon Viṣṇu grants him immortality and makes him his mount and banner _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Kaśyapa, Indra, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (World History Encyclopedia, Garuda; Wikipedia)
- **Lingodbhava — the pillar of fire** — Shiva manifests as the infinite pillar of fire between Brahma and Vishnu, establishing the linga as supreme; carried by the Kurma Purana _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha** — Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, ordering creation against primordial chaos _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Brahma, Yoganidra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Mahabharata, Devi Mahatmya 1, Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vac Ambhrini Proclaims Herself the Supreme Power** — The seeress Vac Ambhrini, daughter of Ambhrina, speaks in the first person proclaiming the goddess Speech as the supreme power pervading all gods — the Vedic seed of Shakta theology _(actors: Vac Ambhrini)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.125 (Devi Sukta))
- **Wedding of Shiva and Parvati** — After Parvati's penance, the Saptarishi arrange the divine wedding of Shiva and Parvati, drawing all the gods to Himavan's city _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Himavan, Saptarishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Kumarasambhava 6-7, Shiva Purana)
- **Kadrū–Vinatā wager over Uccaiḥśravas' tail** — The wager between Kadrū and Vinatā over the colour of the churning-born horse Uccaiḥśravas' tail triggers Vinatā's enslavement, the origin of Garuḍa's nectar-quest and the Nāga–bird enmity _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, Uccaiḥśravas, Garuḍa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Uchchaihshravas (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Madhu-Kaitabha slain by Vishnu** — Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, asserting order against primordial chaos _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Mahabharata; Devi Mahatmya 1; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Parvati becomes Gauri and Annapurna** — Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion as Gauri (the cast sheath becoming Kali), and manifests as Annapurna at Kashi to feed even Shiva _(actors: Parvati (Gauri, Annapurna), Shiva, Kali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana, Annapurna Upanishad / Sthala-purana)
- **The Cosmic Egg (Brahmanda) splits open** — The creator's golden seed becomes an egg incubating on the waters; it splits — upper shell to heaven, lower to earth, the space between to sky _(actors: Brahma (Svayambhu))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Manusmriti 1.5-13, Vishnu Purana 1.2)
- **Forging of Sudarśana, Triśūla, and Puṣpaka from Sūrya's radiance** — When Saṃjñā could not bear Sūrya's heat, Viśvakarmā grinds the sun on his lathe and forges Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra, Śiva's Triśūla, and the Puṣpaka Vimāna from the shavings of solar radiance _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Sūrya, Saṃjñā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Ayudhapurusha)
- **Varaha lifts the Earth at the Kalpa's dawn** — At the dawn of the current Shveta-Varaha Kalpa, Vishnu as the boar Varaha lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters, the act that names this Day of Brahma _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha avatara))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.4; Bhagavata Purana 3.13)
- **Varaha lifts the earth at the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa's dawn** — The current kalpa is named Shveta-Varaha for Vishnu's boar avatara who lifted the earth at its dawn on the first day of Brahma's 51st year _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalpa-and-pralaya.md) — (Vishnu Purana I.4)
- **Brahma seeks the root of the lotus-stalk** — Brahma, born on the lotus and ignorant of his origin, descends the stalk seeking its root, fails, performs tapas, and is granted vision of Vishnu, establishing Vishnu's supremacy _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8-9)
- **Devi creates the Trimurti (Shakta account)** — The Supreme Goddess (Adi Parashakti) brings forth Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti from her own portions _(actors: Mahadevi (Adi Parashakti), Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana 3, Devi Mahatmya)
- **Martanda cast away and reclaimed as Surya** — In the Rigvedic account Aditi casts away her eighth son Martanda, who is reclaimed as Surya the Sun _(actors: Aditi, Martanda/Surya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Rigveda)
- **Agastya Mediates Indra and the Maruts** — As Rigvedic seer Agastya composes hymns mediating a quarrel between Indra and the storm-gods, reconciling the Indra-Maruts dispute _(actors: Agastya, Indra, the Maruts)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Rigveda 1.165, 1.170-1.171)
- **Brahma forms within the cosmic egg and splits it** — The creator's seed becomes a golden egg incubating a divine year; Brahma develops within and splits it into heavens, earth, and the sky between, with fluids becoming mountains and oceans _(actors: Brahma / Svayambhu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Manusmriti 1.5-13; Vishnu Purana 1.2)
- **Primary unfolding of prakriti (Prakrita sarga)** — From Vishnu's will, unmanifest prakriti is disturbed and the gunas lose equilibrium, emitting mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses, and gross elements into the cosmic egg _(actors: Vishnu, Brahma, Prakriti)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.2, Bhagavata Purana 3.5)
- **Viśvakarmā forges the twin bows Pināka and Śārṅga** — To settle the Śiva–Viṣṇu superiority contest, Viśvakarmā crafts the twin bows Pināka (Śiva) and Śārṅga (Viṣṇu); Viṣṇu 'wins' and Śiva's bow passes to the kings of Mithilā _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Śiva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa; divine-bows tradition)
- **Bhairava severs Brahmā's fifth head** — From his fury at the arrogant fifth head of Brahmā, Śiva manifests Kāla Bhairava, who shears off the offending head, incurring brahmahatyā that clings as a skull until expiated at Kāśī _(actors: Kāla Bhairava, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Śatarudra-saṃhitā; Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Brahma creates the universe and begins time (Ugadi charter)** — The Gudi Padwa/Ugadi charter marks the day Brahma created the universe and began kala (time) — Yuga-adi, the 'beginning of the age' _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (traditional)
- **Lingodbhava — the infinite pillar of light** — Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy when an endless fiery jyotirlinga appears; neither finds its end and Shiva emerges from the linga as the true source of both _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **The nine creations (sargas) of Brahma** — Creation proceeds through nine graded sargas — three elemental (Prakrita) and five derived (Vaikrita) plus the Kaumara — from Mahat down to the Kumaras _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.5, Bhagavata Purana 3.10)
- **Birth of the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — Brahma produces from his mind the Brahmarshis/Prajapatis — Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, Vasishtha — progenitors of all beings _(actors: Brahma, the nine Prajapatis)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7, Manusmriti 1.34-35)
- **Yoganidra withdraws so Vishnu slays Madhu-Kaitabha** — At a cycle's start the Goddess as Yoganidra withdraws from the sleeping Vishnu so he can wake and slay Madhu and Kaitabha, showing the Goddess drives even Vishnu's creative role _(actors: Devi (Yoganidra/Mahamaya), Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Devi brings forth the Trimurti** — The Supreme Goddess brings forth Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti who is her own portion _(actors: Mahadevi, Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana 3)
- **The Kumaras refuse to procreate** — Brahma's first sons, the four eternal celibate Sanaka-kumaras, reject creation and remain renunciant, frustrating Brahma's plan to populate the world _(actors: Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12, Vishnu Purana 1.7)
- **Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the sacrificial fire** — Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the cosmic fire of the gods' sacrifice and creates and orders the worlds _(actors: Lalita Tripurasundari)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brahmanda Purana (Lalitopakhyana))
- **Lingodbhava establishes Shiva's supremacy** — Shiva manifests as an infinite column of fire whose top (Brahma as swan) and bottom (Vishnu as boar) neither can find, establishing his supremacy and grounding the 12 Jyotirlingas _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana Vidyeshvara Samhita)
- **Brahma splits into Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his body into male and female halves becoming Svayambhuva Manu (the first Manu) and Shatarupa, whose union begins the human dynastic line _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7, Manusmriti 1.32)
- **Primary unfolding of prakriti into the tattvas** — From Vishnu's will unmanifest prakriti is disturbed, the gunas lose equilibrium, and mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses and gross elements emerge in sequence, forming the cosmic egg _(actors: Vishnu, Prakriti/Pradhana)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.2; Bhagavata Purana 3.5, 3.26)
- **Brahma emanates the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — Brahma produces his Brahmarshi/Prajapati sons from his mind, the progenitors of all beings _(actors: Brahma, Bhrigu, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, Vasishtha and others)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7; Manusmriti 1.34-35)
- **Daksha populates the worlds (maithuni srishti)** — Daksha Prajapati fathers numerous daughters who, married to gods and sages, become mothers of devas, asuras, animals, and all living kinds, beginning sexual generation _(actors: Daksha, Kashyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15, 1.21, Bhagavata Purana 6.6)
- **Birth of Rudra from Brahma's anger** — Enraged at the Kumaras' refusal, Brahma emits Rudra (half male, half female) from his brow; bidden to divide, the male becomes eleven Rudras and the female the shaktis _(actors: Brahma, Rudra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Vishnu's cosmic sleep induced by Mahamaya** — Vishnu's cosmic sleep is induced by Yoganidra/Mahamaya, the deluding power of the Goddess, in the Devi Mahatmya opening _(actors: Vishnu, Mahamaya (Yoganidra))_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/maya-and-avidya.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Innumerable universes from Maha-Vishnu's breath** — Universes (brahmandas) emanate like bubbles with each exhalation of Maha-Vishnu, each sealed in seven concentric layers, a Brahma born in each _(actors: Maha-Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.5, 3.11, Brahma Samhita 5.11-13)
- **Birth of Narmada from Shiva** — The river Narmada is born from a drop of Shiva's sweat during the tandava and granted to be imperishable, alone flowing through pralayas _(actors: Shiva, Narmada, Markandeya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Skanda Purana, Reva-khanda; Narmada Purana)
- **The cosmic lotus and Brahmā spring from reclining Viṣṇu** — From the navel of Viṣṇu reclining on Ananta-Śeṣa springs the cosmic lotus bearing Brahmā, who begins the next creation _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Śeṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Birth of the Maruts from Rudra and Pṛśni** — In the Vedic account the storm-troop Maruts are born together as sons of Rudra and the dappled cow-goddess Pṛśni, self-arising from the storm _(actors: Rudra, Pṛśni, Maruts)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-maruts.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.85; 5.57–60)
- **Brahmā emits the mind-born sons** — At the dawn of the kalpa Brahmā emits his first conscious beings, the mānasaputra Prajāpatis and seers, from his mind/body without sexual union _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Manusmṛti 1.34–35; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **The four Kumāras refuse procreation** — Brahmā's first mind-sons, the four Kumāras, are born fully realized and choose eternal childhood and celibacy, the 'failed first creation' that forces Brahmā to emit the procreating Prajāpatis _(actors: Brahmā, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12.4–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Brahmā emits Manu Svāyambhuva and Śatarūpā** — To get creation moving Brahmā emits from his body the first man Manu Svāyambhuva and the first woman Śatarūpā _(actors: Brahmā, Manu Svāyambhuva, Śatarūpā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **The Kumāras curse Jaya and Vijaya** — Barred from Vaikuṇṭha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the wrathful Kumāras curse the pair to three demonic births, the engine of three of Viṣṇu's avatāra-descents _(actors: Kumāras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.15–16, 7.1)
- **Aditi casts away and recovers Mārtāṇḍa** — In the original Āditya account, the mother Aditi flings away the 'dead egg' eighth son Mārtāṇḍa (Sūrya) and then recovers him _(actors: Aditi, Mārtāṇḍa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Ṛgveda 2.27; 10.72.8–9)
- **Rudras born from Brahmā's weeping brow** — The eleven Rudras are born from Brahmā's brow when he wept, hence their name from rud, 'to cry' _(actors: Brahmā, Rudras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **Birth of the Vālakhilyas to Kratu** — The Saptarṣi-Prajāpati Kratu and his wife Sannati beget sixty-thousand thumb-sized celibate ascetic sons, the Vālakhilyas, who escort the Sun's chariot _(actors: Kratu, Sannati, Vālakhilyas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Mahābhārata)

## The Earlier Manvantaras (1–6) & Primordial Reigns  ·  342 events

*Events of the six manvantaras before ours, and the primordial kings/sages (Dhruva, Pṛthu, Vena, Daksha).*

- **Aṅga Abandons the Throne over Vena** — King Aṅga weds Sunīthā, daughter of Death, whose evil grandson Vena is born; despairing of his wicked son, Aṅga abandons the throne for the forest _(actors: Aṅga, Sunīthā, Vena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.13; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Ajāmila's fall and life of sin** — The virtuous brāhmaṇa Ajāmila is ruined by lust for a dāsī, abandons his wife and dharma, and lives by theft and deceit, naming his youngest son Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Ajāmila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.1)
- **Atri and Anasūyā's austerity for a divine son** — The sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā perform severe tapas seeking a son equal to the Supreme, and the Trimūrti grant that portions of all three will be born to them _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Avatar Satyasena destroys the evil spirits** — Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and Dharma, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas and lying bhutas, fighting beside Indra Satyajit _(actors: Satyasena, Sunrita, Dharma, Indra Satyajit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1.25)
- **Avatar Vaikuntha creates the realm of Vaikuntha** — Vishnu's avatar Vaikuntha, born of his own accord, creates his eternal abode Vaikuntha at the request of his consort Rama (Lakshmi) _(actors: Vaikuntha (Vishnu), Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Birth of Cyavana** — The Rākṣasa Puloman abducts the pregnant Pulomā, and the unborn Bhārgava child slips prematurely from the womb (hence 'Cyavana'), his radiance burning the Rākṣasa to ashes _(actors: Bhṛgu, Pulomā, Puloman, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 5–6)
- **Birth of Rishabhadeva from Merudevi** — King Nabhi and Merudevi perform a sacrifice longing for a son, and Vishnu descends, born as Rishabha (the bull), counted an avatara of Narayana _(actors: Nabhi, Merudevi, Vishnu/Rishabhadeva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.3; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Birth of the avatar Vaikuntha** — In the Raivata Manvantara Vishnu manifests of his own accord as Lord Vaikuntha, born together with the deva-class called Vaikunthas _(actors: Vaikuntha, the Vaikuntha gods, Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Birth of Vaivasvata Manu** — Vaivasvata, the 7th and current Manu, is born of Surya (Vivasvat) and Saranyu/Chhaya, becoming the present progenitor of humankind _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Surya, Saranyu/Chhaya)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13)
- **Birth of Viśravas from Pulastya** — The rākṣasa line descends from Brahmā's mind-born son Pulastya, whose circumstance at Tṛṇabindu's hermitage produces the sage Viśravas _(actors: Pulastya, Viśravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 2–3)
- **Brahma to Vaivasvata Manu Descent** — The cosmological spine runs Brahma to Marichi to Kashyapa to Vivasvan (Surya) to Vaivasvata Manu, whose children fork into the two royal dynasties _(actors: Brahma, Kashyapa, Surya, Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV; Bhagavata Purana IX)
- **Chakshusha Manu's previous-birth as Ananda** — Before becoming the sixth Manu, the future Chakshusha lives as Ananda, switched at birth by a cat into a royal household, and on learning the truth withdraws to the forest for tapas, whereupon Brahma blesses him to be reborn as Manu _(actors: Ananda/Chakshusha, Anamitra, King Vikranta, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **Dadhīci teaches the Madhu-vidyā through a horse's head** — To evade Indra's curse, the Aśvins fit Dadhyañc with a horse's head so he can teach them the honey-doctrine, then restore his own head _(actors: Dadhīci (Dadhyañc), the Aśvins, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.5; Ṛgveda 1.116–117)
- **Daksha's Yajna and Snub of Shiva** — Daksha Prajapati holds a great sacrifice and deliberately omits to invite Shiva and Sati out of contempt for his ascetic son-in-law _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana)
- **Dhruva is slighted by his stepmother and vows penance** — The boy-prince Dhruva, pushed from his father's lap by queen Suruci's scorn, resolves to win the highest station and leaves for the forest _(actors: Dhruva, Suruci, Sunīti, Uttānapāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Founding of Ayodhya by Manu Vaivasvata** — Vaivasvata Manu lays out Ayodhya on the south bank of the Sarayu as the capital of Kosala, founding the Suryavamsha/Ikshvaku city _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Bala-kanda 1.5; Skanda Purana Ayodhya-mahatmya)
- **Founding of Ayodhyā by Manu Vaivasvata** — Ayodhya, the unconquerable city and Suryavamsha capital, is founded by Manu Vaivasvata himself as one of the oldest cities _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Gajendra-moksha** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile and dragged toward death over a thousand celestial years, surrenders to the Supreme and is rescued by Vishnu, who arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his Sudarshana chakra _(actors: Gajendra, Vishnu (avatar Hari), the crocodile (Huhu), Garuda)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Gajendra-moksha (liberation of Gajendra)** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile, surrenders to the Supreme; Vishnu arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his chakra _(actors: Gajendra, the crocodile (Huhu), Vishnu, Indradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Kacha steals the Mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā** — Bṛhaspati's son Kacha serves Śukra to learn the dead-reviving mantra; killed thrice by the asuras and revived from Śukra's own belly, he masters it _(actors: Kacha, Śukrācārya, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 71-72)
- **Kapila descends and teaches Samkhya to Devahuti** — The sage Kapila, an avatara of Vishnu, descends and expounds the Samkhya tattva-system (the Kapila-gita) to his mother Devahuti, the foundational teaching of the school _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **Krishna teaches the imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, Manu, and Ikshvaku** — Krishna recounts that at the dawn of the current Manvantara he first taught this imperishable yoga to the sun-god Vivasvan, who told Manu, who told Ikshvaku, a royal-sage lineage later lost and now restored _(actors: Krishna, Vivasvan, Manu, Ikshvaku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/03-to-06-karma-shatka.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 4.1-3)
- **Kubera's penance and Brahma's boons** — Kubera performs severe tapas standing on one leg and Brahma grants him immortality, lordship of all wealth and the nine nidhis, the office of Lokapala of the North, and the Pushpaka vimana _(actors: Kubera, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kubera.md) — (Ramayana; Puranic tradition)
- **Mṛkaṇḍu's Boon and Choice** — The childless sage Mṛkaṇḍu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son destined to live only sixteen years over a dull long-lived one _(actors: Mṛkaṇḍu, Marudvatī, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Pravara rejects Varuthini** — The pious brahmana Pravara, stranded in the Himalayas after a flying-paste wears off, is propositioned by the lovesick apsaras Varuthini but refuses her, bound by his vow of one wife _(actors: Pravara, Varuthini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **Saraṇyū flees Vivasvat and the substitute is made** — After bearing Vivasvat twin children, Saraṇyū vanishes; the gods fashion a likeness (savarṇā) in her place, on whom the Aśvins are later begotten _(actors: Saraṇyū, Vivasvat, Tvaṣṭṛ)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.17.1-2; Nirukta 12.10; Bṛhaddevatā 6.162ff)
- **Sati born as Daksha's daughter** — The Great Goddess consents to be born as a daughter of the Prajapati Daksha, named Sati, specifically to win Shiva as her husband _(actors: Adi Shakti (Sati), Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda; Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII)
