- **The conscious deer-Bharata quits its body detached** — Born remembering his past life, the deer-Bharata abandons the herd, returns to Pulaha-ashrama, lives austerely, and quits the deer-body wholly detached _(actors: deer-Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.8)
- **The Pracetas and the Rudra-gita** — The ten Pracetas meet Shiva who teaches them the Rudra-gita, then perform a 10,000-year underwater austerity and father Daksha reborn _(actors: Pracetas, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.24, 4.30-31)
- **Birth of Hanumān and the vajra-strike** — Hanumān, son of Vāyu and Añjanā, leaps at the sun as an infant and is struck on the jaw by Indra's vajra (hence Hanumān), then heaped with boons by the gods _(actors: Hanumān, Vāyu, Añjanā, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 35)
- **Churning of Vena's corpse and birth of Prithu** — From the churned thigh of dead Vena emerges the dwarf Nishada, then from his churned arms arise Prithu (a Vishnu amsa-avatara) and his consort Arcis; Prithu is the first consecrated king _(actors: Prithu, Arcis, Nishada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.15)
- **Parvati's tapas and the Brahmin-test** — Parvati undertakes ferocious austerities to win Shiva by merit, earning the name Aparna; Shiva, disguised as a young Brahmin, disparages himself to test her, and on her fierce defense reveals himself and accepts her _(actors: Parvati, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Kumarasambhava 5; Shiva Purana)
- **Priyavrata Carves the Oceans and Continents** — Priyavrata drives his chariot seven times round Meru and the wheel-ruts become the seven oceans and continents _(actors: Priyavrata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.1)
- **Rebirth as Jada Bharata, the silent sage** — The soul is reborn in an Angirasa brahmana family and deliberately acts deaf, dumb, and dull to avoid entanglement, earning the mocking name Jada Bharata _(actors: Jada Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.9)
- **Sagara's sons burnt by Kapila** — Sagara's sons digging the ocean-bed for the lost sacrificial horse are incinerated by Kapila's glance _(actors: Sagara's sons, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **The mutual curses of Kaca and Devayānī** — When Kaca refuses to marry Devayānī on grounds of kinship, she curses that the Sañjīvanī will fail when he wields it, and he counter-curses that no brahmin will ever marry her — fating her to wed the kṣatriya Yayāti _(actors: Kaca, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 76)
- **Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into the well** — After Indra swaps their garments and a quarrel over rank erupts, the asura princess Śarmiṣṭhā strips, strikes, and casts Devayānī into a dry well, leaving her for dead _(actors: Śarmiṣṭhā, Devayānī, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 78)
- **Bhadra Kali saves Jada Bharata from human sacrifice** — Seized by a dasyu-chief's robbers to be offered to Bhadra Kali, Jada Bharata is saved when the goddess springs from her image, slays the would-be sacrificers, and frees him _(actors: Jada Bharata, Bhadra Kali, the dasyu robbers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.9)
- **Prithu milks the Earth** — When the famished Earth-cow hides her herbs, Prithu pursues her with drawn bow until she yields and is milked, using Svayambhuva Manu as calf, giving grain to beings and naming the Earth Prithvi _(actors: Prithu, Earth (Prithvi), Svayambhuva Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.17-18; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Sagara's 60,000 sons burnt by Kapila** — King Sagara's sixty thousand sons, digging for the sacrificial horse, wrongly accuse the meditating sage Kapila and are burnt to ash by his glance _(actors: Sagara, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 38–40)
- **Sages curse Hanumān to forget his powers** — For childhood mischief the ṛṣis curse Hanumān to forget his immense powers until reminded — the back-story for Jāmbavān's reminding before the ocean leap _(actors: Hanumān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 36)
- **Shibi offers his flesh to ransom a dove** — King Shibi, tested by Indra as a hawk and Agni as a dove, offers his own flesh to ransom the dove _(actors: Ushinara/Shibi, Indra, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **Sunatanartaka wins Parvati's hand** — Shiva takes the graceful dancer form to appear before Himavan as a wandering performer and win the hand of Parvati _(actors: Sunatanartaka (Shiva), Himavan, Parvati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **The Three Lives of Bharata (Jada Bharata)** — King Bharata, son of Rishabha, lives through three births (king, deer, then the realized dull brahmana) and instructs King Rahugana _(actors: Rishabha, Bharata, Rahugana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.2-14)
- **The wedding of Shiva and Parvati** — Himavan consents and Shiva sends the Saptarishi and Arundhati to ask for Parvati; the divine wedding draws all the gods _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Himavan, Saptarishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Kumarasambhava 6-7; Shiva Purana)
- **Birth of Skanda and the slaying of Taraka** — From the union of Shiva and Parvati comes Kumara/Skanda/Kartikeya, the war-god, who slays Taraka, the purpose of the whole rebirth-cycle _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Skanda, Taraka)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Kumarasambhava 7+; Shiva Purana)
- **Cyavana restored to youth by the Ashvins** — The aged Bhargava is restored to youth by the Ashvins, who in return gain a share of the soma _(actors: Cyavana, Sukanya, the Ashvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **Descent of the Gaṅgā (Gaṅgāvataraṇa)** — Bhagīratha's austerities bring Gaṅgā from heaven to redeem Sagara's sons' ashes; Śiva breaks her fall in his hair as Gaṅgādhara _(actors: Bhagīratha, Gaṅgā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 42–44)
- **Jada Bharata teaches King Rahugana (Bharata-gita and forest allegory)** — Conscripted to carry Rahugana's palanquin and rebuked for his erratic gait, Jada Bharata breaks his silence with the Bharata-gita and the bhavatavi forest-of-samsara allegory, humbling the king _(actors: Jada Bharata, King Rahugana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.10-14)
- **Prithu's 100 horse-sacrifices and clash with Indra** — Indra repeatedly steals Prithu's sacrificial horse in disguises until Brahma brokers peace, after which the four Kumaras and Vishnu instruct Prithu, who delivers a discourse and retires to the forest _(actors: Prithu, Indra, Brahma, the four Kumaras, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.19-23)
- **Yayāti rescues Devayānī from the well** — King Yayāti, hunting and thirsty, finds Devayānī in the well and lifts her out by her right hand, which she construes as a betrothal _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 78-81; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Śarmiṣṭhā enslaved to Devayānī** — Threatened with abandonment by his indispensable preceptor, Vṛṣaparvan gives his daughter Śarmiṣṭhā with a thousand maidens as a servant to the woman she wronged _(actors: Śarmiṣṭhā, Devayānī, Vṛṣaparvan, Śukrācārya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 81; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Aruna hatched prematurely as Surya's charioteer** — The legless dawn-deity Aruna, hatched prematurely from Vinata's egg, becomes the charioteer of Surya _(actors: Aruna, Vinata, Surya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Mahabharata; Garuda Purana)
- **Birth of Ganesha and his beheading** — Parvati creates Ganesha from the paste of her own body; his beheading and elephant-head restoration follows as a parallel myth _(actors: Parvati, Ganesha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita)
- **Narada Curses Daksha's Sons to Renunciation** — Narada turns Daksha's sons the Haryashvas and Savalashvas to renunciation, earning Daksha's counter-curse that Narada wander forever _(actors: Narada, Daksha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.5)
- **The ten Prachetas perform underwater tapas** — The ten Prachetas brothers undertake 10,000 years of underwater tapas, receiving from Vishnu the boon to be progenitors of mankind _(actors: The ten Prachetas, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.14-15; Bhagavata Purana 4.24-30)
- **Dadhichi gives his bones for the Vajra** — The sage gives his bones to forge Indra's Vajra weapon _(actors: Dadhichi, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **Marriage of Yayāti and Devayānī** — Śukra weds Devayānī to Yayāti on the binding condition that he never summon Śarmiṣṭhā, who enters the palace as part of the dowry-train _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī, Śukrācārya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 81-82; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Parvati becomes Gauri** — Taunted as dark, Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion and emerges radiant as Gauri, the sloughed dark sheath becoming the goddess Kaushiki/Kali _(actors: Parvati (Gauri), Kaushiki/Kali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana; Devi Mahatmya context)
- **Shiva teaches the Prachetas the Rudra-Gita** — Shiva (Rudra) appears to the Prachetas as they begin their austerity and teaches them the hymn of self-realization, the Rudra-Gita _(actors: Shiva, the Prachetas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.24)
- **The Prachetas' quarrel with the trees and birth of the second Daksha** — Emerging to find the Earth overgrown, the Prachetas nearly burn the forests until Soma mediates and gives them the tree-born maiden Marisha, from whom the reborn Daksha is born _(actors: The Prachetas, Soma, Marisha, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15; Bhagavata Purana 4.30)
- **The two queens bear five sons** — Yayāti secretly fathers children on Śarmiṣṭhā despite the oath; Devayānī bears Yadu and Turvaśu, Śarmiṣṭhā bears Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru — the breach that later provokes the curse of old age and splits the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 83-84; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Viśvāmitra wars with Vasiṣṭha over the wish-cow** — The kṣatriya king Viśvāmitra covets Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā, wars with him and loses, then begins millennia of tapas to become a brahmarṣi _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 51–65)
- **Vīrabhadra destroys Dakṣa's sacrifice** — After Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's yajña, the grief-maddened Śiva creates Vīrabhadra, who storms the sacrifice and beheads Dakṣa; Satī's scattered limbs become the Śakti Pīṭhas _(actors: Śiva, Satī, Dakṣa, Vīrabhadra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Kālikā Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Triśaṅku raised to heaven and the counter-heaven** — Viśvāmitra raises the outcast king Triśaṅku bodily to heaven and, when the gods cast him down, creates a counter-heaven holding him mid-sky _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Triśaṅku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 57–60)
- **Birth of Budha and the Tara Scandal** — Candra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, triggering the Tarakamaya war; Tara bears Budha of disputed paternity, and the Moon's waning is linked to a resulting curse _(actors: Candra, Tara, Brihaspati, Budha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata IX.14)
- **Śunaḥśepa saved from sacrifice** — The human-sacrifice victim Śunaḥśepa is saved by mantras Viśvāmitra gives him at Ambarīṣa's rite _(actors: Śunaḥśepa, Viśvāmitra, Ambarīṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 61–62)
- **Dhruva's Penance at Madhuvana** — The boy Dhruva performs tapas at Dhruva-ṭīlā in Madhuvana, one of the twelve forests of Braj _(actors: Dhruva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Vraja-mahatmya)
- **Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's penance; birth of Śakuntalā** — The apsarā Menakā seduces Viśvāmitra, begetting Śakuntalā; he later conquers desire and anger to win the title Brahmarṣi _(actors: Menakā, Viśvāmitra, Śakuntalā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 63–65)
- **Savitri wins back Satyavan from Yama** — The devoted wife out-argues Yama to win back her husband's life _(actors: Savitri, Satyavan, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva)
- **Daksha populates the worlds through his daughters** — Daksha Prajapati's daughters, married to the sages and to Kashyapa, become mothers of the Adityas (gods), Daityas, Danavas, animals, nagas and all living kinds; he later resorts to sexual generation _(actors: Daksha, Kashyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15, 1.21; Bhagavata Purana 6.6)
- **Indra seduces Ahalyā and is cursed** — Indra, disguised as the sage Gautama, seduces his wife Ahalyā; Gautama curses Indra and condemns Ahalyā to penance to be released only by Rāma _(actors: Indra, Ahalyā, Gautama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 48)
- **Galava and Madhavi** — Sage Galava lends out the princess Madhavi, who bears a king to each of four lords while regaining her virginity each time, to gather the guru-dakshina horses _(actors: Galava, Madhavi, Vishvamitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Bhagavadyana Parva)
- **Yayati's Exchange of Old Age** — Cursed with premature old age by Shukra for wronging Devayani, Yayati borrows youth from his son Puru, later returns it and crowns Puru over the elder Yadu _(actors: Yayati, Shukra, Devayani, Puru, Yadu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana IV.10; Bhagavata IX.18-19)
- **Pururavas and Urvasi** — The Lunar-line tale of Pururavas and the apsara Urvasi, a morality story on lust and renunciation _(actors: Pururavas, Urvasi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Sudyumna/Ila's Monthly Sex-Change** — Vaivasvata Manu's child enters Shiva's forbidden grove and alternates monthly between man (Sudyumna) and woman (Ila), branching the solar and lunar lines _(actors: Sudyumna, Ila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Nahusa kicked from heaven into serpenthood** — The over-proud Nahusa, made temporary Indra, is kicked from heaven by Agastya into serpenthood _(actors: Nahusa, Agastya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Anushasana/Santi Parva)
- **Reign of Svayambhuva, the first Manu** — Svayambhuva, the self-born spiritual son of Brahma, rules the first manvantara and is the reputed promulgator of the Manu Smriti _(actors: Svayambhuva Manu, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Manu Smriti 1, Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Vaivasvata's sons found the royal lineages** — Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties — Ikshvaku begins the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeds the Lunar line through Pururavas _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2, 4.1, Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest (the Trimūrti test)** — The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in the Bhṛgu-pada test to decide the supreme god, cursing and blessing the Trimūrti accordingly and earning the Śrīvatsa mark _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.89; Padma Purāṇa)
- **Soma Abducts Tara and the Birth of Budha** — Soma abducts Brihaspati's wife Tara, Budha is born of the union, and the lunar dynasty begins _(actors: Soma, Tara, Budha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Vamana subdues Bali in the Vaivasvata manvantara** — The dwarf-brahmin Vamana, manvantara-avatara of the present age, reclaims the three worlds from the demon-king Bali in three steps and restores them to Indra Purandara _(actors: Vamana, Bali, Indra Purandara)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23, Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Birth of the submarine fire from Aurva's wrath** — The seer Aurva's world-burning wrath against the kṣatriyas produces the submarine fire (Vāḍava), which is restrained into the ocean-mare's-mouth _(actors: Aurva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Rantideva's Fourfold Charity** — After a 48-day fast, King Rantideva gives away his last food and water to a brahmana, a shudra, a man with dogs, and a chandala, and the testing Trimurti grant him liberation _(actors: Rantideva, Trimurti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.21)
- **The caru-swap of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī** — The brahmin and kṣatriya rice-cakes are exchanged in the marriage of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī, producing a martial brahmin line and a priestly king _(actors: Ṛcīka, Satyavatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Mahābhārata; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Soma, Dattātreya and Durvāsas to Atri** — By the Trimūrti's boon, the sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā father three deities as sons: Soma (Candra), Dattātreya and Durvāsas _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Soma, Dattātreya, Durvāsas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Chandra from Atri** — Chandra is born to the sage Atri and his chaste wife Anasuya, welling from Atri's penetrating gaze/tears of austerity (in some versions as an amsa of Brahma), and is placed in the sky by Brahma _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Chandra, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Vishnu, Bhagavata 4, Brahmanda Puranas)
- **Budha weds Ila and Pururavas is born** — Budha marries Ila (originally Sudyumna, Vaivasvata Manu's son cursed to alternate sexes), and their son Pururavas begins the human lunar dynasty (Aila line) _(actors: Budha, Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4; Bhagavata 9.14)
- **Indra grants the Puṣpaka and Uparicara Vasu's vimāna** — Indra grants King Uparicara Vasu a crystalline aerial car letting him move godlike through the sky _(actors: Indra, Uparicara Vasu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Vimana (Wikipedia); Mahabharata)
- **Dakṣa-yajña: Satī's self-immolation and Dakṣa's beheading** — Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's sacrifice; in the catastrophe Dakṣa is beheaded by Vīrabhadra and later restored with a goat's head _(actors: Dakṣa, Satī, Vīrabhadra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Nārada cursed by Dakṣa to wander ceaselessly** — For persuading Dakṣa's sons to renounce procreation, Nārada is cursed by Dakṣa to wander the worlds eternally _(actors: Nārada, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5)
- **Nārada converts the Haryaśvas to renunciation** — Dakṣa's first thousand sons, the Haryaśvas, sent to procreate, are dissuaded by Nārada's riddle and renounce and disperse forever _(actors: Nārada, Haryaśvas, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Nārada converts the Śabalāśvas** — Dakṣa's next thousand sons, the Śabalāśvas, are likewise converted by Nārada, enraging Dakṣa into cursing him, after which Dakṣa begets daughters instead _(actors: Nārada, Śabalāśvas, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Dakṣa's daughters wed Kaśyapa and breed all beings** — Dakṣa's daughters married to Kaśyapa (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā and others) produce every class of being — devas, daityas, dānavas, nāgas, birds, beasts and more _(actors: Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21; Bhāgavata 6.6)
- **Dakṣa gives 27 nakṣatra-daughters to Candra; the Moon's curse** — Dakṣa marries 27 daughters (the lunar mansions) to Candra, whose neglect of all but Rohiṇī provokes Dakṣa's curse that the Moon waxes and wanes, partly relieved at Prabhāsa _(actors: Dakṣa, Candra, Rohiṇī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.14; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Nara-Nārāyaṇa to Mūrti and Dharma** — Dakṣa's daughter Mūrti, married to Dharma, mothers the twin sage-avatāra Nara-Nārāyaṇa of Viṣṇu _(actors: Mūrti, Dharma, Nara-Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Satī reborn as Pārvatī** — After self-immolating at the Dakṣa-yajña, Dakṣa's daughter Satī, wife of Śiva, is reborn as Pārvatī _(actors: Satī, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Bhāgavata 4.2–7)
- **Agastya's curse of Indradyumna** — King Indradyumna, a Pandya/Dravida devotee, is cursed by sage Agastya to be reborn as an elephant for a lapse of courtesy, becoming Gajendra _(actors: Agastya, Indradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Devala's curse of the gandharva Huhu** — The gandharva Huhu is cursed by sage Devala to become a crocodile for seizing his leg in the water, becoming the graha that attacks Gajendra _(actors: Devala, Huhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)

## Satya (Kṛta) Yuga — current 28th Mahāyuga  ·  175 events

*Dharma on four legs. The early avatars and the churning of the ocean.*

- **Apsarās arise from the Samudra Manthana** — The celestial nymphs arise from the churned waters between devas and asuras; claimed by neither side, they become common (sādhāraṇa) to all _(actors: Apsarās, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 45; Mahābhārata)
- **Avatara of Mahotkata Vinayaka** — Ganesha descends in Satya Yuga as the ten-armed lion-mounted Mahotkata Vinayaka and slays the demon-brothers Narantaka and Devantaka (and Dhumraksha) _(actors: Ganesha (Mahotkata Vinayaka), Narantaka, Devantaka, Dhumraksha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda))
- **Birth of Nara–Nārāyaṇa to Dharma and Mūrti** — The twin sage-avatāra of Viṣṇu are born to the prajāpati Dharma and his wife Mūrti (var. Ahiṃsā), among the ascetic offspring of Dharma's line _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Dharma, Mūrti/Ahiṃsā, Dakṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana** — When devas and asuras churn the Ocean of Milk with Mount Mandara and Vasuki, Dhanvantari rises bearing the pot of amrita, precipitating the deva-asura war over the nectar _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Ramayana Bala-kanda 45)
- **Jaya–Vijaya born as Hiraṇyakaśipu (birth #1)** — Viṣṇu's cursed Vaikuṇṭha gatekeepers incarnate as the daitya brothers Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu, the first of three demonic births _(actors: Jaya, Vijaya, Diti, Kaśyapa, Sanaka-kumāras, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1–7.2; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.17)
- **Madhu & Kaiṭabha Slain** — Two primordial Dānava brothers born from Viṣṇu's ear menace Brahmā and steal the Vedas, slain by Viṣṇu after the Goddess Yoganidrā withdraws her sleep-spell; their fat forms the earth _(actors: Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Viṣṇu, Yoganidrā, Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Devī Māhātmya 1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Matsya avatara and the great deluge** — Vishnu as a fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of the world-ending flood, tows his boat (Saptarshi, seeds, creatures) to safety via Vasuki tied to his horn, and slays Hayagriva to recover the stolen Vedas _(actors: Vishnu (Matsya), Vaivasvata Manu, Saptarshi, Vasuki, Hayagriva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Matsya saves Manu from the deluge flood** — A tiny fish begging Manu's protection grows monstrous and reveals itself as Vishnu, warns of the deluge, and tows Manu's ark — loaded with the seeds of beings, the seven rishis and the Vedas — to safety, then narrates the Purana _(actors: Vishnu (Matsya), Manu Vaivasvata, the seven rishis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana (frame))
- **Samudra Manthana and the Spilling of Amṛta** — The churning of the ocean of milk produces the kumbha of amrita; in the ensuing fight, drops spill at four earthly sites that become the Kumbh Mela cities _(actors: devas, asuras, Viṣṇu, Garuḍa, Dhanvantari)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Britannica)
- **Samudra Manthana — emergence of the fourteen ratnas** — The Devas and Asuras churn the milk-ocean using Mt. Mandara and the serpent Vāsuki, drawing up the fourteen ratnas including Amṛta, Kāmadhenu, Kalpavṛkṣa, Kaustubha, Airāvata, Uccaiḥśravas and Lakṣmī _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Vāsuki, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9)
- **Surabhi Churned from the Ocean of Milk** — Surabhi/Kāmadhenu rises among the fourteen ratnas churned from the Ocean of Milk, and Brahmā assigns her to yield the milk and ghee of Vedic sacrifice, giving her to the seven ṛṣis _(actors: Surabhi/Kāmadhenu, Brahmā, seven ṛṣis)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas)
- **The Matsya flood and Manu's survival** — Vishnu as the Fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of a world-dissolving deluge, has him build a boat carrying the seven sages, seeds, and creatures, and tows it to a Himalayan peak by a horn on the fish's head, preserving the seeds of life into the new age _(actors: Matsya/Vishnu, Vaivasvata Manu (Satyavrata), the Saptarishi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva 3.186; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vamana measures the three worlds (Trivikrama)** — Born as a dwarf brahmana to Aditi and Kashyapa, Vishnu begs three paces from the asura-king Bali, swells into cosmic Trivikrama, and presses Bali to the netherworld, restoring Indra's sovereignty _(actors: Vamana/Vishnu, Bali, Aditi, Kashyapa, Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana; cf. Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Vishnu-as-Kurma bears Mount Mandara at the churning** — Vishnu descends as the tortoise Kurma to support sinking Mount Mandara during the Samudra-manthana, and from within that episode discourses the whole Purana to King Indradyumna _(actors: Vishnu (Kurma), King Indradyumna, the rishis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (opening))
- **Vāsuki the Churning-Rope at Samudra Manthana** — The nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mount Mandara at the Samudra Manthana, vomiting the Hālāhala poison that Śiva drinks, and is worn by Śiva as a neck-ornament _(actors: Vāsuki, Śiva, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Dhanvantari rises last bearing the Amṛta-kumbha** — The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Āyurveda, rises last from the churning bearing the pot (kumbha) of amṛta, the nectar of immortality _(actors: Dhanvantari, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Durvasa's curse and Lakshmi's withdrawal** — Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra slights and Airavata tramples; the offended Lakshmi abandons the three worlds, which lose their lustre, prompting the churning to recover her _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Lakshmi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Durvasa's curse triggers the churning** — Durvasa's garland is trampled by Indra's elephant Airavata; he curses the Devas to lose their shri, Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean, and the Asuras rout the weakened Devas _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Airavata, Lakshmi, Bali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Eternal tapas at Badarīkāśrama** — Nara and Nārāyaṇa retire to the Himālayan hermitage of Badarī (Badrīnāth) and perform unbroken, cyclically-renewed austerity for the welfare of the worlds _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Śānti Parva)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu's vow of vengeance** — After Hiraṇyākṣa is slain by Varāha, Hiraṇyakaśipu swears to destroy Viṣṇu and all his devotees _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Diti, Hiraṇyākṣa (slain), Varāha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.2)
- **Hiraṇyākṣa Slain by Varāha** — The daitya Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth down into the cosmic ocean and is slain by Viṣṇu as the Boar Varāha, who lifts Earth back on his tusks _(actors: Hiraṇyākṣa, Viṣṇu (Varāha))_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13-19; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Matsya saves Manu and recovers the Vedas from Hayagrīva** — Viṣṇu's fish-avatāra grows enormous, warns Vaivasvata Manu of the deluge, tows his boat with the seven ṛṣis and the seeds/Vedas to safety, and recovers the Vedas from the demon Hayagrīva _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Vaivasvata Manu, Hayagrīva, seven ṛṣis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 2)
- **Matsya slays Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas** — In the Puranic version the Matsya avatar slays the demon Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas he had stolen _(actors: Matsya/Vishnu, Hayagriva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Matsya Purana)
- **Mohinī distributes the amṛta to the devas** — After the ocean-churning Viṣṇu takes his only female form, Mohinī, beguiling the asuras and distributing the nectar of immortality to the devas alone _(actors: Mohinī (Viṣṇu), devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8-9, 8.12; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Mohini Tricks the Asuras for the Amṛta** — Viṣṇu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini to seize the pot of amrita and trick the asuras out of immortality _(actors: Viṣṇu (Mohini), asuras)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Origin of Mahalakshmi at the churning** — Lakshmi (Sri) rises among the treasures churned from the milk-ocean and chooses Vishnu, exalted as the supreme Shakti _(actors: Lakshmi (Sri), Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Prahlada counsels Andhaka and undertakes a tirtha-circuit** — The Vishnu-devotee Prahlada counsels his kinsman Andhaka against lust for Gauri and later makes an extended pilgrimage circuit, serving as a vehicle for the text's pilgrimage doctrine _(actors: Prahlada, Andhaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana)
- **Samudra Manthana — churning of the ocean** — Gods and asuras churn the milk-ocean with Mandara and Vasuki over Kurma, producing the fourteen ratnas (Lakshmi, Dhanvantari with amrita, the poison Shiva swallows, etc.), and Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar _(actors: devas, asuras, Vishnu (Kurma, Mohini), Vasuki, Shiva, Dhanvantari, Lakshmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana)
- **The Matsya flood and rescue of Vaivasvata Manu** — Vishnu as Matsya the fish warns Vaivasvata of a coming deluge; the Manu builds a boat tied to the fish's horn and carries the seven sages, seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, founding current humanity _(actors: Matsya (Vishnu), Vaivasvata Manu, Saptarishis)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva)
- **Vishnu takes Mohini form to recover the amrita** — After the asuras seize the amrita-pot, Vishnu takes the enchantress Mohini form to recover and redistribute the nectar to the devas _(actors: Vishnu/Mohini, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9)
- **Vāruṇī Emerges at the Churning** — Vāruṇī, goddess of wine and consort of Varuṇa, emerges among the treasures churned from the ocean at the Samudra Manthana _(actors: Vāruṇī, Varuṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/dikpalas-and-lokapalas.md) — (Samudra Manthana tradition)
- **Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope at the Samudra Manthana** — The Nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mt. Mandara at the Samudra Manthana _(actors: Vāsuki, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md (cross-ref))
- **Yogeśvarī Emitted Against Andhaka's Blood** — When Śiva spears Andhaka and each blood-drop becomes a new demon, Śiva emits Yogeśvarī from his mouth-flame and the gods send their śaktis to follow and drink the blood, checking the flood _(actors: Śiva, Yogeśvarī, Andhaka, the gods' śaktis)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati; Matsya Purāṇa 179; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Cursed devas churn the Milk Ocean** — The weakened devas lose to the asuras and are told to churn the Milk Ocean in alliance with them to recover amṛta and lost treasures, from which Airāvata and Uccaiḥśravas re-emerge _(actors: Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.6; Mahābhārata Ādiparva)
- **Emergence of Lakshmi from the Samudra Manthana** — When devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean, Lakshmi rises seated on a lotus among the ratnas, is bathed by the celestial elephants, and garlands Vishnu as her eternal consort _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.9; Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Mahabharata)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu Slain by Narasiṃha** — Granted a loophole-bound boon of invulnerability, Hiraṇyakaśipu tortures his devotee-son Prahlāda and is slain by Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha at twilight on a threshold _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Viṣṇu (Narasiṃha), Prahlāda)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Ikshvaku Founds Ayodhya** — Ikshvaku, eldest son of Manu, establishes the Solar dynasty and the kingdom of Kosala at Ayodhya after the deluge _(actors: Ikshvaku)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2; Bhagavata IX.6)
- **Kurma avatara supports Mount Mandara** — As Mandara (churning rod) wound with Vasuki sinks into the ocean of milk, Vishnu incarnates as the tortoise Kurma to bear the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning _(actors: Vishnu (Kurma), Vasuki, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana)
- **Manu and the Flood (Matsya rescue)** — Viṣṇu as the fish (Matsya) warns Manu of the pralaya-flood and saves him and the seeds of life across the deluge — the earliest extant Hindu flood account _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī** — The Śiva Purāṇa narrates the marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī among the central cosmic Śaiva events _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Nārāyaṇa produces Urvaśī from his thigh to humble Indra's apsarās** — When Indra sends Kāmadeva and apsarās to break their penance, the unmoved Nārāyaṇa creates the nymph Urvaśī from his thigh, shaming Indra's nymphs, then gifts her to the gods _(actors: Nārāyaṇa, Nara, Indra, Kāmadeva, the apsarās, Urvaśī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Samudra Manthana (Churning of the Ocean of Milk)** — Devas and asuras use Mandara as the churning-rod and Vasuki as the rope to churn the ocean; Vishnu as Kurma bears the sinking mountain, and the fourteen ratnas including amrita and Lakshmi rise _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Vishnu (Kurma), Vasuki)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.6-8; Mahabharata Adi-parva; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **The boon of near-invulnerability** — Through extreme tapas Hiraṇyakaśipu wins from Brahmā a death hedged by impossibilities — no created being, no weapon, not day or night, not inside or outside, not earth or sky, not man or beast _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.3)
- **The Mātṛkās' Rampage and Pacification** — Drunk on power after drinking the demon-blood, the Mātṛkās begin devouring gods, demons and creatures indiscriminately until Viṣṇu/Śiva must pacify them _(actors: Mātṛkās, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Vaivasvata Manu begets the ten progenitor children** — Through a son-yielding sacrifice, Manu and his wife Shraddha beget ten children who found the two great royal lines, including Ikshvaku and Ila/Sudyumna _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Shraddha, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9; Vishnu Purana 4)
- **Airāvata emerges from the churning** — The white elephant-king Airāvata rises from the Samudra-manthana as one of the ratnas and is seized by Indra as his vāhana and East-guardian _(actors: Airāvata, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9; Mahābhārata)
- **Amṛta Falls at Brahmakund (Haridwar)** — A drop of amṛta from the celestial kumbha spills at Brahmakund within Har-ki-Pauri during the flight after the Samudra Manthana, making it Haridwar's holiest bathing point and a Kumbh site _(actors: Garuḍa, devas, asuras)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia, Haridwar Kumbh Mela; Puranic Kumbh sources)
- **Births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya** — The Śiva Purāṇa records the births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya (Skanda) _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa, Kārttikeya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Conquest of the three worlds** — Armoured by the boon, Hiraṇyakaśipu usurps the realms of the devas and rules heaven, earth, and underworld as universal tyrant _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.4; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.17)
- **Dhanvantari rises from the ocean with the amṛta** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the churned ocean bearing the pot of amṛta, founding and patronizing Āyurveda _(actors: Dhanvantari (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.3, 8.8; Garuḍa Purāṇa)
- **Drops of amṛta fall at the four Kumbh Mela sites** — During the deva-asura scramble for the kumbha, drops of nectar fall at Prayāg, Haridvāra, Ujjain and Nāsik — the etiology of the Kumbh Mela _(actors: Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Puranic/folk tradition)
- **Halahala poison and Shiva Nilakantha** — The world-destroying Halahala poison rises first from the churn; Shiva drinks it and Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Kūrma supports the churning of the ocean** — The tortoise-avatāra Kūrma serves as the support beneath Mount Mandara during the churning of the ocean _(actors: Kūrma (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 3)
- **Prahlāda Survives His Father's Attempts** — Prahlāda, a Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb, miraculously survives poison, fire and the pillar, becoming the paradigmatic bhakta and a righteous asura-king _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Sharabha pacifies Narasimha** — Shiva assumes the colossal part-lion part-bird Sharabha form to pacify Vishnu's Narasimha when his fury threatens the cosmos _(actors: Sharabha (Shiva), Narasimha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Sharabha Upanishad)
- **The Churning of the Ocean (Amrita-manthana)** — The churning of the milk-ocean to win amrita, told within the Astika frame to explain the gods' immortality _(actors: devas, asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Astika Parva)
- **Vikukshi Shashada Eats the Sacrificial Hare** — Sent to fetch sacrificial meat, Vikukshi eats a hare himself, earning the nickname Shashada and a brief exile _(actors: Vikukshi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2)
- **Vṛtra slain by Indra** — Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra, who withheld the cosmic waters, with the Vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32, Mahābhārata, Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9-13)
- **Birth and devotion of Prahlāda** — Prahlāda, son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, is a perfected Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb (taught by Nārada), rejecting demon-schooling and preaching bhakti _(actors: Prahlāda, Nārada, Ṣaṇḍa, Amarka, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.4–7.5, 7.7)
- **Dakṣa's sacrifice** — The Śiva Purāṇa narrates Dakṣa's sacrifice and its destruction, a key cosmic Śaiva event _(actors: Dakṣa, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Descent of the Ganga (Gangavataran) at Gangotri** — The Ganga descends from heaven at Gangotri to liberate the ancestors of King Bhagiratha, the headstream named Bhagirathi after him _(actors: Ganga, Bhagiratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Ramayana/Mahabharata Gangavataran legend)
- **Emergence of Lakshmi from the ocean** — The goddess of fortune re-emerges radiant from the churned ocean and of her own choice garlands and weds Vishnu, restoring shri to the cosmos _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **First demonic birth: Hiranyaksa and Hiranyakasipu slain** — Jaya and Vijaya are reborn as the asura brothers Hiranyaksa (slain by Varaha) and Hiranyakasipu (torn open by Narasimha) in Satya-yuga _(actors: Hiranyaksa, Hiranyakasipu, Varaha, Narasimha, Prahlada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.17-19; 7.2-8)
- **Ila/Sudyumna roots the Lunar Dynasty** — Ila/Sudyumna, who shifts between female and male after entering a Shiva-sacred grove, becomes root of the Chandra Vamsha via the child Pururavas, descending to the Kurus, Pandavas, and Krishna's kin _(actors: Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas, Budha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Mahabharata)
- **Kakutstha Rides Indra-as-Bull** — Puranjaya rides into battle against the Asuras seated on Indra's hump in bull form, earning the patronymic Kakutstha later applied to Rama _(actors: Kakutstha/Puranjaya, Indra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Ramayana)
- **Kāmadhenu given to the Saptarṣi and Vasiṣṭha** — The wish-cow Kāmadhenu emerges from the churning and is given to the seven sages, passing into the keeping of Vasiṣṭha _(actors: Kāmadhenu, Saptarṣi, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Kamadhenu (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Namuci beheaded by Indra** — Indra circumvents Namuci's boon by decapitating him at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra, neither wet nor dry, by day nor night _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda, Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, Mahābhārata)
- **Sanaka-kumaras curse Jaya and Vijaya** — Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya are cursed by the four child-sages to three demonic births each ending in death at the Lord's hand, of which Shishupala is the third _(actors: Sanaka-kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1)
- **Shiva Drinks the Hālāhala Poison at Alangudi** — During the Samudra Manthana the world-destroying halahala poison rises first and Shiva drinks it to save creation, his throat turning blue; Alangudi is held to be the spot, making Shiva Apatsahaya, savior in distress _(actors: Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Sthala-purana; Samudra Manthana cycle)
- **Varaha avatara slays Hiranyaksa** — The Boar avatara lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters and slays the demon Hiranyaksa, the first life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse _(actors: Varaha/Viṣṇu, Hiranyaksa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3)
- **Varaha Stays on Venkata Hill After Slaying Hiranyaksha** — In a variant, the Varaha avatar remains on the hill as guardian after lifting the earth and slaying Hiranyaksha, and Shrinivasa must obtain his permission to settle there _(actors: Varaha, Hiranyaksha, Shrinivasa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Sthala Purana of Tirumala)
- **Agastya drinks the ocean to expose the Kālakeyas** — To destroy the ocean-hiding Kālakeyas who devoured sages by night, the gods enlist Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry _(actors: Agastya, the Kālakeyas, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Birth of Mandhatr from His Father's Side** — Mandhatr is born from his father Yuvanashva's side after the king drinks consecrated water meant for his queen, and becomes a universal emperor _(actors: Mandhatr, Yuvanashva, Indra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2; Mahabharata)
- **Daksha's yajna and Sati's self-immolation** — Prajapati Daksha holds a grand sacrifice snubbing his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva; insulted when she attends uninvited, Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Dhanvantari rises with the amrita** — The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Ayurveda and an aspect of Vishnu, rises last from the ocean bearing the kalasha of amrita, the goal of the entire churning _(actors: Dhanvantari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Mahabharata; Vishnu Purana)
- **Hālāhala / Nīlakaṇṭha — Śiva drinks the world-poison** — During the churning of the milk-ocean Vāsuki disgorges the all-destroying Hālāhala poison; Śiva drinks it and Pārvatī halts it at his throat, making him the blue-throated saviour of creation _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Vāsuki)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Indra bears the Kalpavṛkṣa to Svarga** — The wish-fulfilling tree Kalpavṛkṣa emerges at the churning and Indra carries it to his paradise, rooting it in the Nandana-vana _(actors: Indra, Kalpavṛkṣa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Kalpavriksha (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Jyeshtha/Alakshmi rises from the churning** — Alakshmi as Jyeshtha, elder sister of Lakshmi, rises from the churning before the nectar and is later married off to the sage Duhsaha, dwelling wherever inauspiciousness is found _(actors: Jyeshtha (Alakshmi), Duhsaha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Linga Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Kapila teaches Devahuti (Kapilopadesa)** — The Kapila avatara, born to Kardama and Devahuti, teaches his mother devotional Sankhya and bhakti-yoga, a primary scriptural Sankhya source _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **King Indradyumna Seeks Nila-Madhava** — Satya-Yuga Malava king Indradyumna sends brahmin Vidyapati (who weds the Shabara chief's daughter Lalita) to find the secret Nila-Madhava image; it vanishes, directing the king to worship a sacred floating log instead _(actors: Indradyumna, Vidyapati, Vishvavasu, Lalita)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana)
- **Markandeya conquers death at the Shiva-linga** — At his destined hour of death the boy Markandeya clasps the Shiva-linga chanting the Maha-mrityunjaya mantra; Shiva bursts forth, defeats Yama, and grants him eternal youth _(actors: Markandeya, Shiva, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Skanda/Linga/Padma Puranas; Markandeya Purana)
- **Prahlāda expounds navadhā bhakti** — Confronting his father, Prahlāda declares Hari is everywhere and teaches the ninefold path of devotion, sealing his father's murderous resolve _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5.23–24, 7.8)
- **Gaṅgādhara — Śiva bears the descent of Gaṅgā** — When Bhagīratha's penance brings the celestial Gaṅgā down to redeem Sagara's 60,000 sons, Śiva catches her world-shattering fall in his matted locks and releases her as a tamed stream, humbling her pride _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Mohini distributes the nectar to the Devas** — The Asuras seize the amrita; Vishnu takes the enchantress form Mohini, beguiles them, and serves the nectar only to the Devas _(actors: Vishnu (Mohini), Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **The failed killings of Prahlāda** — Hiraṇyakaśipu has Prahlāda trampled, bitten, hurled from cliffs, burned, poisoned, and cast into the sea; Viṣṇu shields him each time. Folk tradition adds the Holikā fire-ordeal (etiology of Holī) _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Holikā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5; later Purāṇic/festival tradition (Holikā))
- **The Unfinished Carving of Jagannatha** — A divine carpenter carves the Puri triad on condition of being undisturbed; the door is opened early, so the images remain armless and legless, and Brahma is brought to consecrate the temple _(actors: Vishnu/Vishvakarma, Indradyumna, Gundica, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana; Brahma & Narada Puranas)
- **Virabhadra destroys Daksha's sacrifice** — Enraged at Sati's death, Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of his hair, who destroy the yajna and behead Daksha; Shiva later revives Daksha with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Viṣṇu claims the Kaustubha jewel from the churning** — The supreme jewel Kaustubha emerges from the Samudra Manthana and Viṣṇu claims it, wearing it on his chest alongside the Śrīvatsa and Vaijayantī _(actors: Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Vishnu Purana; Kaustubha (Wikipedia))
- **Beheading of Svarbhānu (Origin of Rāhu and Ketu)** — During the Samudra Manthana the asura Svarbhanu disguises himself to sip the amrita; exposed by Sun and Moon, Vishnu as Mohini beheads him with the Sudarshana Chakra, and his immortal head becomes Rahu and body becomes Ketu, who cause eclipses _(actors: Svarbhanu, Vishnu (Mohini), Surya, Chandra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Samudra Manthana cycle)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse; Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts it into pieces that fall across the land, founding the Shakti Pithas, and Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati, Vishnu, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Harishchandra's Truth-Test** — Harishchandra sells himself, wife, and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra and is tested mercilessly but never lies, restored and ascending to heaven as the archetype of satya _(actors: Harishchandra, Vishvamitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Aitareya Brahmana; Devi-Bhagavata)
- **Indra Slays Vṛtra with the Vajra** — The drought-serpent Dānava Vṛtra withholds the cosmic waters and is slain by Indra with the vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers — the foundational Vedic combat _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32; Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9-13)
- **The pillar challenge and Narasiṃha bursting forth** — Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes a pillar to disprove Viṣṇu's omnipresence; Narasiṃha, the man-lion, erupts from it roaring _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.12–22; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.20; Narasiṃha Purāṇa)
- **Varāha lifts the Earth** — Viṣṇu as the boar (Varāha) raises the Earth from the cosmic waters — a Satya-Yuga / Manvantara-boundary avatāra event framing the Varāha Purāṇa _(actors: Varāha (Viṣṇu), Earth (Bhūmi))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Varāha Purāṇa)
- **Indra Decapitates Namuci with Sea-Foam** — Bound by a truce and a no-wet-no-dry boon, Indra beheads the asura Namuci at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra — the loophole-archetype and origin of his brahmahatyā guilt-stain _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Skanda slays Tārakāsura** — The Skanda Purāṇa records Skanda/Kārttikeya's birth and his slaying of the demon Tārakāsura _(actors: Skanda/Kārttikeya, Tārakāsura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa)
- **The threshold disembowelment of Hiraṇyakaśipu** — At twilight, on the doorway threshold, on his lap, with bare claws, Narasiṃha disembowels Hiraṇyakaśipu — voiding every loophole of the boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.23–29)
- **Uccaiḥśravas emerges from the churning** — The seven-headed snow-white horse-king Uccaiḥśravas arises at the Samudra-manthana, born of the amṛta, and is seized by Indra (or claimed by Bali) _(actors: Uccaiḥśravas, Indra, Bali)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **War over the nectar and Indra restored** — Strengthened by the amrita, the Devas with Vishnu defeat the Asuras in the post-churning war and Indra is reinstated to Svarga _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11; Mahabharata)
- **Agastya Drinks the Ocean Dry, Kālakeyas Slain** — The ocean-hiding Kālakeyas devour sages by night until the gods beg Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry, exposing and enabling the slaughter of the Kālakeya asuras _(actors: Agastya, Kālakeyas, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Bhagiratha Brings Down the Ganga** — Through epic tapas Bhagiratha brings Ganga from heaven to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons, with Shiva catching her in his locks; the river is named Bhagirathi for him _(actors: Bhagiratha, Ganga, Shiva)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata IX.9)
- **Curse of the Sanaka-kumaras on Jaya and Vijaya** — Brahma's four child-sages curse Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya to three demonic births, setting off the Hiranyaksha/Hiranyakashipu and later demon incarnations _(actors: Sanaka-kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12, 3.15-3.16, 7.1)
- **Kāmadahana — the burning of Kāma** — Sent by the gods to kindle Śiva's desire for Pārvatī so a son can slay Tārakāsura, Kāmadeva fires his arrow and Śiva's third eye burns him to ash; Śiva later restores him bodiless (Ananga) _(actors: Śiva, Kāmadeva, Rati, Pārvatī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa; Kālidāsa's Kumārasaṃbhava)
- **Prahlāda pacifies Narasiṃha's wrath** — Narasiṃha's fury terrifies even the gods and Lakṣmī; the child Prahlāda alone calms him with the Nṛsiṃha-stuti and is offered any boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Prahlāda, Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.9–7.10)
- **Samudra Manthana - the curse that triggers it** — Sage Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra's elephant Airavata tramples; Durvasa curses the devas to lose their fortune and strength, and Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Airavata, Lakshmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Varaha rescues Bhudevi from the cosmic ocean** — As Bhudevi, the Earth goddess is rescued by the boar Varaha from the cosmic ocean _(actors: Varaha, Bhudevi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Daskavatara tradition)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu liberated; Prahlāda enthroned** — Slain by the Lord's own hand, Hiraṇyakaśipu attains liberation (dveṣa-bhakti), discharging curse-birth #1; Narasiṃha enthrones Prahlāda as righteous daitya king, whose line leads to Bali _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Bali (descendant))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1, 7.10)
- **Kurma supports Mount Mandara** — As the churning rod Mount Mandara sinks, Vishnu becomes the giant tortoise Kurma and bears the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning the Ocean of Milk for amrita _(actors: Kurma/Vishnu, devas, asuras, Vasuki, Mandara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Vishnu Purana)
- **The Kadrū–Vinatā wager over the horse's tail** — Kadrū and Vinatā wager over the colour of Uccaiḥśravas's tail with the loser to become slave; Kadrū's nāga sons coil as black hairs to deceive, winning and enslaving Vinatā _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Tārakāsura Slain by Skanda** — The daitya Tāraka, boon-protected to die only by a son of Śiva, forces the gods to engineer Śiva's marriage to Pārvatī, whose son Kārttikeya/Skanda slays him in the Tārakāmaya war _(actors: Tārakāsura, Skanda, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Varaha avatara rescues the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — The Asura Hiranyaksha drags Bhumi to the bottom of the cosmic ocean; Vishnu as the boar Varaha dives in, slays him in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth on his tusks _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha), Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Emergence of the fourteen ratnas** — During the churning fourteen treasures rise from the ocean — including Kamadhenu, Uccaihshravas, Airavata, Kaustubha, Parijata, the Apsaras, Lakshmi, Varuni, Candra, Shankha, and Dhanvantari with the amrita _(actors: the churning devas and asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8.8; Vishnu Purana; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Śiva Burns the Three Cities (Tripurāntaka)** — Three sons of Tāraka win three indestructible flying fortresses destroyable only by a single aligned arrow; Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns all three with one shaft from his earth-chariot _(actors: Śiva, Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Kadrū curses the reluctant nāgas** — The serpents who refuse to deceive the tail are cursed by their mother Kadrū to perish in King Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, driving the Mahābhārata's nāga frame-story _(actors: Kadrū, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Matsya saves Manu from the pralaya-flood** — Viṣṇu as the fish Matsya saves Manu and the seeds of life across the deluge — the Manvantara-transition framing the Matsya Purāṇa _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Andhaka Impaled by Śiva** — The blind asura Andhaka, born of Pārvatī covering Śiva's eyes, lusts after Pārvatī and is impaled on Śiva's triśūla until his clone-spawning blood dries, drunk by the Mātṛkās; redeemed, he becomes the gaṇa-chief Bhṛṅgi _(actors: Andhaka, Śiva, Pārvatī, Mātṛkās)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Garuḍa ransoms Vinatā by stealing the amṛta** — To redeem his enslaved mother Vinatā, Garuḍa is forced to fetch the amṛta from Indra's heaven, originating his nectar-theft, his enmity with the serpents and his recruitment as Viṣṇu's vāhana _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva, Garuḍa cycle)
- **Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu** — Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha kills the demon Hiraṇyakaśipu to protect the devotee Prahlāda — a Satya-Yuga avatāra event _(actors: Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu), Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Nṛsiṃha (Narasiṃha) Upapurāṇa)
- **Prahlada's devotion survives every attempt to kill him** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-bhakti by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Saptarishi carried across the flood by Vaivasvata Manu** — In the Matsya flood, Vaivasvata Manu carries the seven sages, the seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, re-seeding knowledge for the current humanity _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, the Saptarishi, Matsya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Shiva drinks the Halahala poison (Nilakantha)** — To save the cosmos from the world-destroying Halahala poison that first rises, Shiva drinks it; Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Holika burns in the fire - origin of Holi** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but perishes while he survives, the origin myth of the festival of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk/festival tradition)
- **Jalandhara Slain by Śiva** — Jalandhara, born of Śiva's third-eye fire and shielded by his wife Vṛndā's chastity, is undone when Viṣṇu deceives Vṛndā in his form, and Śiva slays him with a toe-carved cakra; Vṛndā self-immolates and becomes the Tulsī plant _(actors: Jalandhara, Śiva, Viṣṇu, Vṛndā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Mohini distributes the amrita** — Vishnu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini, beguiles the Asuras who had seized the nectar pot, and distributes the amrita only to the Devas _(actors: Mohini/Vishnu, Devas, Asuras, Dhanvantari)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8-8.9)
- **Beheading of Svarbhanu (origin of Rahu and Ketu)** — The Asura Svarbhanu disguises himself among the Devas to drink amrita; exposed by Surya and Candra, he is beheaded by the Sudarshana chakra, his immortal head and body becoming Rahu and Ketu who cause eclipses out of grudge _(actors: Svarbhanu/Rahu/Ketu, Surya, Candra, Mohini/Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Hiranyakasipu's boon of near-invincibility** — Hiranyakasipu obtains a boon of near-invincibility (not by man or beast, day or night, indoors or out), the second life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse _(actors: Hiranyakasipu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Mahalakshmi born at the Samudra Manthana** — The supreme Lakshmi, consort of Vishnu, is born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk _(actors: Mahalakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Sri Sukta)
- **Narasimha avatara slays Hiranyakashipu** — Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha and kills Hiranyakashipu at twilight on the threshold upon his lap with claws, voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Vishnu (Narasimha), Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Sudarśana severs Rāhu at the churning** — Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra severs the asura Rāhu's head at the Samudra Manthana after he steals a sip of amṛta _(actors: Viṣṇu, Rāhu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia))
- **The Matsya and Manu flood narrative** — Manu rears a tiny fish that grows into the giant Matsya, who tows his boat to safety through the deluge _(actors: Manu, Matsya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 185)
- **Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthana)** — Viśvāmitra tells the Bāla-Kāṇḍa version of devas and asuras churning the Milk-Ocean with Mandara and Vāsuki, yielding the Hālāhala poison, Dhanvantari, apsarases, and Amṛta _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Śiva, Vāsuki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 45)
- **Narasimha disembowels Hiranyakasipu** — The Man-Lion avatara bursts from a pillar at twilight to disembowel Hiranyakasipu, threading every clause of the boon, and saves Prahlada _(actors: Narasimha/Viṣṇu, Hiranyakasipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Prahlada enthroned as righteous Asura king** — Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers; Prahlada is enthroned as a virtuous Asura king and becomes ancestor of Bali _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Bali)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **War over the nectar and Indra's reinstatement** — Devas and Asuras battle over the nectar; with strength restored the Devas prevail and Indra is reinstated as king of the gods _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11)
- **Dhruva becomes the Pole Star** — Rebuffed by his stepmother, the boy Dhruva performs intense tapas guided by Narada; Vishnu appears and fixes him as the immovable Dhruva Nakshatra around which the Saptarshi revolve _(actors: Dhruva, Uttanapada, Suniti, Suruci, Narada, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.11-1.12; Bhagavata Purana 4.8-4.12 (canonically Svayambhuva Manvantara))
- **Varaha lifts the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — When the Asura Hiranyaksha drags Earth (Bhumi) to the bottom of the cosmic ocean, Vishnu becomes the colossal boar Varaha, slays Hiranyaksha in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth back on his tusks _(actors: Varaha/Vishnu, Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Daksha Yajna and Sati's self-immolation** — Prajapati Daksha snubs his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva at a grand yajna; the insulted Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Kalidasa Kumarasambhava)
- **Hiranyakashipu's boon of near-invulnerability** — Enraged at his brother's death, Hiranyakashipu performs extreme tapas and wins from Brahma a boon that he cannot be slain by man or beast, day or night, indoors or outdoors, on earth or sky, by any weapon, then tyrannizes the three worlds _(actors: Hiranyakashipu, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.3-7.4; Harivamsha)
- **Nimi and Vasishtha's Mutual Curse** — Nimi and his purohita Vasishtha curse each other to bodilessness over a sacrifice dispute; from Nimi's churned body is born Janaka, founding the Videha/Mithila line _(actors: Nimi, Vasishtha, Janaka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.5; Bhagavata IX.13)
- **Samudra-manthana (churning of the milk-ocean)** — Devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean with the Kurma avatara as pivot, producing amṛta, Dhanvantari, and Lakṣmi _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Kurma/Viṣṇu, Dhanvantari, Lakṣmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Manu and the Flood (Matsya Avatara)** — The fish-avatara (Matsya) saves Manu from the cosmic deluge in the earliest extant Hindu flood narrative recorded in the Shatapatha Brahmana _(actors: Manu, Matsya/Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/yajurveda.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1)
- **Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar** — The Mohini avatara enchants the asuras and distributes the amṛta to the devas, denying the demons immortality _(actors: Mohini/Viṣṇu, Asuras, Devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Prahlada's devotion and survival** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-devotion by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives his father's repeated murder attempts by poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Virabhadra's rampage and beheading of Daksha** — Enraged Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of hair; they destroy the yajna and behead Daksha, who is later revived with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas and Sati's rebirth as Parvati** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse, which Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts into pieces that fall across the land founding the 51 Shakti Pithas; Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati/Parvati, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Holika burned (origin of Holi)** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but herself perishes while he survives — the origin myth of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk tradition)
- **Narasimha Bursts from the Pillar to Slay Hiranyakashipu** — In defense of the boy-devotee Prahlada, the man-lion Narasimha bursts from a pillar at dusk and slays the demon-king Hiranyakashipu _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1-10)
- **Ikshvaku founds the Solar dynasty** — Vaivasvata Manu's eldest son Ikshvaku, granted Aryavarta/Kosala, becomes progenitor of the Suryavamsha, the line of Mandhata, Sagara, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Rama _(actors: Ikshvaku, Vaivasvata Manu, Nimi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.2-4.4; Harivamsha)
- **Matsya saves Satyavrata and the Vedas from the flood** — The Fish avatara saves Satyavrata (Manu), the seeds of life, and the Vedas from the dissolution-flood, the manvantara-transition par excellence _(actors: Matsya/Viṣṇu, Satyavrata/Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu** — When challenged whether Vishnu is in a pillar, Hiranyakashipu smashes it and Vishnu bursts out as the man-lion Narasimha, seizing the Asura at twilight on the threshold upon his lap and disemboweling him with claws — voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Narasimha/Vishnu, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Pururavas and Urvashi** — The first mortal king of the Lunar line loves the apsara Urvashi under conditions, loses her when they break, and is eventually reunited _(actors: Pururavas, Urvashi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Rigveda X.95; Shatapatha Brahmana XI; Vishnu Purana)
- **Dhanvantari Emerges at the Churning Bearing Amrita** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana carrying the pot of amrita, linking the churning of the ocean to the origin of Ayurveda _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas, asuras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Ila/Sudyumna and the founding of the Lunar dynasty** — From Vaivasvata Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna springs the Lunar dynasty (Chandravamsha) via Budha _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ila/Sudyumna, Budha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Prahlada enthroned as Asura king** — After Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers, Prahlada is enthroned as a righteous Asura king and ancestor of Bali _(actors: Prahlada, Narasimha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **Kapila burns the 60,000 sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates King Sagara's 60,000 sons for accusing him of stealing the ashvamedha horse, the curse later driving Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, Sagara's sons, Bhagiratha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Kapila burns the sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates the 60,000 sons of King Sagara for accusing him of stealing the sacrificial horse — the curse that later drives Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, the 60,000 sons of Sagara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Markandeya granted a short brilliant life** — The childless sage Mrkandu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son fated to die at sixteen; the radiant boy Markandeya is born and masters the Vedas _(actors: Mrkandu, Marudvati/Manasvini, Markandeya, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Matsya Rescues Manu and the Vedas** — The fish-avatara Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge at the pralaya _(actors: Matsya, Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Descent of Ganga (Gangavatarana)** — Ganga is brought to earth by Bhagiratha's austerities, her fall broken by Shiva's matted hair, to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons _(actors: Ganga, Bhagiratha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Bhagavata; Mahabharata)
