- **Birth of Karna in armor** — Karna is born already wearing a golden kavacha and kundala fused to his skin, dipped in amrita, making him invulnerable while he keeps them _(actors: Karna, Surya, Kunti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva ~308; Adi Parva)
- **Birth of Karna to Kunti and Surya** — Using Durvasa's mantra Kunti summons Surya and bears Karna armored with kavacha-kundala, then sets the infant adrift on the river _(actors: Kunti, Surya, Karna, Adhiratha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Adi/Vana Parva)
- **Birth of Krishna** — Krishna is born at midnight on Janmashtami as the dark-hued eighth child, displaying his four-armed Vishnu form before assuming infant shape _(actors: Krishna, Devaki, Vasudeva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.3)
- **Birth of Krishna and the substituted goddess** — Balarāma's embryo is moved to Rohiṇī and Krishna is born and carried across the Yamunā to Nanda and Yaśodā, swapped for the infant goddess Ekānaṃśā/Nidrā who escapes Kaṃsa's hand and prophesies his doom _(actors: Krishna, Vasudeva, Nanda, Yaśodā, Ekānaṃśā, Kaṃsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Composition of the Mahabharata** — Vyasa authors the 100,000-verse Mahabharata, dictated to Ganesha as scribe on the condition that Vyasa never pause and Ganesha never write without understanding _(actors: Vyasa, Ganesha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 1)
- **Damayantī's svayaṃvara and the five identical Nalas** — At the svayaṃvara the four Lokapālas mimic Nala's form; Damayantī picks the true Nala by divine signs and the gods grant him boons _(actors: Damayantī, Nala, Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 53–56)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Krishna** — Vishnu descends as Krishna at the close of the Dvapara Yuga of this 28th Mahayuga, the defining reason this cycle matters above all others _(actors: Vishnu; Krishna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1; Mahabharata)
- **Dhanvantari reborn as king of Kashi** — A later Dhanvantari is reborn into the royal house of Kashi (identified with Divodasa), where he systematizes and publicly teaches the Ayurvedic system _(actors: Dhanvantari, Divodasa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Brahmanda Purana; Sushruta Samhita)
- **Duryodhana hides in Lake Dvaipayana** — With his army destroyed, Duryodhana flees and by yogic power solidifies the waters of Lake Dvaipayana, lying hidden beneath the surface to regather strength _(actors: Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva (Hrada-pravesha))
- **Dushyanta meets Shakuntala at Kanva's ashrama** — King Dushyanta, hunting from Hastinapura, enters Kanva's hermitage in the sage's absence, is received and smitten by Shakuntala, and the two fall in mutual love _(actors: Dushyanta, Shakuntala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Duṣyanta & Śakuntalā Wed by Gandharva Rite** — Duṣyanta and Śakuntalā marry by gandharva vivāha (mutual consent without ritual) in Kaṇva's forest hermitage — the locus classicus of the love-match marriage _(actors: Duṣyanta, Śakuntalā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/gandharvas-and-kinnaras.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Abhijñānaśākuntalam)
- **Ekalavya seals the dog's mouth with arrows** — On a hunt Ekalavya fires seven arrows by sound alone (śabda-vedha) into a barking dog's open mouth, sealing it without drawing blood, astonishing the Kuru princes _(actors: Ekalavya, Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Gandhari's panoramic lament over the slain** — By her divine eye Gandhari surveys all of Kurukshetra and describes the carnage corpse by corpse to Krishna, naming Duryodhana, Abhimanyu, Karna, Drona, Jayadratha and the slaughtered warrior aristocracy _(actors: Gandhari, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/11-stri-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Stri Parva 16-25 (Stri-vilapa))
- **Gods reveal themselves and boon Shibi a son** — Indra and Agni resume true form, heal Shibi, and promise him a glorious son Kapotaroma, proving dharma upheld without limit overrides death _(actors: Indra, Agni, Shibi, Kapotaroma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shibi.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva)
- **Irāvān's cavalry exploits at Kurukṣetra** — Mounted, Irāvān routs the cavalry of Śakuni's Gāndhāra brothers, slaying several in the early days of the war _(actors: Irāvān, Śakuni's brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Mahābhārata Bhīṣma Parva)
- **Kama reborn as Pradyumna and slays Sambara** — Kama is reborn as Pradyumna, son of Krishna and Rukmini; stolen by Sambara and raised by Mayavati (Rati), the grown Pradyumna slays Sambara and weds her _(actors: Pradyumna/Kama, Krishna, Rukmini, Sambara, Mayavati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.55; Vishnu Purana 5.27)
- **Kṛṣṇa revives the stillborn Parikṣit** — Parikṣit, struck in Uttarā's womb by Aśvatthāman's Brahmāstra and born seemingly dead, is restored to life by Kṛṣṇa's act of truth, securing the continuity of the Kuru line _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Parikṣit, Uttarā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.65-69)
- **Karkoṭaka Bites and Disguises Nala** — The black nāga Karkoṭaka bites and disfigures King Nala in a benign bite that hides him from Kali's persecution and later lets him resume his form _(actors: Karkoṭaka, Nala)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Nala-Damayantī episode)
- **Kaṃsa Deposes and Imprisons Ugrasena** — Kaṃsa deposes and imprisons his father Ugrasena, king of Mathurā, ruling as a despot allied to Jarāsandha of Magadha _(actors: Kaṃsa, Ugrasena, Jarāsandha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10)
- **Krishna absorbs the Vaishnavastra; Arjuna slays Bhagadatta** — Bhagadatta of Pragjyotisha hurls the Vaishnavastra, which Krishna absorbs onto his chest as the Vaijayanti garland; Arjuna then slays Bhagadatta on his elephant Supratika _(actors: Bhagadatta, Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 25-29)
- **Krishna delivers the Uddhava Gita** — At the eve of Kali Yuga Krishna gives Uddhava his final systematic teaching (the Uddhava/Hamsa Gita) synthesizing bhakti, jnana, yoga and Samkhya before departing _(actors: Krishna, Uddhava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.6.40-11.29)
- **Krishna's Departure and Onset of Kali** — Krishna passes away and the Yadava line ends, after which Kali personified enters the world, marking the turn into the Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Kali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.15)
- **Krishna's lap fulfils the sign** — When Shrutashrava places the child on Krishna's lap the third eye and extra arms drop away, revealing Krishna as the appointed killer _(actors: Krishna, Shrutashrava, Shishupala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha-parva 40)
- **Krishna Slays Shankhasura at Bet Dvaraka** — At Shankhoddhara (Bet Dvaraka) Krishna slays the conch-demon Shankhasura and recovers the Vedas, the myth tied to his Panchajanya conch _(actors: Krishna, Shankhasura)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (sthala-purana; Wikipedia)
- **Kuntī invokes Sūrya and bears Karṇa** — Testing the mantra, Kuntī summons Sūrya, who is compelled to beget Karṇa upon her, born with natural golden armor and earrings, while restoring her virginity _(actors: Kuntī, Sūrya, Karṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi/Vana Parva)
- **Kuntī invokes Vāyu and conceives Bhīma** — Using Durvāsā's mantra, Queen Kuntī invokes Vāyu and conceives Bhīma, strongest of the Pāṇḍavas, Vāyu's might made mortal _(actors: Kuntī, Vāyu, Bhīma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Samba cured by worshipping Surya** — The leprous Samba, son of Krishna, is cured by worshipping Surya, founding solar worship at Mitravana/Multan _(actors: Samba, Surya, Krishna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Samba Purana; Bhavishya Purana)
- **Shalya tricked to the Kaurava side** — The Madra king Shalya, intercepted by Duryodhana's hospitality, is bound by gratitude to fight for the Kauravas but secretly promises Yudhishthira to dishearten Karna as charioteer _(actors: Shalya, Duryodhana, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Sainyodyoga)
- **Slaying of Jarasandha by Bhima** — Disguised as brahmanas, the three reach Magadha; Krishna's leaf-splitting hint lets Bhima tear Jarasandha in two and fling the halves apart, freeing the captive kings _(actors: Krishna, Bhima, Arjuna, Jarasandha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 20-24)
- **The agra-pūjā to Kṛṣṇa and beheading of Śiśupāla** — Yudhiṣṭhira awards the first-worship of the Rājasūya to Kṛṣṇa; when Śiśupāla protests and exhausts his hundred allotted offenses, Kṛṣṇa beheads him with his discus _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Kṛṣṇa, Śiśupāla)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā Parva)
- **The double rejection of Ambā** — Śālva spurns Ambā as won by another; Vicitravīrya and the vow-bound Bhīṣma also refuse her, leaving her abandoned and fixing blame on Bhīṣma _(actors: Ambā, Śālva, Vicitravīrya, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~174–178)
- **The faithful housewife humbles Kauśika** — A devoted wife tending her husband tells the impatient Kauśika she is no crane to be burnt, that household duty done in love is itself the path, and sends him to the butcher of Mithilā _(actors: Kauśika, the pativratā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyadha-gita.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~198)
- **The Golden Swan Carries Nala's Suit** — A captured golden swan, released by Nala, flies to Vidarbha and extols him to Damayantī, kindling her longing _(actors: Nala, Damayantī, the haṃsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 51-52)
- **The iron club ground to powder and the eraka grass born** — Samba produces the cursed iron club; on Ugrasena's order it is ground to powder and cast into the sea, but one unground lump is swallowed by a fish (whose splinter the hunter Jara takes as an arrowhead) and the filings wash ashore to grow into the sharp eraka reed _(actors: Samba, Ugrasena, Jara, a fish)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.1; Vishnu Purana 5.37)
- **The Pandavas take disguises at Virata's court** — The five brothers and Draupadi assume hidden identities (Kanka, Vallabha, Brihannala, Granthika, Tantipala, Sairandhri) and enter service at Virata's court, Arjuna's eunuch disguise fulfilling Urvashi's curse _(actors: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 1-12)
- **The Yakṣa-praśna (riddles of dharma)** — Yudhiṣṭhira chooses to answer rather than drink, and the disguised guardian poses a rapid catechism of dharma — the mother heavier than earth, the greatest wonder being men's denial of death, conduct over birth _(actors: the Yakṣa, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yaksha-prashna.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 312-313)
- **Urvashī curses Arjuna to be a eunuch** — When Arjuna refuses her advances, Urvashī curses him to spend a year as the eunuch Bṛhannala _(actors: Urvashī, Arjuna)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Uttanka and King Paushya trade and retract curses** — Over a perceived insult Uttanka curses King Paushya to blindness and Paushya curses Uttanka to childlessness, then both retract _(actors: Uttanka, Paushya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Paushya Parva)
- **Vidura's coded warning of the lac-house** — As the Pāṇḍavas depart for Vāraṇāvata, Vidura warns Yudhiṣṭhira in coded Mleccha speech of the planned arson and arranges a miner's tunnel and a boat for their escape _(actors: Vidura, Yudhiṣṭhira, Purocana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Jatugṛha-parva)
- **Vow to fight for the losing side** — Barbarīka vows to his mother to always fight for whichever side is losing, then rides toward Kurukṣetra to join the war _(actors: Barbarīka, his mother)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Folk Mahābhārata traditions)
- **Vyāsa, Devala and Nārada console Yudhiṣṭhira** — The sages console the grieving king, with Vyāsa arguing the slain went to heaven by kṣatriya-dharma and that expiation, not flight, is the king's path _(actors: Vyāsa, Devala, Nārada, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.23-36)
- **Yājñavalkya Teaches Janaka the Tattvas** — Yājñavalkya expounds the Sāṃkhya enumeration of 24 tattvas, the 25th puruṣa, and the supreme 26th Īśvara to King Janaka _(actors: Yājñavalkya, Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 310-311)
- **Abandonment of the infant Karṇa on the river** — To hide her disgrace, Kuntī sets the armored infant Karṇa adrift in a basket; he is found and raised by the charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Rādhā _(actors: Kuntī, Karṇa, Adhiratha, Rādhā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Abhimanyu breaks into the cakra-vyuha** — Day 13: Drona forms the spinning cakra-vyuha; Abhimanyu, knowing only how to enter, breaks in while Jayadratha (by Shiva's boon) seals the gap behind him, trapping the boy alone _(actors: Abhimanyu, Drona, Jayadratha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 33-41)
- **Arjuna wins the Pashupatastra from Shiva** — Performing fierce tapas, Arjuna duels Shiva disguised as a Kirata over a slain boar and is granted the supreme Pashupata weapon _(actors: Arjuna, Shiva, Muka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 38-41)
- **Balarama returns from his Saraswati pilgrimage** — Having stayed neutral on a tirtha-yatra along the Saraswati for the war's duration, Balarama returns to Kurukshetra exactly in time to preside as referee over his two pupils' mace-duel _(actors: Balarama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva (Saraswata/Gada-yuddha))
- **Bhima Carries the Pandavas from the Lacquer-House** — When the Kauravas set the flammable house at Varanavata ablaze, Bhima carries Kunti and his four brothers out through the escape tunnel _(actors: Bhima, Kunti, the Pandavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~145-147)
- **Bhishma's vow** — King Shantanu weds Ganga who bears Devavrata (Bhishma); to enable Shantanu's marriage to Satyavati, Bhishma takes the vow of lifelong celibacy and renounces the throne, earning the boon of death-at-will _(actors: Shantanu, Ganga, Bhishma, Satyavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Birth of Kṛṣṇa at Mathurā** — Krishna is born in the prison of his uncle Kamsa at Mathura on the Yamuna in the Dvapara Yuga, later slaying Kamsa _(actors: Krishna, Kamsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Bhagavata Purana 10; Vishnu Purana)
- **Chitrasena Captures Duryodhana** — The gandharva Chitrasena, who taught Arjuna music in Amarāvatī, defeats and captures Duryodhana at the Ghoṣa-yātrā, only for the Pāṇḍavas to rescue him _(actors: Chitrasena, Duryodhana, Arjuna, Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/gandharvas-and-kinnaras.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Ghoṣa-yātrā Parva)
- **Death of Irāvān by Alambuṣa** — The rākṣasa Alambuṣa beheads Irāvān through illusion-war; his fall (placed on the first or eighth day) grieves Arjuna _(actors: Irāvān, Alambuṣa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Mahābhārata Bhīṣma Parva)
- **Dhanvantari teaches Sushruta surgery** — Sages led by Sushruta approach the Kashi king-physician to learn medicine, and he teaches them Shalya-tantra (surgery), transmitted as the Sushruta Samhita _(actors: Dhanvantari, Sushruta)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Sushruta Samhita Sutrasthana 1)
- **Division of the one Veda into four and the four disciples** — Vyāsa splits the single Veda into Ṛg, Yajur, Sāman and Atharva and entrusts each to Paila, Vaiśampāyana, Jaimini and Sumantu, with the itihāsa-purāṇa to Romaharṣaṇa _(actors: Vyāsa, Paila, Vaiśampāyana, Jaimini, Sumantu, Romaharṣaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Ekalavya surrenders his thumb as guru-dakṣiṇā** — When Arjuna protests being outclassed, Droṇa demands Ekalavya's right thumb as his teaching-fee, and Ekalavya without hesitation severs his thumb, permanently crippling his archery and preserving Arjuna's primacy _(actors: Ekalavya, Droṇa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Gandhari's curse on Krishna** — Charging Krishna with allowing the slaughter, Gandhari curses that in the thirty-sixth year his Yadava kin will destroy one another as the Kurus did and that he will die alone in the wilderness; Krishna accepts it as his own will _(actors: Gandhari, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/11-stri-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Stri Parva 25)
- **Ganesha Gita spoken to King Varenya** — As Gajanana, Ganesha reveals the Ganesha Gita to King Varenya, teaching karma-, jnana-, and bhakti-yoga in a Ganesha-fied Bhagavad Gita _(actors: Gajanana (Ganesha), King Varenya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda ch. 138-148))
- **Kṛṣṇa delivers the Anugītā to Arjuna** — Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the Gītā's wisdom; unable to repeat it verbatim, Kṛṣṇa relays an old conversation of the same import (the Anugītā) on transmigration, karma, the guṇas, and mokṣa _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.16-51)
- **Kali vows to destroy Nala and possesses him** — The age-demon Kali, enraged Nala won the bride, waits twelve years for a ritual lapse then enters Nala; Dvāpara possesses the dice _(actors: Kali, Dvāpara, Nala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 56)
- **Karna cast on the river** — Fearing disgrace, Kunti seals the infant in a basket and floats him down the rivers to the Ganga _(actors: Kunti, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva ~308)
- **Karna defeats but spares the lesser Pandavas** — Karna overpowers Nakula, Sahadeva and Yudhishthira but spares each, honoring his promise to Kunti to kill none of her sons but Arjuna _(actors: Karna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva 21-49)
- **Kṛṣṇa's leaf-test** — Disguised as a brāhmaṇa, Kṛṣṇa tests Barbarīka; the marking arrow pierces every leaf of a Pīpala tree and hovers over Kṛṣṇa's foot where a leaf is hidden _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Barbarīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Folk Mahābhārata; Khāṭū Śyām sthala-tradition)
- **Kicaka's harassment of Sairandhri** — Kicaka, the queen's brother and army-commander, becomes inflamed with lust for Sairandhri (Draupadi), assaults her, and humiliates her by kicking and dragging her in the assembly hall _(actors: Kicaka, Draupadi, Sudeshna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 14-16)
- **Krishna, Balarama and Sudama Study at Sandipani's Gurukula** — Krishna, Balarama and the poor brahmin Sudama study the Vedas, 64 arts and weaponry at Rshi Sandipani's gurukula in Ujjain, where the Krishna-Sudama friendship begins _(actors: Krishna, Balarama, Sudama, Sandipani)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ujjain-avantika.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X)
- **Krishna's boon to forgive a hundred offenses** — At Shrutashrava's plea Krishna vows to pardon a full hundred offenses of Shishupala before exacting any penalty _(actors: Krishna, Shrutashrava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha-parva 40)
- **Krishna's Vṛndāvana demon-slayings** — Growing among the cowherds, Krishna and Balarāma slay the pastoral demons Pūtanā, Śakaṭa, the twin Arjuna trees, Kāliya, Dhenuka, Pralamba, Ariṣṭa, and Keśin in early form _(actors: Krishna, Balarāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Mahabharata War and Krishna's Departure** — The Mahabharata war is fought near the Dvapara-Kali junction; Krishna's departure (3102 BCE) marks Kali Yuga fully entering, the traditional onset of the present age _(actors: Krishna; Pandavas; Kauravas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.15; Mahabharata; Surya Siddhanta epoch)
- **Nahuṣa freed by Yudhiṣṭhira's riddles** — Ages later the python Nahuṣa seizes Bhīma; Yudhiṣṭhira answers his dharma-riddles, freeing both Bhīma and the cursed king, who ascends to heaven _(actors: Nahuṣa, Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 176-181)
- **Omens at Dwarka and the divine weapons depart** — Portents multiply at Dwarka as the 36th year comes; Krishna's Sudarshana Chakra, conch Panchajanya, chariot and horses, and Balarama's plough rise and vanish, the instruments of the avatar leaving first, and Krishna orders the fatal pilgrimage to Prabhasa _(actors: Krishna, Balarama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.2)
- **Pañcaśikha Instructs Janaka** — Pañcaśikha teaches Janaka an austere atheistic Sāṃkhya of guṇas and discriminative knowledge, witnessing the Kapila-Āsuri-Pañcaśikha lineage _(actors: Pañcaśikha, Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 211-212, 218-219)
- **Paraśurāma's duel with Bhīṣma** — Ambā appeals to Bhīṣma's guru Paraśurāma, who fights Bhīṣma in a multi-day stalemate at Kurukṣetra ended by the gods' and Nārada's intervention _(actors: Ambā, Paraśurāma, Bhīṣma, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~178–186)
- **Sanjaya's peace-embassy fails** — Dhritarashtra sends Sanjaya with a message offering no land; Yudhishthira and Krishna expose its emptiness, refusing to surrender their birthright _(actors: Sanjaya, Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Sanjaya-yana)
- **Sudama's Reunion with Krishna at Bet Dvaraka** — The poor brahmin Sudama's pinch of beaten rice is repaid with untold wealth at Bet Dvaraka, a key bhakti parable of Krishna's love for the lowly _(actors: Sudama, Krishna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Bhagavata 10.80-81)
- **Takshaka steals the earrings** — Takshaka, disguised as a naked mendicant, snatches the earrings Uttanka has set down and dives into a hole leading to Nagaloka _(actors: Takshaka, Uttanka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Paushya Parva)
- **The avadhuta's teaching of the 24 gurus** — Within the Uddhava Gita Krishna retells how a wandering avadhuta-brahmana, questioned by King Yadu, named 24 natural gurus as the source of his serene bliss _(actors: Krishna, Uddhava, avadhuta, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.7-9)
- **The Aśvamedha prescribed as expiation** — To purge the sin of the war, Yudhiṣṭhira is told he must rule and later perform the horse-sacrifice as prāyaścitta _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.36-37)
- **The Bhagavad Gita spoken** — Krishna delivers his 700-verse teaching resolving Arjuna's paralysis through the imperishable atman, nishkama-karma, and the yogas of knowledge, action and devotion, climaxing in the Vishvarupa-darshana _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/06-bhishma-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Bhishma Parva 25-42 (Bhagavad Gita))
- **The Dharma-vyādha teaches Kauśika** — The righteous butcher of Mithilā delivers the Vyādha-gītā — that no duty is impure, svadharma done without malice does not defile, ahiṃsā is intention, and service to parents is the highest dharma _(actors: Dharma-vyādha, Kauśika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyadha-gita.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~198-206)
- **The Digvijaya: conquest of the four quarters** — The four younger Pandavas subdue the four directions, bringing back vast tribute that ignites Duryodhana's envy _(actors: Arjuna, Bhima, Sahadeva, Nakula)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 25-31)
- **The Four Gods Make Nala Their Messenger** — En route to the svayaṃvara the four Lokapālas compel the truthful Nala to plead their suit to the very woman he loves _(actors: Nala, Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, Yama, Damayantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 53-54)
- **The gandharva marriage with the heir-condition** — Dushyanta argues gandharva marriage lawful and weds Shakuntala on her binding condition that her son shall be heir-apparent; he departs giving no token, and Kanva blesses the union on his return _(actors: Dushyanta, Shakuntala, Kanva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **The Kashi Abduction of Amba, Ambika, Ambalika** — Bhishma storms the Kashi svayamvara and carries off the three princesses by force as brides for Vicitravirya, defeating the assembled kings and Shalva _(actors: Bhishma, Amba, Ambika, Ambalika, Shalva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhishma.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~102)
- **The meeting of Hanumān and Bhīma** — Seeking the saugandhika flower, Bhīma cannot lift an old monkey's tail blocking his path; the monkey reveals himself as Hanumān, his elder half-brother, and blesses him _(actors: Bhīma, Hanumān)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **The night massacre of the sleeping camp** — Ashvatthaman strangles Dhrishtadyumna, slays the five sons of Draupadi, cuts Shikhandin in two, and butchers the Panchala chiefs and host as they sleep while Kripa and Kritavarman fire the camp gates _(actors: Ashvatthaman, Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin, Upapandavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva 8)
- **The Vasus Steal Nandinī; Vasiṣṭha's Curse** — The eight Vasus steal Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Nandinī, and the enraged sage curses them to be born as mortals, with the instigator Dyaus condemned to a long mortal life _(actors: Vasus, Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha, Dyaus)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Sambhava Parva)
- **Transfer of Balarāma to Rohiṇī's Womb** — The seventh embryo Śeṣa/Balarāma is mystically transferred by Yoga-māyā from Devakī's womb to Rohiṇī at Gokula, giving Balarāma the epithet Saṃkarṣaṇa _(actors: Balarāma, Devakī, Rohiṇī, Yoga-māyā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.2)
- **Uttaṅka beholds Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa and the Uttaṅka-megha boon** — In the Āśvamedhika doublet Uttaṅka would curse Kṛṣṇa for the war, is shown the Universal Form, fails the Caṇḍāla-amṛta test, and is granted desert rain-clouds _(actors: Uttaṅka, Kṛṣṇa, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahābhārata Āśvamedhika Parva 14.52–58)
- **Vasudeva carries Krishna across the Yamuna** — Vasudeva bears the newborn across the flooding Yamuna to Gokula, swapping him for Yashoda's just-born daughter Yogamaya _(actors: Vasudeva, Krishna, Nanda, Yashoda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.3)
- **Vidura delivers the Vidura-nīti** — Over eight chapters Vidura, incarnation of Dharma, pours out aphoristic counsel on the wise and the fool, kingship, truth and forgiveness, urging restraint of Duryodhana _(actors: Vidura, Dhṛtarāṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vidura-niti.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva 33-40)
- **Vidura protests Draupadī's outrage at the dice-game** — At the rigged dice-game Vidura alone rises to denounce the assembly and the king as Draupadī is dragged in and disrobed, warning that adharma will consume the house _(actors: Vidura, Draupadī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Duḥśāsana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā Parva)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira chooses Nakula** — Offered one brother's life, Yudhiṣṭhira passes over Bhīma and Arjuna and asks for Nakula so that both his father's wives have a living son, prizing impartiality _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, the Yakṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yaksha-prashna.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 314)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira's fall at the dice-game** — Lured into a rigged dice-game played by the cheating Śakuni, Yudhiṣṭhira loses wealth, kingdom, his brothers, himself, and finally Draupadī, triggering the disrobing _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Śakuni, Duryodhana, Draupadī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā Parva)
- **Abhimanyu slain by six warriors** — Inside the formation Abhimanyu kills thousands and slays Duryodhana's son Lakshmana, but is ganged upon by six maharathis and finally clubbed to death by Duhshasana's son, an open breach of the war-code _(actors: Abhimanyu, Drona, Karna, Duhshasana's son)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 47-48)
- **Ambā's tapas, Śiva's boon, and self-immolation** — Out of human remedies, Ambā performs fierce austerities; Śiva grants she will cause Bhīṣma's death and remember her past life, and she immolates herself to hasten rebirth _(actors: Ambā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~187–188)
- **Arjuna nearly kills Yudhishthira; Krishna intervenes** — When the wounded Yudhishthira reviles Arjuna and insults the Gandiva, Arjuna draws his sword to honor a vow to kill any who insults it; Krishna resolves the dilemma through casuistry without bloodshed _(actors: Arjuna, Yudhishthira, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva 68-69)
- **Ashwatthama's night slaughter of the Pandava camp** — Born as a Rudra-portion to Drona, the immortal cursed warrior Ashwatthama slaughters the Pandava camp by night _(actors: Ashwatthama (Rudra-amsha), the Pandavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Mahabharata)
- **Bhima Slays Hidimba and Weds Hidimba** — Bhima kills the cannibal rakshasa Hidimba in a wrestling match and weds his sister Hidimba, fathering Ghatotkaca _(actors: Bhima, Hidimba, Hidimba, Ghatotkaca)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~154-155)
- **Bhima slays Kicaka** — Lured to a night tryst in the dance-hall where Bhima lies in Sairandhri's place, Kicaka is seized and crushed into a shapeless ball of flesh, avenging Draupadi's humiliation _(actors: Bhima, Kicaka, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 21-22)
- **Birth and boyhood of Sarvadamana (Bharata)** — Shakuntala bears a son of extraordinary power, Sarvadamana, raised in the hermitage, so strong he ties up lion and tiger cubs in play _(actors: Shakuntala, Sarvadamana/Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Birth of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura** — After Satyavati's sons die heirless, Vyasa fathers by niyoga the blind Dhritarashtra, the pale Pandu, and the wise Vidura (an incarnation of Dharma) on the widowed queens and a maid _(actors: Vyasa, Ambika, Ambalika, Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Birth of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura** — By niyoga, Vyasa fathers the blind Dhritarashtra, pale Pandu, and wise Vidura on the Kuru queens _(actors: Vyasa, Ambika, Ambalika, Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Birth of Kṛṣṇa in Kaṃsa's Prison** — Kṛṣṇa is born at midnight on Janmāṣṭamī in the prison cell as Devakī and Vasudeva's eighth child; the chains fall and the guards sleep _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Devakī, Vasudeva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.3-4)
- **Composition of the Mahābhārata, dictated to Gaṇeśa** — Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata; Gaṇeśa scribes on condition of unbroken dictation, Vyāsa seeds knotted kūṭa-ślokas, and Gaṇeśa breaks his tusk to write _(actors: Vyāsa, Brahmā, Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (longer recensions; disputed/interpolated))
- **Damayantī Chooses Nala at the Svayaṃvara** — Confronted with five identical Nalas, Damayantī recognizes the true mortal by his shadow, sweat and dusty feet and garlands him _(actors: Damayantī, Nala, the four gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 54)
- **Day 1 — Bhishma slays Shveta; Shalya slays Uttara** — On the first day Bhishma kills Shveta son of Virata with a celestial weapon and Shalya kills prince Uttara, two of Virata's sons falling in a single day _(actors: Bhishma, Shveta, Shalya, Uttara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/06-bhishma-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Bhishma Parva 45)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra rejects the counsel** — The blind king concedes Vidura's wisdom is just yet cannot break his love for Duryodhana and resigns to fate, the epic's tragedy in miniature _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vidura-niti.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva 40)
- **Draupadi's vow of vengeance for the gem** — Learning all her sons and kin are dead, Draupadi vows to fast to death unless Ashvatthaman is killed and the invulnerability-gem on his forehead is brought to her; Bhima races ahead in pursuit _(actors: Draupadi, Bhima, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva 11)
- **Durvasa's Curse Separating Rukmini** — Sage Durvasa, yoked to Rukmini's chariot by Krishna and Rukmini, curses that she will thirst and dwell apart, explaining her temple's location outside Dvaraka town _(actors: Durvasa, Rukmini, Krishna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (local sthala-purana)
- **Ekalavya allies with Jarāsandha against the Yādavas** — As king of the Niṣādas, Ekalavya fights alongside Jarāsandha of Magadha in his invasions of Mathurā, hurling himself against the Yādavas _(actors: Ekalavya, Jarāsandha, Hiraṇyadhanus)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Harivaṃśa; Mahābhārata Sabhā Parva)
- **Gaṅgā Bears the Vasus; Birth of Bhīṣma** — To discharge Vasiṣṭha's curse, Gaṅgā bears the eight Vasus by King Śāntanu, drowning seven at birth to free them; the eighth, Dyaus, survives as Devavrata-Bhīṣma _(actors: Gaṅgā, Śāntanu, Vasus, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Ganesha scribes the Mahabharata and breaks his tusk** — Ganesha agrees to write Vyasa's Mahabharata; when his pen breaks mid-dictation he snaps off his own tusk to keep writing, becoming Ekadanta _(actors: Ganesha, Vyasa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Jayadratha Seals the Breach** — Jayadratha, using a boon from Shiva, holds the entry-point and turns back the other Pandavas, stranding Abhimanyu alone inside the formation _(actors: Jayadratha, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata, Drona Parva)
- **Kṛṣṇa lodges with Vidura during the embassy** — Arriving as peace-envoy, Kṛṣṇa declines Duryodhana's lavish feast and stays at the humble home of the righteous Vidura _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva)
- **Kṛṣṇa restores Bhīṣma's faculties for the teaching** — Kṛṣṇa grants the dying Bhīṣma freedom from pain and clarity of mind for the duration of his instruction, and Bhīṣma sings a hymn to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.47, 52-54)
- **Kṛṣṇa reveals the Viśvarūpa to Arjuna** — Kṛṣṇa reveals his cosmic all-form (Viśvarūpa) to Arjuna on the battlefield, an infinite theophany of all worlds and time devouring the armies _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhagavad Gītā 11; Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva; Bhāgavata 10.7)
- **Karna found and raised by the suta couple** — The childless charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Radha recover the basket at Campa and raise Karna as their own, branding him Sutaputra _(actors: Adhiratha, Radha, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva ~308; Adi Parva)
- **King Pāṇḍu's Penance and the Birth of the Pandavas at Pandukeshwar** — King Pandu does penance at Yogadhyan Badri to be cleansed of killing two mating deer; the Pandavas are born there and Pandu attains salvation _(actors: Pandu, Pandavas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Mahabharata tradition)
- **Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana** — Krishna persuades the cowherds to worship Mount Govardhana instead of Indra, and when Indra sends rains he lifts the mountain as an umbrella, after which Indra consecrates him as Govinda _(actors: Krishna, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Krishna Restores Sandipani's Dead Son as Guru-Dakshina** — As guru-dakshina, Krishna and Balarama slay the demon Pancajana (taking the Pancajanya conch) and descend to Yama's realm to restore Sandipani's son lost in the sea at Prabhasa _(actors: Krishna, Balarama, Sandipani, Pancajana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ujjain-avantika.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X)
- **Kunti reveals Karna's birth to the Pandavas** — Kunti discloses that Karna, whom they killed, was their eldest brother born to her by Surya before her marriage, overwhelming the Pandavas with fresh grief and remorse _(actors: Kunti, Yudhishthira, Pandavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/11-stri-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Stri Parva)
- **Kuntī's svayaṃvara and marriage to Pāṇḍu** — At her self-choice ceremony Kuntī garlands the Kuru king Pāṇḍu, becoming his senior queen (Mādrī being the second) _(actors: Kuntī, Pāṇḍu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Lakshmi incarnates as Rukmini with Krishna** — When Vishnu descends as Krishna, Lakshmi incarnates as his chief queen Rukmini (and as Radha in devotional tradition) _(actors: Lakshmi (Rukmini), Krishna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Marriage of Revati and Balarama** — On Brahma's counsel Revati is married to Balarama, who taps her with the tip of his plough to reduce her from her earlier-yuga height to the stature of his own age _(actors: Revati, Balarama, Kakudmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.3; Vishnu Purana 4.1)
- **Nala loses his kingdom at dice and is exiled** — Possessed Nala gambles away his entire kingdom to his brother Puṣkara and is stripped and exiled into the wilderness _(actors: Nala, Puṣkara, Damayantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 57–58)
- **Nara and Nārāyaṇa reborn as Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa** — The twin sages take their final earthly descent as Arjuna (Nara) and Kṛṣṇa (Nārāyaṇa), their cross-yuga friendship explaining the inseparable Kurukṣetra bond _(actors: Nara/Arjuna, Nārāyaṇa/Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva / Nārāyaṇīya; Bhagavad Gītā)
- **Pandu's curse and birth of the Pandavas** — Cursed by sage Kindama, Pandu cannot father children; Kunti and Madri invoke gods to bear Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva _(actors: Pandu, Kunti, Madri, Dharma/Vayu/Indra/Ashvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Pāṇḍavas Worship Śiva at Sthāneśvar before the War** — The Pāṇḍavas worship Śiva at Sthāneśvar Mahādev in Thanesar to secure victory before the Kurukṣetra war _(actors: Pāṇḍavas, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (local sthala-purana)
- **Pulastya Names Pushkar First of Tīrthas to Bhīṣma** — In the Tirtha-yatra Parva sage Pulastya instructs Bhishma on holy fords, opening with Pushkar where Brahma and the gods are ever present, the textual root of its Adi Tirtha rank _(actors: Pulastya, Bhishma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Mahabharata (Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva))
- **Release of the sacrificial horse and Arjuna's campaign begins** — The consecrated stallion is set loose to roam for a year; Arjuna is appointed its protector, instructed to conquer without needless slaughter, and follows it with an army _(actors: Arjuna, Yudhiṣṭhira, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.71-73)
- **Sparing Maya the Architect** — Arjuna and Krishna spare the asura-architect Maya, who in gratitude builds the Pandavas' illusion-hall at Indraprastha _(actors: Arjuna, Krishna, Maya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi/Sabha Parva)
- **The butcher's past-life curse revealed** — The butcher reveals he was a learned Brāhmaṇa in a former life, brought to the butcher's caste by a curse, now re-ascending through faultless duty and filial service _(actors: Dharma-vyādha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyadha-gita.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 205-206)
- **The dāna of the head** — Recognising the danger of the vow, Kṛṣṇa begs Barbarīka's head as alms; bound by dāna-dharma Barbarīka offers it, asking to witness the war before he dies _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Barbarīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Folk Mahābhārata; Khāṭū Śyām sthala-tradition)
- **The exile-stake and second dice-game** — After Dhṛtarāṣṭra's boons free the Pāṇḍavas, a single decisive throw lost commits them to twelve years' forest exile and a thirteenth incognito year _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Śakuni, Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā Parva)
- **The kaḷappali — Aravān's self-sacrifice to Kālī** — In the Tamil tradition Aravān, one of three flawless warriors bearing the thirty-two perfections, freely offers his own head to Kālī before the war to secure Pāṇḍava victory _(actors: Aravān, Kālī, Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Tamil Mahābhārata (Villiputtūrār); Kūttāṇṭavar temple tradition)
- **The Lokapalas arm Arjuna** — The world-guardians appear and bestow the danda, pasha, and antardhana weapons, and Indra invites Arjuna to heaven _(actors: Arjuna, Yama, Varuna, Kubera, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 41-42)
- **The mace-duel and Duryodhana's broken thighs** — In the gada-yuddha Bhima cannot beat the more skilled Duryodhana fairly; on Krishna's thigh-slapping cue he strikes a forbidden blow below the navel, shattering Duryodhana's thighs to fulfill his dice-hall vow _(actors: Bhima, Duryodhana, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva (Gada-yuddha))
- **The Pandavas Pursue Shiva as a Bull (Pancha Kedar)** — Seeking absolution after Kurukshetra, the Pandavas pursue Shiva, who flees as a bull and dives into the earth, re-emerging in five parts to form the Pancha Kedar shrines _(actors: Pandavas, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Panch Kedar sthala-purana)
- **The Rajasuya sacrifice performed** — Yudhishthira is consecrated samrat in the grand Rajasuya, the high-water mark of Pandava fortune _(actors: Yudhishthira, Vyasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 32-34)
- **The Yadava clan self-destructs in the brawl at Prabhasa** — At a drunken festival Satyaki beheads Kritavarma after mutual taunts; the mob kills Satyaki and Pradyumna, and every Yadava who grabs the eraka reeds finds it transformed into an iron club, so brother slays brother until almost the entire Vrishni-Andhaka race lies dead, fulfilling the curse _(actors: Satyaki, Kritavarma, Pradyumna, Krishna, the Yadavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.3)
- **The Yakṣa revealed as Dharma; brothers revived** — Pleased by the son's equitable virtue, the Yakṣa reveals himself as Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira's divine father, restores all four brothers and returns the firesticks _(actors: Dharma (Yama), Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yaksha-prashna.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 314)
- **Ulūpī Weds Arjuna and Bears Irāvān** — The nāga princess Ulūpī of the Airāvata line weds Arjuna in Nāgaloka and bears Irāvān, later reviving Arjuna after his death by Babhruvāhana _(actors: Ulūpī, Arjuna, Irāvān, Babhruvāhana)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata)
- **Uttanka descends into Nagaloka and burns it with the Agni-horse** — Indra's vajra tunnels Uttanka into the serpent-world where, after the cosmic loom-vision, he blows into the fire-horse Agni, flooding Nagaloka with flame until the serpents return the earrings _(actors: Uttanka, Indra, Agni, Takshaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Paushya Parva)
- **Vidura-niti delivered** — During Dhritarashtra's sleepless night Vidura delivers a long aphoristic treatise on statecraft and ethics, urging the king to restrain Duryodhana and return the Pandavas' share _(actors: Vidura, Dhritarashtra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 33-40 (Prajagara))
- **Vyasa Fathers the Kuru Heirs by Niyoga** — When Vicitravirya dies childless and Bhishma refuses the widows, Satyavati summons Vyasa, who by niyoga fathers Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura _(actors: Vyasa, Satyavati, Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhishma.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~104-106)
- **Vyāsa divides the Veda into four** — At the Dvāpara–Kali junction Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa splits the single Veda into four for the diminished memory of Kali-Yuga humans _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.3–4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4; Mahābhārata)
- **Vyāsa Teaches Śuka, Who Merges into Brahman** — Vyāsa teaches his son Śuka the path to Brahman; perfected, Śuka ascends and merges into the all-pervading Brahman _(actors: Vyāsa, Śuka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 224-250)
- **Yogamaya escapes Kamsa as the goddess** — Kamsa dashes the substituted girl on a rock, but she rises as the eight-armed goddess, declares his slayer is born, and vanishes _(actors: Kamsa, Yogamaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.4)
- **Abduction of the Kashi princesses** — Bhishma seizes the three Kashi princesses for Vicitravirya; Amba, in love with Shalva, is released and vows vengeance, reincarnating as Shikhandin _(actors: Bhishma, Amba, Ambika, Ambalika, Shalva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 102-103)
- **Abhimanyu Slays Lakshmana** — Trapped within the array, Abhimanyu wreaks havoc and slays Lakshmana, Duryodhana's son, enraging the king _(actors: Abhimanyu, Lakshmana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata, Drona Parva)
- **Aravān's three last wishes and the Mohinī marriage** — Granted last wishes, Aravān asks not to die unmarried; Kṛṣṇa takes the female form Mohinī to wed him for one night _(actors: Aravān, Kṛṣṇa (as Mohinī))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Tamil Mahābhārata; Kūttāṇṭavar temple tradition)
- **Arjuna ascends to Indra's heaven** — Matali carries Arjuna to Amaravati, where he learns the vajra and celestial weapons and is taught song and dance by Citrasena _(actors: Arjuna, Mátali, Indra, Citrasena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 42-46)
- **Arjuna subdues the Trigartas** — The surviving grandsons of the Trigarta kings attack to avenge their war-dead elders; Arjuna subdues them after a hard fight _(actors: Arjuna, Trigarta warriors)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.73)
- **Arjuna's vow to slay Jayadratha** — Learning of his son's death, Arjuna swears to slay Jayadratha by next sunset or enter the fire himself; Drona walls Jayadratha off with three nested formations _(actors: Arjuna, Krishna, Jayadratha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 72-84 (Pratijna))
- **Balarama's fury and Krishna's justification** — Enraged at the illegal thigh-blow, Balarama raises his plough-weapon against Bhima and must be restrained by Krishna, who justifies the blow as retribution for Duryodhana's own adharma _(actors: Balarama, Krishna, Bhima)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva (Gada-yuddha))
- **Balarama's yogic departure as Shesha-Ananta** — Krishna finds Balarama seated in yoga giving up his body; a great white serpent issues from his mouth and glides into the sea received by Ocean and the Nagas, Balarama returning to his nature as the cosmic serpent Shesha/Ananta _(actors: Balarama, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.4)
- **Bhṛgu Teaches Bharadvāja on Cosmogony and Varṇa** — Bhṛgu teaches the Mind-born primeval Being and a color-coded varṇa, but Bharadvāja's objection resolves that caste is by conduct, not birth _(actors: Bhṛgu, Bharadvāja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 182-192)
- **Bhima kills Duhshasana and drinks his blood** — Bhima seizes Duhshasana, tears open his chest and drinks his blood, fulfilling his dice-hall vows; Draupadi at last binds up the hair she had left loose since her disrobing _(actors: Bhima, Duhshasana, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva 61/83)
- **Bhima Slays Bakasura of Ekachakra** — Bhima eats the food tribute meant for the man-eating rakshasa Baka and breaks his back across his knee, freeing the town _(actors: Bhima, Bakasura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~159-160)
- **Bhima slays the 105 Upakicakas** — When Kicaka's kinsmen seize Sairandhri to burn her on his pyre, Bhima uproots a tree, charges in, and kills all 105 Upakicakas, freeing her _(actors: Bhima, Upakicakas, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 23)
- **Bhīṣma accepts the role of teacher on the arrow-bed** — Empowered by Kṛṣṇa, the dying Bhīṣma agrees to instruct Yudhiṣṭhira in rāja-, āpad-, and mokṣa-dharma until the sun turns north _(actors: Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.54-55)
- **Birth of the Pandavas** — Cursed Pandu's heirs are born via Kunti's mantra summoning gods — Yudhishthira (Dharma), Bhima (Vayu), Arjuna (Indra), and via Madri the twins Nakula and Sahadeva (Ashvins); Kunti's earlier secret son by Surya is Karna _(actors: Pandu, Kunti, Madri, Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Karna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Bāṇāsura Defeated by Kṛṣṇa** — The thousand-armed Śiva-devotee Bāṇāsura, whose daughter Uṣā loved Aniruddha, is defeated by Kṛṣṇa, his arms shorn to four, and spared at Śiva's plea _(actors: Bāṇāsura, Kṛṣṇa, Uṣā, Aniruddha, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.62-63)
- **Building and Rule of Dvārakā by Kṛṣṇa** — Krishna builds and rules the golden many-gated sea-fortress city of Dwarka after leading the Yadavas out of Mathura _(actors: Krishna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Compilation of the eighteen Purāṇas and the Bhāgavata** — Vyāsa compiles the eighteen Mahā-Purāṇas; reproached by Nārada for not glorifying the Lord, he composes the Bhāgavata and teaches it to Śuka _(actors: Vyāsa, Nārada, Śuka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Day 3 — Krishna's first wheel-charge against Bhishma** — Seeing Arjuna fight half-heartedly while Bhishma devastates the army, Krishna breaks his vow, seizes a chariot-wheel and rushes at Bhishma; Arjuna restrains him and swears to fight in earnest _(actors: Krishna, Bhishma, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/06-bhishma-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Bhishma Parva 55-59)
- **Dharma's boon of non-recognition** — Dharma grants that during the coming thirteenth year of incognito living the Pāṇḍavas pass unrecognized, plus inner conquest over the six foes, easing the year in Virāṭa's kingdom _(actors: Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yaksha-prashna.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 315)
- **Dushyanta's denial and the celestial voice naming Bharata** — At court Dushyanta publicly disowns Shakuntala, who rebukes him with a fierce dharma speech; a sky-voice declares the child his and decrees the name Bharata, after which the king reveals his denial was a deliberate strategy _(actors: Dushyanta, Shakuntala, Bharata, the akashavani)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Karna becomes Parashurama's disguised pupil** — Rejected by Drona, Karna goes to Parashurama claiming to be a brahmana to learn brahmastra-grade weapons _(actors: Karna, Parashurama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Santi/Vana back-narratives)
- **Kṛṣṇa slays Ekalavya** — Kṛṣṇa kills Ekalavya in battle, commonly by crushing him with a hurled boulder; in the Harivaṃśa's kinship framing this is the slaying of a lost Yādava cousin _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Ekalavya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Harivaṃśa; Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva)
- **Kauśika sent home to serve his parents** — The butcher tells Kauśika he neglected his aged parents for tapas; the twice-humbled ascetic returns home, tends them, and is reconciled to true dharma _(actors: Kauśika, Dharma-vyādha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyadha-gita.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~206)
- **Krishna abducts Rukmini** — Krishna elopes with Rukmini on the eve of her wedding to Shishupala, publicly humiliating him and seeding his enmity _(actors: Krishna, Rukmini, Shishupala, Rukmi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.52-54)
- **Krishna slays Kaṃsa at Mathurā** — Summoned to Mathurā's bow-festival, Krishna and Balarāma kill the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa and the wrestlers Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika, then Krishna drags Kaṃsa from his throne and kills him, reinstating Ugrasena _(actors: Krishna, Balarāma, Kaṃsa, Ugrasena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Mass cremation and water-offering for the dead** — At Yudhishthira's command Vidura cremates the slain warriors with full Vedic rites, and both armies' survivors descend to the Ganga to offer water-libations, Kunti openly making the offering for Karna _(actors: Yudhishthira, Vidura, Kunti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/11-stri-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Stri Parva 26-27 (Shraddha/Jalapradanika))
- **Nala deserts Damayantī in the forest** — Tormented by Kali, Nala cuts away half his sleeping wife's garment and abandons her in the night _(actors: Nala, Damayantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 59)
- **Pāṇḍu's curse by the sage Kindama** — Pāṇḍu kills the sage Kindama mating in deer form and is cursed to die the instant he approaches a wife in desire, making natural fatherhood impossible _(actors: Pāṇḍu, Kindama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Rebirth as Drupada's child Śikhaṇḍin(ī)** — Ambā is reborn to King Drupada of Pāñcāla as a daughter raised secretly as a son, Śikhaṇḍin, precipitating a marriage crisis with Daśārṇa _(actors: Ambā reborn as Śikhaṇḍin, Drupada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~188–192)
- **Sanatsujatiya teaching** — The boy-sage Sanatsujata teaches the still-sleepless king that death is not annihilation but ignorance, expounding Brahman, true knowledge, and liberation _(actors: Sanatsujata, Dhritarashtra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 41-46 (Sanatsujata))
- **Slaying of Putana** — The demoness sent with poisoned breast-milk is drained of life by the suckling infant Krishna and granted liberation _(actors: Krishna, Putana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.6; Harivamsa)
- **Slaying of Sisupala** — After Sisupala exceeds his hundred forgiven offenses objecting to Krishna's first-honour, Krishna beheads him with the Sudarsana Cakra and his radiance merges into Krishna _(actors: Krishna, Sisupala, Bhishma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 39-42; Bhagavata Purana 7.1)
- **The 18-Day Mahābhārata War at Kurukṣetra** — Eighteen akṣauhiṇīs assemble between the Sarasvatī and Dṛṣadvatī and fight the 18-day Kaurava–Pāṇḍava war that seals the Dvāpara–Kali yuga-turn _(actors: Pāṇḍavas, Kauravas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Mahabharata, Bhishma-parva onward)
- **The Brahmashiras duel and Vyasa's intervention** — Cornered at Vyasa's hermitage, Ashvatthaman invokes the Brahmashiras on a blade of grass; Arjuna counters with his own Brahmastra, and Vyasa and Narada step between to halt the world-ending collision _(actors: Ashvatthaman, Arjuna, Vyasa, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva 13-14 (Aishika))
- **The Gods Grant Nala Boons and the Marriage** — Pleased, the four gods grant Nala gifts of fire, water, dharma and cooking; the couple marries and bears Indrasena and Indrasenā _(actors: Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, Yama, Nala, Damayantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 56)
- **The Iron-Club Curse on the Yadavas** — Sages mocked when young Yadavas disguised Samba as a pregnant woman curse that he will bear an iron club destroying the clan; Samba births an iron bolt ground to powder and cast into the sea _(actors: Vishvamitra, Kanva, Narada, Samba)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Mahabharata 16.1-2; Bhagavata 11.1)
- **The Parashurama-Bhishma Duel** — Spurned Amba appeals to Parashurama, who fights Bhishma a multi-day duel at Kurukshetra that ends inconclusively when the gods intervene _(actors: Amba, Parashurama, Bhishma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhishma.md) — (Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva ~179-186)
- **The Pāṇḍavas Visit Pushkar** — The Pandavas visit Pushkar on their pilgrimage from the Kamyaka forest, attesting its established sanctity by the Pandava era _(actors: Pandavas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Mahabharata (Vana Parva))
- **The Python Seizes Bhīma** — Ages later during the Pāṇḍava exile, the boon-strengthened serpent Nahuṣa seizes Bhīma in a mountain cave and drains his strength _(actors: Nahuṣa, Bhīma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 176-177)
- **The witnessing head over Kurukṣetra** — Kṛṣṇa immortalises Barbarīka's head and sets it on a high hill to watch the entire eighteen-day war _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Barbarīka's head)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Folk Mahābhārata traditions)
- **Uddhava departs for Badarikashrama** — After the final bhakti teaching Uddhava, overwhelmed, takes leave of Krishna and proceeds to Badarikashrama to practice renunciation _(actors: Uddhava, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.29)
- **Uttanka discharges the fee before sunset** — The fire-horse carries Uttanka back to deliver the earrings in time, and Veda explains all the omens he met _(actors: Uttanka, Veda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Paushya Parva)
- **Vasudeva Carries Kṛṣṇa Across the Yamunā to Gokula** — Vasudeva carries the infant Kṛṣṇa across the flooding Yamunā to Gokula, exchanging him for Nanda and Yaśodā's newborn daughter Yoga-māyā, who announces Kaṃsa's doom _(actors: Vasudeva, Kṛṣṇa, Nanda, Yaśodā, Yoga-māyā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.3-4)
- **Vidura speaks the Vidura-nīti and resigns his post** — On the eve of war Vidura pours out his eight-chapter aphoristic discourse on nīti to the sleepless king, and renounces his ministerial post and weapons to take no part in the war _(actors: Vidura, Dhṛtarāṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 33-40)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira receives the akṣaya-pātra from Sūrya** — In exile Yudhiṣṭhira propitiates Sūrya, who grants the inexhaustible vessel that feeds the Pāṇḍavas' guests until Draupadī finishes her daily meal _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Sūrya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Amba's Rebirth as Shikhandin** — After tapas and Shiva's boon to be the cause of Bhishma's death, Amba immolates herself and is reborn as Shikhandin, child of Drupada, who obtains manhood by exchanging sex with a yaksha _(actors: Amba, Shiva, Shikhandin, Drupada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhishma.md) — (Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva ~187-193)
- **Arjuna defeats Vajradatta of Prāgjyotiṣa** — Vajradatta, son of the slain Bhagadatta, rides his war-elephant against Arjuna; a fierce three-day duel ends in Vajradatta's submission _(actors: Arjuna, Vajradatta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.74-75)
- **Arjuna slays Karna's son Vrishasena** — Keeping his fresh vow to avenge Abhimanyu, Arjuna kills Karna's son Vrishasena before his eyes with razor-arrows, breaking the grief-stricken Karna's spirit _(actors: Arjuna, Vrishasena, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva 85)
- **Ashvatthaman redirects the weapon into Uttara's womb** — Unable to withdraw his weapon, Ashvatthaman redirects it into the wombs of the Pandava women, especially Uttara, to extinguish the line; Krishna vows to revive the slain embryo and names him Parikshit _(actors: Ashvatthaman, Uttara, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva 15-16 (Aishika))
- **Authorship of the Brahma Sūtras (Bādarāyaṇa)** — Under the name Bādarāyaṇa, Vyāsa is the traditional author of the Brahma Sūtras founding the Vedānta darśana, with a scholarly debate over the identity _(actors: Vyāsa / Bādarāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Tradition; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4)
- **Bharata crowned Cakravartin and namesake of the land** — Dushyanta installs Bharata as crown prince; Bharata becomes a universal sovereign whose conquests give his name to the Bharatas and the subcontinent Bharatavarsha, continuing the Paurava-Kuru line _(actors: Dushyanta, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Bhima kills Jarasandha** — Jarasandha of Magadha is slain by Bhima, clearing the way for Yudhishthira's Rajasuya _(actors: Bhima, Jarasandha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha-parva 20-22)
- **Bhima Slays Kirmira and Jatasura** — During the exile Bhima kills the rakshasa Kirmira in the Kamyaka forest and later slays Jatasura who abducted his kin _(actors: Bhima, Kirmira, Jatasura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva ~11, ~157)
- **Birth of the Kauravas** — Gandhari bears from a mass of flesh divided into a hundred jars the hundred Kauravas led by Duryodhana, plus a daughter Duhshala _(actors: Gandhari, Duryodhana, the Kauravas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Birth of Yudhiṣṭhira by Dharma** — At Pāṇḍu's request Kuntī invokes Dharma and bears Yudhiṣṭhira, the eldest Pāṇḍava and embodiment of righteousness _(actors: Kuntī, Dharma/Yama, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Condensed Mahābhārata and Kṛṣṇa carita** — The Agni Purāṇa gives a précis of the Yādava birth of Kṛṣṇa, his Vṛndāvana/Mathurā exploits, and the Pāṇḍava–Kaurava conflict and war _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Pāṇḍavas, Kauravas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa (Hari-vaṃśa/Mahābhārata digest))
- **Damayantī curses the hunter and reaches Chedi** — Abandoned Damayantī curses a lustful hunter dead by her chastity, then is taken in as an attendant in Chedi and recognized by her lotus-mark _(actors: Damayantī, the hunter, Sudeva, Subāhu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 60–66)
- **Day 8 — Iravan beheaded by Alambusha** — Iravan, Arjuna's son by the Naga princess Ulupi, fights brilliantly but is beheaded by the rakshasa Alambusha, while Ghatotkaca dominates the field with illusions _(actors: Iravan, Alambusha, Ghatotkaca)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/06-bhishma-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Bhishma Parva 83-91)
- **Death of Ketumāna at Kurukṣetra** — Ekalavya's son Ketumāna, a Niṣāda warrior, fights and is slain on the Kaurava side in the great Kurukṣetra war _(actors: Ketumāna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Mahābhārata Droṇa Parva)
- **Draupadi Becomes Wife to the Five Pandavas** — On Kunti's unseeing instruction to 'share it among you,' Draupadi becomes the common wife of all five Pandavas _(actors: Kunti, Draupadi, the Pandavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~182-191)
- **Duryodhana left dying appoints Ashvatthaman** — Mortally wounded but still alive at the lake, Duryodhana reviles Krishna for the unfair killings and survives into the night to appoint Ashvatthaman as the last commander _(actors: Duryodhana, Ashvatthaman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva (Gada-yuddha))
- **Ekalavya's thumb as guru-dakshina** — The self-taught Nishada prince Ekalavya surpasses Arjuna, and Drona demands his right thumb to preserve Arjuna's supremacy _(actors: Ekalavya, Drona, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Harivamsha)
- **Founding of Dvārakā** — To escape Jarāsandha's relentless sieges and Kālayavana, Krishna leads the Yādavas west and builds with Viśvakarman the island-fortress city of Dvārakā in the sea _(actors: Krishna, Viśvakarman, Jarāsandha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Kṛṣṇa Delivers the Bhagavad Gītā at Jyotisar** — As the armies face off at Jyotisar, Kṛṣṇa speaks the Bhagavad Gītā to Arjuna and grants the viśvarūpa-darśana under the immortal banyan _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 1.1; Mahabharata, Bhishma-parva)
- **Kali Vows to Destroy Nala** — Arriving too late and enraged that a mortal won the bride the gods coveted, the age-demon Kali vows to destroy Nala and lurks twelve years for an opening _(actors: Kali, Dvāpara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 56)
- **Kṛṣṇa's Infant Līlās at Gokula** — At Gokula the infant Kṛṣṇa slays Pūtanā, Śakaṭāsura and Tṛṇāvarta, steals butter, and is bound to the mortar in the damodara-līlā _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Pūtanā, Śakaṭāsura, Tṛṇāvarta)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.3-11)
- **King Nala Released from Śani's Affliction** — Under Saturn's malefic grip King Nala loses his kingdom and is parted from Damayanti; bathing in the Nala Tirtham and worshipping at Tirunallar, he is freed from Sani's affliction and regains throne and queen _(actors: Nala, Damayanti, Shani)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Mahabharata (Nalopakhyana); Sthala-purana)
- **Krishna's false sunset and the slaying of Jayadratha** — Day 14: Krishna covers the sun feigning sunset; Jayadratha exposes himself and Arjuna beheads him, shooting the head into his meditating father Vriddhakshatra's lap so the boon recoils and bursts the father's head _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna, Jayadratha, Vriddhakshatra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 85-146 (Jayadratha-vadha))
- **Krishna's peace embassy to Hastinapura** — Krishna goes personally to ask for only five villages; he lodges with Vidura, visits Kunti, and pleads in the Kaurava court, but Duryodhana refuses even a needle-point of land _(actors: Krishna, Duryodhana, Kunti, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Bhagavad-yana 74-150)
- **Manu Instructs Bṛhaspati on the Self** — Bṛhaspati questions Manu, who teaches the field and knower of the field, the supremacy of jñāna, and the ascent to the supreme Self _(actors: Manu, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 194-199)
- **Mohinī's widowhood and mourning** — After Aravān is sacrificed at dawn, Kṛṣṇa-as-Mohinī mourns him as a widow before resuming male form _(actors: Kṛṣṇa (as Mohinī), Aravān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Tamil Mahābhārata; Kūttāṇṭavar temple tradition)
- **Muchukunda Incinerates Kalayavana** — Awakened from his boon of long sleep in Dvapara, Muchukunda's glance incinerates Kalayavana, linking the Solar line to Krishna's story _(actors: Muchukunda, Kalayavana, Krishna)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Bhagavata X; Vishnu Purana)
- **Niyoga and the births of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura** — Vyasa fathers Dhritarashtra (born blind), Pandu (born pale), and Vidura (born wise to a maidservant) on the widows by niyoga _(actors: Vyasa, Satyavati, Ambika, Ambalika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 105-107)
- **Parashurama's curse on Karna** — After Karna endures a worm boring his thigh without flinching, Parashurama deduces his kshatriya birth and curses that his memory of the supreme astra will fail at his greatest need _(actors: Parashurama, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata)
- **Sex-change via the yakṣa Sthūṇa** — The yakṣa Sthūṇakarṇa exchanges sex with Śikhaṇḍin; Kubera's curse fixes the maleness on Śikhaṇḍin for life, defusing the Daśārṇa war _(actors: Śikhaṇḍin, Sthūṇa, Kubera)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~192–193)
- **Shiva Flees as a Bull at Kedarnath** — The Pandavas seek Shiva at Kedarnath to expiate the Kurukshetra slaughter; Shiva flees as a bull and dives into the ground, leaving the worshipped hump and the Panch Kedar _(actors: Pandavas, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Shiva Purana; Mahabharata-derived sthala-purana)
- **Slaying of Shakatasura** — Baby Krishna overturns and destroys the cart-demon with a kick _(actors: Krishna, Shakatasura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.7)
- **Submergence of Dvārakā** — After Krishna's departure the city of Dwarka sinks into the sea, marking the hinge into the present Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Yadavas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Mahabharata (Mausala Parva); Bhagavata & Vishnu Puranas)
- **Susharma's Trigarta cattle-raid** — The Trigarta king Susharma raids Matsya's cattle and captures King Virata; the four Pandavas rescue Virata, rout the Trigartas, and capture Susharma, whom Yudhishthira mercifully frees _(actors: Susharma, Virata, Bhima)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 30-33)
- **The first game of dice** — Playing for Duryodhana, the cheating Shakuni wins everything from Yudhishthira in escalating stakes down to his brothers, himself, and finally Draupadi _(actors: Yudhishthira, Shakuni, Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 45-58)
- **The hunter Jara's arrow and Krishna's departure** — As Krishna lies in meditation, the hunter Jara mistakes his raised foot for a deer and shoots him with the very iron splinter from the cursed club; Krishna consoles and blesses Jara, then withdraws into his supreme abode, ending the Krishna avatar and marking the onset of Kali Yuga _(actors: Jara, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.4; Bhagavata Purana 11.30-31)
- **The Killing of Abhimanyu** — A ring of Kaurava maharathis disarms the weaponless sixteen-year-old Abhimanyu and Duhshasana's son strikes him dead with a mace, the moral nadir of the war _(actors: Abhimanyu, Karna, Drona, Kripa, Duhshasana's son)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata, Drona Parva)
- **The verdict — Sudarśana alone won the war** — After the war the witnessing head declares it saw no human warrior win, only Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana cakra and the Goddess's tongue drinking blood; the heroes were mere instruments _(actors: Barbarīka's head, Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Folk Mahābhārata; Khāṭū Śyām sthala-tradition)
- **The Yadava Massacre at Prabhasa** — Drunk on maireya at the Prabhasa festival, the Yadavas quarrel and uproot the lethal eraka reeds as clubs, slaughtering one another until nearly all the Vrishnis die _(actors: Satyaki, Kritavarman, Pradyumna, Samba, Aniruddha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Mahabharata 16.3-4; Bhagavata 11.30)
- **The Yakṣa Praśna** — After his four brothers drink and die at a guarded lake, Yudhiṣṭhira answers a Yakṣa's riddles, chooses to revive Nakula for impartial dharma, and the Yakṣa — his father Dharma — revives all four and grants undetected passage of the thirteenth year _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Dharma/Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Third demonic birth: Sisupala and Dantavakra slain** — The pair are reborn as the human kings Sisupala (beheaded by the Sudarsana Cakra) and Dantavakra (killed by Krishna), their radiance merging into Krishna to discharge the curse _(actors: Sisupala, Dantavakra, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1, 10.74, 10.78)
- **Tulādhāra Instructs Jājali** — A heavenly voice tells the penance-proud ascetic Jājali he is unequal to the humble grocer Tulādhāra, who expounds ahiṃsā and honest livelihood as true dharma _(actors: Jājali, Tulādhāra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva 261-264)
- **Urvashi's curse on Arjuna** — Spurned by Arjuna, the apsara Urvashi curses him to be a eunuch, which Indra softens to last only one year of his choosing _(actors: Urvashi, Arjuna, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 45-46)
- **Uttanka receives Krishna's Vishvarupa darshana** — In the Ashvamedhika version, an enraged Uttanka makes to curse Krishna for the war's carnage but is shown the Universal Form and taught the war's necessity for dharma _(actors: Uttanka, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Ashvamedhika Parva 14.53-54)
- **Vidura's death and merger into Yudhiṣṭhira** — In forest penance Vidura casts his life-breaths and tejas into Yudhiṣṭhira by yogic power, both being portions of Dharma; a heavenly voice forbids cremating the yogin's body, closing Yama's curse-arc _(actors: Vidura, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Āśramavāsika Parva)
- **Viśvakarmā raises Dvārakā in a single night** — At Kṛṣṇa's request Viśvakarmā raises the sea-girt capital Dvārakā in a single night on land reclaimed from the ocean _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishvakarma-and-tvashtar.md) — (Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Harivaṃśa)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira's Dharma-Catechism Frees Nahuṣa** — Yudhiṣṭhira answers the serpent's riddles on dharma and varṇa, satisfying Nahuṣa, who releases Bhīma, sheds the serpent body, and ascends to heaven _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Nahuṣa, Bhīma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 179-181)
- **Arjuna destroys the Nivatakavachas and Hiranyapura** — As guru-dakshina to Indra, Arjuna destroys the Nivatakavacha danavas of the sea and the flying demon-city Hiranyapura _(actors: Arjuna, the Nivatakavachas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 168-173)
- **Arjuna's Oath to Kill Jayadratha** — Finding his son dead, Arjuna swears to kill Jayadratha before sunset the next day or enter fire, a feat Krishna later engineers _(actors: Arjuna, Jayadratha, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata, Drona Parva)
- **Arjuna spares the Saindhava forces at Duḥśalā's plea** — In the Sindhu country of the dead Jayadratha, the bereaved widows and boy-heir give battle; Arjuna spares them when Duḥśalā pleads and her grandson faints _(actors: Arjuna, Duḥśalā, Jayadratha's son)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.78)
- **Arjuna's Union with Ulupi** — During his pilgrimage-exile Arjuna is drawn under the Ganga by the Naga princess Ulupi, fathering Iravan _(actors: Arjuna, Ulupi, Iravan)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~206)
- **Balarama's Departure at Prabhasa** — Balarama withdraws into yoga on the Prabhasa shore and the white serpent Shesha, whose portion he was, issues from his mouth into the sea, his return to source _(actors: Balarama, Shesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Mahabharata 16.4; Bhagavata 11.30)
- **Bhima Splits Jarasandha** — Bhima wrestles Jarasandha for many days and, on Krishna's split-leaf hint, rends him in two and hurls the halves apart so they cannot rejoin, freeing the captive kings _(actors: Bhima, Jarasandha, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Sabha Parva ~20-24)
