- **Dattatreya's Twenty-Four Gurus Recounted** — Within the Uddhava-gita, Krishna recounts the avadhuta Dattatreya's dialogue with King Yadu listing the twenty-four gurus he took from nature _(actors: Krishna, Dattatreya, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.7-9)
- **Narayanastra released and countered** — Ashvatthama unleashes Vishnu's Narayana weapon; Krishna has the army submit unresisting so it dissipates harmlessly _(actors: Ashvatthama, Krishna, Bhima, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva)
- **The Uddhava-Gita delivered** — Krishna gives his last great discourse to Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and the avadhuta's 24 gurus, then sends him to Badarikashrama _(actors: Krishna, Uddhava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana XI.7-29)
- **Death of Duhshasana** — Bhima tears open Duhshasana's chest and drinks his blood, fulfilling his dice-hall vow; Draupadi binds her hair in the blood _(actors: Bhima, Duhshasana, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva)
- **Krishna's Departure by the Hunter Jara** — The hunter Jara mistakes Krishna's foot for a deer and shoots him; Krishna ascends and Dvaraka sinks beneath the sea _(actors: Krishna, Jara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.30-31)
- **Yadava fratricide at Prabhasa** — Drunken Yadavas turn the cursed reeds-turned-clubs on each other and almost the whole clan dies at Prabhasa _(actors: the Yadavas, Balarama, Satyaki, Kritavarma, Pradyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana XI.30; Mausala Parva 3)
- **Yudhishthira's reign and the Ashvamedha** — Yudhishthira is crowned at Hastinapura, Bhishma delivers the Shanti and Anushasana teachings before dying at the solstice, and a horse-sacrifice is performed _(actors: Yudhishthira, Bhishma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti, Anushasana, Ashvamedhika Parvas)
- **Departure of Balarama** — Balarama merges into yoga by the sea as a great white serpent issues from his mouth into the ocean _(actors: Balarama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana XI.30; Mausala Parva)
- **Fall of Duryodhana** — Drawn from a lake, Duryodhana duels Bhima with maces; Bhima smashes his thigh on Krishna's hint, fulfilling his vow _(actors: Duryodhana, Bhima, Krishna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva)
- **The sages' curse on Samba** — Krishna's son Samba, dressed as a pregnant woman to mock visiting sages, is cursed to bear an iron club that will doom the Yadava clan; ground to powder it regrows as deadly reed-grass _(actors: Samba, Vishvamitra, Durvasa, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Death of Krishna marks onset of Kali Yuga** — The death of Krishna, traditionally on 17/18 February 3102 BCE, marks the onset of the Kali Yuga and the epoch of the Kali-samvat era _(actors: Krishna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/hindu-calendar-and-panchanga.md) — (Surya Siddhanta; Puranic tradition)
- **Karṇa born with the Kavaca-Kuṇḍala; Indra extracts it** — Karṇa is born with invulnerable golden armor and earrings fused to his body, the gift of his father Sūrya; Indra extracts them by guile to make Karṇa killable _(actors: Karṇa, Sūrya, Indra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana/Karṇa Parvas)
- **The Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the Dvapara-Kali transition** — The great Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the turn from Dvapara into Kali Yuga, traditionally dated to 3102 BCE _(actors: Krishna, Pandavas, Kauravas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana 1.18, 11.31, 12.2)
- **The Sauptika night massacre** — Ashvatthama raids the sleeping camp, killing Draupadi's five sons; his Brahmashiras aimed at Parikshit's womb is countered by Krishna, who curses him _(actors: Ashvatthama, Draupadi's sons, Krishna, Parikshit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Yadava civil war at Prabhasa** — On pilgrimage the drunken Yadavas quarrel, the reeds turn to iron clubs in their hands, and the entire clan slaughters itself _(actors: the Yadavas, Satyaki, Kritavarma, Pradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Death of Balarama** — Balarama withdraws into yoga at the seashore and Shesha-naga issues from his mouth into the ocean as he departs the world _(actors: Balarama, Shesha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana 11.30)
- **Death of Shakuni** — Sahadeva beheads Shakuni, the dice-master architect of the war, fulfilling his own dice-hall vow _(actors: Sahadeva, Shakuni, Uluka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva)
- **Garga names Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma** — The Yādava family-priest Garga performs the naming rite for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma _(actors: Garga, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.8; Garga Saṃhitā)
- **Planets align in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga** — The Surya Siddhanta sets all planets in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga (18 Feb 3102 BCE), synchronizing the planetary clock with the cosmological clock _(actors: the grahas (planets))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/jyotisha-and-the-zodiac.md) — (Surya Siddhanta)
- **Submersion of Dwaraka** — As Krishna departs the sea reclaims Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates the surviving women and children, who are raided by bandits en route _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Mausala Parva 7-8)
- **Death of Krishna** — Krishna sits in meditation under a pipal tree and the hunter Jara, mistaking his reddish sole for a deer, shoots an arrow piercing it; Krishna ascends to his abode, ending the avatar and marking the onset of Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Jara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana 11.30-11.31)
- **Onset of Kali Yuga at Krishna's departure** — Krishna's departure (traditionally 3102 BCE) marks the start of Kali Yuga and the Pandavas' final journey _(actors: Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana XI; Mausala Parva)
- **The mace-duel and fall of Duryodhana** — In the gada-yuddha Bhima, cued by Krishna, breaks Duryodhana's thighs with a foul below-the-belt blow, effectively ending the war _(actors: Bhima, Duryodhana, Krishna, Balarama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva)
- **The Uddhava-Gita** — Krishna gives his last great discourse to his devotee Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and the avadhuta's 24 gurus before the end _(actors: Krishna, Uddhava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.7-11.29)
- **Viṣṇu slays the demon Pañcajana and takes the conch** — In the Mahābhārata/Skanda variant, Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa slays the demon Pañcajana (in whale-form, who had swallowed Sāndīpani's son) and seizes the conch he dwelt in, naming it Pāñcajanya _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Pañcajana, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata; Skanda Purāṇa; Panchajanya (Wikipedia))
- **Ashvatthama's night massacre** — Empowered by Shiva, Ashvatthama with Kripa and Kritavarman slaughters the sleeping Pandava camp, killing Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin and the Upapandavas _(actors: Ashvatthama, Kripa, Kritavarman, Dhrishtadyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Curse of the sages on Samba** — Krishna's son Samba is dressed as a pregnant woman to mock sages, who curse the clan to be doomed by an iron club _(actors: Samba, Vishvamitra, Durvasa, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Krishna's Vishvarupa theophany — 'I am Time'** — At the climax of the universal-form vision Krishna declares 'kalo'smi' — I am Time, the world-destroyer — revealing the cosmic person as the cosmic clock and Arjuna as its instrument _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 11.32-33)
- **Submergence of Dvaraka** — As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dvaraka; Arjuna evacuates the survivors but is robbed en route, his powers fading with the age _(actors: Arjuna, the survivors)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla** — Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla after his hundred offenses are exhausted _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Śiśupāla)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Mahābhārata)
- **Brahmashiras duel and curse of Ashvatthama** — Ashvatthama aims the Brahmashiras at Uttara's womb; Krishna vows to revive the child Parikshit, takes Ashvatthama's gem and curses him to wander 3,000 years _(actors: Ashvatthama, Arjuna, Krishna, Uttara, Vyasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Brahma-vimohana-lila (Bewilderment of Brahma)** — Doubting child-Krishna, the Brahma of our universe steals Krishna's cowherd boys and calves; Krishna duplicates them all for a year and reveals countless universes each with its own Brahma, humbling his pride _(actors: Brahma, Krishna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.13-14; Brahma Samhita 5.40-48)
- **Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head after the night-raid** — After all five Draupadeyas are slain in the night-raid, Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head but accepts the gem from his crest instead _(actors: Draupadī, Aśvatthāman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Sauptika/Strī Parvas)
- **Karṇa loses his Nāgāstra against Arjuna** — Karṇa looses the nāgāstra (the serpent Aśvasena) at Arjuna's head, but Kṛṣṇa presses the chariot into the earth so it strikes only Arjuna's crown _(actors: Karṇa, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, Aśvasena)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa Parva)
- **Krishna delivers the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna** — Krishna answers Arjuna's crisis by teaching svadharma, niskama-karma, and the imperishable atman, reconciling the warrior's duty with ahimsa _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/ahimsa-and-hindu-ethics.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 2.19-25, 2.47-48, 3.35, 18.47)
- **Krishna slays Narakasura (Naraka Chaturdashi)** — Krishna with Satyabhama slays the asura Narakasura of Pragjyotishapura and frees 16,000 captives, the South Indian Deepavali charter _(actors: Krishna, Satyabhama, Narakasura)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Harivamsha)
- **Posthumous revelation of Karna's birth** — After the war Kunti reveals Karna was the eldest Pandava; the anguished Yudhishthira curses all women never to keep a secret _(actors: Kunti, Yudhishthira, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Stri/Shanti Parva)
- **Bhagadatta's Vaiṣṇavāstra absorbed by Kṛṣṇa** — Bhagadatta looses the infallible Vaiṣṇavāstra at Arjuna, but Kṛṣṇa absorbs it onto his own chest, where it becomes the Vaijayantī garland _(actors: Bhagadatta, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Draupadī's death on the Himālayan ascent** — On the great departure toward heaven, Draupadī is the first of the six to fall dead, attributed by Yudhiṣṭhira to her partiality for Arjuna _(actors: Draupadī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Mahāprasthānika Parva)
- **Sage's curse on Samba's iron club** — Yadava princes mock rishis with Samba dressed as a pregnant woman; the cursed iron club is ground to powder that becomes the deadly eraka grass _(actors: Samba, Vishvamitra, Narada, Kanva, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Vishnu Purana)
- **Aśvatthāman looses the Nārāyaṇāstra; Pāṇḍavas survive by submission** — Aśvatthāman discharges Viṣṇu's Nārāyaṇāstra, and Kṛṣṇa has the Pāṇḍava host drop their weapons and dismount so the auto-multiplying barrage finds no resistance _(actors: Aśvatthāman, Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Draupadī restored as Śrī in heaven** — In heaven Yudhiṣṭhira finds Draupadī revealed as the goddess Śrī/Lakṣmī, closing her prior-birth incarnation _(actors: Draupadī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Svargārohaṇa Parva)
- **Submergence of Dwaraka** — As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates survivors but is robbed en route as his powers fade _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **The Yadava clan self-destructs at Prabhasa** — Thirty-six years after the war the drunken Vrishni-Andhakas slay one another with eraka-turned-iron clubs, fulfilling Gandhari's and the sages' curses _(actors: Satyaki, Kritavarman, Pradyumna, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Death of Balarama and Krishna; sinking of Dvaraka** — Balarama departs as Shesha; the hunter Jara's arrow pierces Krishna's foot and he ascends, after which the sea swallows Dvaraka, ending the Dvapara Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Balarama, Jara, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Śeṣa incarnates as Balarāma** — When Viṣṇu descends as Kṛṣṇa, Śeṣa descends as his elder brother Balarāma, whose serpent-nature departs his mouth as a white nāga at his death _(actors: Śeṣa, Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Indra gives Karṇa the Vāsava-śakti for his kavaca-kuṇḍala** — Indra trades his one-use infallible dart, the Vāsava-śakti, to Karṇa in exchange for his birth-armor and earrings (kavaca-kuṇḍala) _(actors: Indra, Karṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa/Droṇa Parva)
- **Karṇa spends the Vāsava-śakti on Ghaṭotkaca** — Forced by Ghaṭotkaca's rampage, Karṇa expends his one-use Vāsava-śakti dart (reserved for Arjuna) to kill Bhīma's son Ghaṭotkaca _(actors: Karṇa, Ghaṭotkaca, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Arjuna beheads Karṇa with the Añjalikāstra** — Arjuna uses Indra's crescent-bladed Añjalikāstra to behead Karṇa, who had lost his Bhārgavāstra knowledge to a curse at the decisive moment _(actors: Arjuna, Karṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa Parva)
- **Śiva grants Barbarīka the three infallible arrows** — Śiva grants Ghaṭotkaca's son Barbarīka three infallible arrows able to end the entire war in a moment — one marks targets to destroy, one to save, the third destroys/binds the marked _(actors: Śiva, Barbarīka)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (folk Mahābhārata traditions (Khāṭū Śyām))
- **Sudarśana obscures the sun to trap Jayadratha** — Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra obscures the sun at Kurukṣetra to trick Jayadratha into the open so Arjuna can fulfill his vow _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, Jayadratha)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Mahābhārata)
- **Brahmaśiras duel of Arjuna and Aśvatthāman; killing and revival of Parīkṣit** — After Kurukṣetra, Arjuna and Aśvatthāman loose Brahmaśiras at each other; Vyāsa and Nārada intervene, Arjuna withdraws his but Aśvatthāman cannot, redirecting it at Uttarā's womb to kill the unborn Parīkṣit, whom Kṛṣṇa revives _(actors: Arjuna, Aśvatthāman, Vyāsa, Nārada, Kṛṣṇa, Parīkṣit, Uttarā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1)
- **Aśvatthāman cursed for the Brahmaśiras misuse** — For aiming the unwithdrawable Brahmaśiras at the Pāṇḍava line, Aśvatthāman is cursed with the loss of his head-jewel and a festering wound enduring for millennia _(actors: Aśvatthāman, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1)
- **Burning of the Khāṇḍava forest and gift of the Gāṇḍīva to Arjuna** — When Agni begs Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa to help him consume the Khāṇḍava forest, Varuṇa gives Arjuna the bow Gāṇḍīva (made by Brahmā) with two inexhaustible quivers _(actors: Agni, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, Varuṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Gandiva (Wikipedia))
- **Pārijātaharaṇa — Kṛṣṇa steals the Pārijāta from Indra** — Kṛṣṇa uproots the Pārijāta tree from Indra's heaven and plants it in Satyabhāmā's courtyard, provoking a brief war with Indra _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Satyabhāmā, Rukmiṇī, Indra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Hari-vaṃśa / Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10; Parijata (Wikipedia))
- **Sūrya gifts the Syamantaka gem to Satrājit** — The sun-gem Syamantaka, source of Sūrya's brilliance and yielding eight bhāras of gold daily, is gifted by Sūrya to the Yādava king Satrājit _(actors: Sūrya, Satrājit)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Syamantaka (Wikipedia); Vishnu Purana; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.56)
- **The Syamantaka affair — Kṛṣṇa fights Jāmbavān and weds Jāmbavatī** — Falsely accused of stealing the Syamantaka after Prasena is killed by a lion and the gem taken by Jāmbavān, Kṛṣṇa fights the bear-king for 28 days (or 21), who yields the gem and his daughter Jāmbavatī in marriage; Kṛṣṇa returns it and weds Satyabhāmā _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Jāmbavān, Jāmbavatī, Prasena, Satrājit, Satyabhāmā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.56–57; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Syamantaka (Wikipedia))
- **Kṛṣṇa sounds the Pāñcajanya to open the Kurukṣetra war** — Kṛṣṇa blows his conch Pāñcajanya, with Arjuna's Devadatta and the Pāṇḍava conches, to open the Bhagavad-gītā and the Kurukṣetra war _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, the Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhagavad-gītā 1.15–18; Panchajanya (Wikipedia))
- **Sūrya gives Yudhiṣṭhira the Akṣaya-pātra** — After Yudhiṣṭhira's penance in the Gaṅgā, Sūrya gives the Pāṇḍavas the inexhaustible food-vessel Akṣaya-pātra, yielding unlimited food each day until Draupadī takes her own meal _(actors: Sūrya, Yudhiṣṭhira, Draupadī, Dhaumya)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva; Akshaya Patra (Wikipedia))
- **Kṛṣṇa sates Durvāsā with a single rice-grain from the Akṣaya-pātra** — When Durvāsā and his thousand disciples arrive after Draupadī has eaten, Kṛṣṇa eats a single clinging rice-grain from the empty pot and thereby sates the sage's whole party _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Durvāsā, Draupadī)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Kāliya-mardana — Kṛṣṇa dances on the serpent Kāliya** — The boy Kṛṣṇa leaps into the Yamunā at Vṛndāvana, is coiled by the venomous Nāga Kāliya, then dances on his hoods until he submits and departs, sparing him at his wives' plea _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Kāliya)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (tell-a-tale, Kaliya Daman; Wikipedia)
- **Kṛṣṇa masters the 64 kalās and 14 vidyās in 64 days** — After slaying Kaṃsa and his upanayana, Kṛṣṇa (with Balarāma) studies under guru Sāndīpani at Avantī/Ujjayinī and masters the 14 vidyās and 64 kalās within 64 days _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sixty-four-kalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.45)
- **Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son as guru-dakṣiṇā** — As guru-dakṣiṇā, Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son from the sea/Yama's realm _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sixty-four-kalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.45)
- **Krishna's life and the Bhagavad Gita** — Krishna slays his tyrant uncle Kamsa, lifts Govardhana hill, and as Arjuna's charioteer at Kurukshetra delivers the Bhagavad Gita; his departure in 3102 BCE marks the start of Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Kamsa, Arjuna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana 10-11; Harivamsa)
- **Balarama's deeds** — Balarama, incarnation of the serpent Shesha and Krishna's elder brother, slays the asuras Dhenuka and Pralamba and drags the Yamuna river with his plow _(actors: Balarama, Dhenuka, Pralamba)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10; Vishnu Purana)
- **Kṛṣṇa destroys Śālva's flying fortress Saubha** — Kṛṣṇa destroys Saubha, the airborne fortress-city of the asura king Śālva, after it attacks Dvārakā _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Śālva)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Vyāsa redacts the Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction** — Vyāsa (Krishna Dvaipayana) arranges and redacts the four Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction (~3102 BCE in the scriptural frame), earning the title Veda-Vyāsa _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/README.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata** — Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata, chronicling the Kuru succession war at Kurukṣetra and containing the Bhagavad Gītā, with Krishna's departure marking the start of Kali Yuga _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/README.md) — (Mahabharata (Vyasa); Itihasa (Wikipedia))
- **The eight Vasus steal Vasiṣṭha's cow Nandinī** — The eight Vasus, led by Prabhāsa at his wife's urging, steal the wish-cow Nandinī from the sage Vasiṣṭha and are cursed to be born among mortals _(actors: Vasus, Prabhāsa, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Sambhava Parva 1.99))
- **Gaṅgā drowns seven Vasu-newborns; the eighth becomes Bhīṣma** — The river-goddess Gaṅgā bears the cursed Vasus by King Śāntanu and drowns the first seven at birth to release them; Śāntanu stays her hand at the eighth, Prabhāsa, who lives on as Bhīṣma _(actors: Gaṅgā, Śāntanu, Prabhāsa, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Arjuna requests the Gita teaching again (Anugita frame)** — After the Kurukshetra war, as Krishna prepares to leave for Dvaraka, Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the supreme teaching of Kurukshetra and begs Krishna to repeat it _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14.16 (Ashvamedhika Parva))
- **Krishna smears color on Radha and the gopis (Holi)** — Krishna playfully smears color on Radha and the gopis in Vrindavan, the devotional origin of Holi's play of colors _(actors: Krishna, Radha, gopis)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila)
- **Krishna declines to repeat the Gita verbatim** — Krishna rebukes Arjuna's lapse and declares he cannot reproduce the original discourse word-for-word since it was uttered in a yogic trance, choosing instead to convey the same truths through an old narrative _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14.16)
- **Krishna speaks the Anugita to Arjuna** — In peacetime after the war, Krishna delivers the Anugita, a jnana-and-Samkhya seminar restating the Gita through embedded ancient stories, within the Ashvamedhika Parva _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14, Anugita (Telang, SBE vol. 8))
- **Yudhishthira performs the Ashvamedha horse-sacrifice** — To expiate the slaughter of the war, Yudhishthira performs the ashvamedha (horse-sacrifice) that gives Book 14 of the Mahabharata its name _(actors: Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva)
- **Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva cursed to become trees** — Kubera's sons Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva are cursed by Nārada to become trees, later liberated by the infant Kṛṣṇa in the yamalārjuna episode _(actors: Nalakūbara, Maṇigrīva, Nārada, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.10)
- **The Yakṣa Praśna and revival of the Pāṇḍavas** — A yakṣa guarding a lake kills the four younger Pāṇḍavas who drink without answering him; Yudhiṣṭhira alone answers the dharma-catechism, and the yakṣa — revealed as Yama-Dharma — restores his brothers to life _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Yama-Dharma, Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Sthūṇa exchanges sex with Śikhaṇḍin** — The yakṣa Sthūṇa compassionately exchanges his sex with Śikhaṇḍinī so she can become male; Kubera curses the exchange permanent, enabling the fall of Bhīṣma _(actors: Sthūṇa, Śikhaṇḍin, Kubera, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva)
- **Astika halts Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (Nag Panchami)** — The sage Astika stops King Janamejaya's sarpa-satra and saves the serpent race, the Adi Parva frame-story commemorated at Nag Panchami _(actors: Astika, Janamejaya)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya** — Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna, recalled in western Nag Panchami strands _(actors: Krishna, Kaliya)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila)
- **Birth of Krishna (Janmashtami)** — Krishna, the 8th avatar, is born at midnight in Mathura's prison to Devaki and Vasudeva, commemorated by Krishna Janmashtami _(actors: Krishna, Devaki, Vasudeva)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill (Govardhan Puja)** — Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill on one finger to shelter Vrindavan from Indra's rains, teaching worship of nature over Indra; commemorated as Annakut _(actors: Krishna, Indra)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata to Ganesha** — Ganesha serves as scribe to whom Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata, invoked at Ganesh Chaturthi as lord of letters and beginnings _(actors: Vyasa, Ganesha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata tradition)
- **Bhishma chooses death at Uttarayana (Makar Sankranti)** — Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows with the boon of icchamrityu, waits for Uttarayana before releasing his life, commemorated at Makar Sankranti _(actors: Bhishma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
- **Draupadi binds her sari on Krishna's finger** — Draupadi binds her torn sari on Krishna's bleeding finger and he vows lifelong protection, repaid at the vastra-haran; a Raksha Bandhan charter _(actors: Draupadi, Krishna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Sabha Parva)
- **Krishna speaks the Gita on Mokshada Ekadashi** — Vaikuntha/Mokshada Ekadashi marks the day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken by Krishna to Arjuna _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Bhagavad Gita tradition)
- **Birth of Vyasa / division of the Veda (Guru Purnima)** — Guru Purnima honors the birth and Veda-division day of Veda Vyasa, the Adi Guru who split the one Veda into four and composed the Mahabharata and Puranas _(actors: Veda Vyasa)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Vyasa tradition)

## Kali Yuga — Scriptural & Prophetic  ·  139 events

*Dharma on one leg. The current age (from 3102 BCE) and its prophesied end with Kalki.*

- **Bhīma's unforgiving taunt drives the elders to renounce** — During fifteen years of concord, Bhīma alone cannot forgive and openly boasts of slaying the Kaurava sons and drinking Duḥśāsana's blood, wounding Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī and pushing them toward renunciation _(actors: Bhīma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Ashramavasa))
- **Coronation of Parīkṣit at Hastināpura** — Renouncing the throne, Yudhiṣṭhira installs Parīkṣit, the lone Kuru heir revived by Kṛṣṇa in the womb, as King of Hastināpura with Kṛpa as his preceptor, and leaves Yuyutsu as regent _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Parīkṣit, Kṛpa, Yuyutsu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Founding of the Four Vaishnava Sampradayas** — To anchor valid initiation in Kali Yuga, four authorized disciplic lines are inaugurated by Shri, Brahma, Rudra and the Kumaras, whose acharyas are prophesied to appear at Purushottama-kshetra _(actors: Shri/Lakshmi, Brahma, Rudra, the four Kumaras)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Padma Purana (attributed); Prameya-ratnavali)
- **Kali Yuga Begins** — Kali Yuga starts at 3102 BCE the moment Kali fully enters, reckoned from Krishna's departure from earth _(actors: Kali (personified age), Krishna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36, Vishnu Purana 5.38, Surya Siddhanta 1.15-20)
- **Naciketas Questions His Father's Gift** — Watching his father give away useless cattle, the boy Naciketas asks three times to whom he himself will be given _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Naciketas sent to the house of Death** — Vājaśravasa angrily gives his son Naciketas to Yama; the boy waits three nights and is granted three boons _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.11.8)
- **Narada chides Vyasa, Bhagavata composed** — Despondent after compiling the Vedas and Mahabharata, Vyasa is told by Narada to glorify Hari directly, and so composes the Bhagavata Purana _(actors: Vyasa, Narada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.5-7)
- **Onset of Kali Yuga** — Kali Yuga begins at midnight 17/18 February 3102 BCE, the moment of Krishna's departure, when the bull of Dharma is reduced to standing on one leg _(actors: Krishna, Kali (personified))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Surya Siddhanta; Vishnu Purana 5.38; Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36)
- **Story of Uttanka and the snake-sacrifice trigger** — Uttanka's quest for his guru's wife's earrings and duel with Takshaka leads him to urge Janamejaya to the snake-sacrifice, the hinge that triggers the epic's recitation _(actors: Uttanka, Takshaka, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Paushya Parva)
- **Sundarar Claimed as Bondsman at Tiruvennainallur** — At Tiruvennainallur, Shiva claims the saint Sundarar as his bondsman (the tozhan episode), beginning Sundarar's career _(actors: Shiva, Sundarar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **The Jagannātha Triad and Sudarśana Pillar** — Purī's sanctum holds the abstract wooden busts of Jagannātha (Kṛṣṇa), Balabhadra, Subhadrā and the Sudarśana post — deliberately armless and unfinished _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā, Sudarśana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-kṣetra Māhātmya); Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Viṣṇu's Kali-yuga refuge promise on Veṅkaṭa hill** — At the dawn of Kali-yuga Viṣṇu agrees to remain standing and visible on the Seven Hills so the merit-poor may win liberation by darśana alone, making Tirumala Bhū-Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Viṣṇu/Śrīnivāsa, the sages)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya (Varāha/Bhaviṣyottara/Skanda Purāṇa))
- **Vyāsa composes the Purāṇas, recited by the Sūta at Naimiṣa** — All 18 Mahāpurāṇas and 18 Upapurāṇas are ascribed to Vyāsa and recited by the sūta Ugraśravas/Romaharṣaṇa to the sages at the Naimiṣa forest in this Kali Yuga _(actors: Vyāsa, Ugraśravas, Romaharṣaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/README.md) — (Purāṇa frame-story)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira finds Duryodhana enthroned in heaven** — Carried to Svarga, Yudhiṣṭhira sees his arch-enemy Duryodhana enthroned in glory; he recoils, but Nārada explains that earthly hatred ceases in heaven and Duryodhana earned the seat by dying bravely on the field of Kurukṣetra _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Duryodhana, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.1)
- **Dharma Bull Stands on One Leg** — With Kali's onset only one quarter of virtue remains; Earth and Dharma lament as cow and bull _(actors: Dharma (bull), Earth (cow))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.16-17, Manusmriti 1.81-86)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī depart for the forest** — Grief-worn, the blind king and Gāndhārī take leave to retire as vānaprasthas; to the Pāṇḍavas' shock Kuntī chooses to accompany them, and the elders cast off royal robes for bark and deerskin at Vyāsa's hermitage on the Gaṅgā _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15)
- **End of the Barhadratha line** — The last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son, beginning the prophesied Kali dynasties of Magadha _(actors: Puranjaya, Shunaka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.2-3)
- **Indradyumna founds the Jagannath deities** — King Indradyumna, instructed in a dream, recovers Krishna's imperishable remains (a sacred daru log washed ashore) and has Vishvakarma carve the three stub-armed deities from neem wood, the carving left unfinished _(actors: Indradyumna, Vishvakarma, Krishna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Skanda Purana)
- **King Indradyumna's Quest for Nīla Mādhava** — The pious king Indradyumna seeks the hidden forest form of Viṣṇu, Nīla Mādhava, and sends Brahmins to find it _(actors: Indradyumna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-kṣetra Māhātmya))
- **Naciketas Consigned to Death** — Provoked, the father angrily declares 'To Death I give you,' and the boy must go to Yama's house _(actors: Vājaśravasa, Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.4; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Naciketas demands the secret of death from Yama** — Rejecting all worldly bribes, Naciketas holds firm to his third boon and Yama teaches him the deathless Self, śreyas/preyas, OM and yoga _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1–2.6)
- **Parikshit Cursed by Shringi** — Abhimanyu's son Parikshit, last of the Kuru line, garlands a meditating sage with a dead snake and the sage's son curses him to die of Takshaka's bite in seven days, occasioning the Bhagavata's recitation _(actors: Parikshit, Shringi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.18-19)
- **Shiva Grants Sundarar the Padikasu at Tiruvarur** — Shiva grants Sundarar a daily gold coin (padikasu) at the Tiruvarur Thyagaraja temple, dramatizing his intimate friend-of-Shiva status _(actors: Shiva, Sundarar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam; Tevaram)
- **Suta recites Bhagavata at Naimisa** — The bard Ugrasrava (Suta Gosvami) recites the entire Bhagavata to the sages of the Naimisa forest during Kali Yuga, opening the outer frame _(actors: Ugrasrava/Suta, Naimisa sages)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1)
- **The 28 Yogeshvaras incarnate to teach Pashupata-yoga** — Shiva incarnates once in every Kali Yuga across the 28 mahayugas of the present manvantara as the 28 Yogeshvaras, each with four disciples, transmitting the yoga of liberation _(actors: Shiva (Pashupati), the 28 Yogeshvaras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (ch. 24))
- **Ugraśravas Sauti recites the epic at Naimiṣa Forest** — The bard Ugraśravas arrives at the Naimiṣa Forest where ṛṣis led by Śaunaka perform a 12-year sacrifice and recites the whole Mahābhārata as he heard it at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (the outer frame narrative) _(actors: Ugraśravas Sauti, Śaunaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/README.md) — (Mahabharata 1 (Adi Parva))
- **Vajra crowned at Indraprastha** — Yudhiṣṭhira enthrones Vajra, the surviving Yādava prince and great-grandson of Kṛṣṇa, over Indraprastha and the Śūrasena lands, preserving the Yādava line after the Mausala fratricide _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Vajra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Varāha's prior ownership of the hill** — Varāha already owns Veṅkaṭa hill from a prior age; Śrīnivāsa must ask his leave to settle and ordains Varāha's darśana be taken first _(actors: Varāha (Viṣṇu boar-avatāra), Śrīnivāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira descends into hell and chooses to remain** — Led down a foul path through the iron-thorned hells (Asipatravana, Vaitaraṇī), Yudhiṣṭhira hears the agonized voices of his brothers, Karṇa and Draupadī and, declaring his presence eases their suffering, resolves to stay in hell with them rather than enjoy heaven with their tormentors _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Karṇa, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.2)
- **Astika halts the snake-sacrifice** — Janamejaya's serpent-sacrifice burns thousands of Nagas until the boy-brahmin Astika wins a boon and halts the rite, the frame at which the epic is recited _(actors: Janamejaya, Astika, Takshaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Astika Parva)
- **Birth of Sambandar at Sirkazhi** — The child-prodigy saint Sambandar, largest contributor of pathigams to the Tevaram canon, is born at Sirkazhi (Brahmapureeswarar) _(actors: Sambandar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam / Tevaram)
- **Chanakya uproots the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta** — A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) uproots the Nanda dynasty and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty in the Puranic king-prophecy _(actors: Chanakya, Chandragupta, the Nandas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.12; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Lakulisha as the 28th avatara founds the Pashupata sect** — Shiva descends at Kayavarohana as the wandering ascetic Lakulisha, the 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples Kushika, Garga, Mitra, and Kaurushya who spread the Pashupata cult _(actors: Shiva (Lakulisha), Kushika, Garga, Mitra, Kaurushya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (ch. 24); Vayu; Kurma)
- **Markandeya's Kali Prophecy** — Sage Markandeya foretells the apocalyptic decline of Kali: mleccha kings, 16-year lifespans, cannibalism, barren earth _(actors: Markandeya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 188-190)
- **Naciketas Waits Three Nights in Yama's House** — Yama being absent, Naciketas waits three nights unfed; to atone for the un-hosted guest Yama grants three boons _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.7-9; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Self-manifestation of the Mūla-virāṭ mūrti** — The standing four-armed Veṅkaṭeśvara image arises svayam-vyakta, not carved by human hands, with Śrī resting on his chest; later fixed as Viṣṇu by Rāmānuja _(actors: Veṅkaṭeśvara, Lakṣmī, Rāmānuja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya; Vaiṣṇava tradition)
- **Shrinivasa Weds Padmavati at Tirumala** — Vishnu as Shrinivasa dwells in a termite-mound on Venkata hill, meets Padmavati (reborn Lakshmi) while hunting, and weds her, founding the Tirumala-Tirupati cult _(actors: Vishnu-Shrinivasa, Padmavati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Venkatacala-Mahatmya)
- **The hell dissolves as māyā; the final test passed** — At Yudhiṣṭhira's choice Indra, Yama and the gods appear and the hell instantly vanishes as illusion; Dharma reveals this was the third and last trial, explains that all must briefly taste hell to exhaust residual karma (his caused by the half-lie about Aśvatthāmā), and Yudhiṣṭhira bathes in the celestial Ganges to shed his human body _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Yama/Dharma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.3)
- **The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī begin the mahāprasthāna** — After final rites and distribution of wealth, the five brothers and Draupadī cast off royalty for ascetic garb and set out walking north toward death with no intention of return, a faithful dog attaching itself to the company _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, the dog)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Uttaṅka incites Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice** — Uttaṅka's grudge against Takṣaka goads King Janamejaya into the sarpa-satra, the frame at which the Mahābhārata is first recited _(actors: Uttaṅka, Janamejaya, Takṣaka, Āstīka, Vaiśampāyana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Vaiśampāyana narrates the epic at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice** — At King Janamejaya's Sarpa Satra, held to avenge his father Parīkṣit's death by the serpent Takṣaka, Vyāsa's pupil Vaiśampāyana narrates the Mahābhārata at Vyāsa's bidding (the middle frame narrative) _(actors: Vaiśampāyana, Janamejaya, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/README.md) — (Mahabharata 1 (Adi Parva))
- **Vidura merges into Yudhiṣṭhira and dies** — Found wasted by tapas, Vidura by yogic power casts his life-breaths and being into Yudhiṣṭhira's body and drops dead, the two merged because both are portions of Dharma; Vyāsa forbids cremating his body and explains the Aṇī-Māṇḍavya curse that made Dharma born as Vidura _(actors: Vidura, Yudhiṣṭhira, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Ashramavasa))
- **Vidyāpati, Viśvāvasu and the Mustard-Seed Trail** — The Brahmin Vidyāpati finds Nīla Mādhava worshipped by the Śabara chief Viśvāvasu, marries his daughter Lalitā, and traces the secret path with mustard seeds _(actors: Vidyāpati, Viśvāvasu, Lalitā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Appar Reconverts from Jainism to Shaivism** — Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), formerly the Jain Dharmasena, reconverts to Shaivism and composes Tirumurai 4–6, famed for his hoe-service temple cleaning _(actors: Appar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam / Tevaram)
- **Arjuna surrenders the Gāṇḍīva to Agni** — At the red-watered sea Agni appears blocking the path and demands Arjuna return the celestial bow Gāṇḍīva and quivers to Varuṇa; Arjuna casts them into the waters, formally ending the kṣatriya phase of their lives _(actors: Arjuna, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Bhṛgu's kick and Lakṣmī's departure from Vaikuṇṭha** — Sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in a test; affronted that her seat was struck, Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha and descends to earth _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **First Boon — A Reconciled Father** — Naciketas asks that his father be freed of anger and welcome him gladly on his return, and Yama grants it _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.10-11)
- **Nama-Sankirtana — Kali's One Virtue** — Though an ocean of faults, Kali offers liberation through mere chanting of God's name, hard-won in earlier ages _(actors: Vyasa/Shuka (narrators))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.3.51-52, Vishnu Purana 6.2)
- **Shrinivasa Borrows Wedding Wealth from Kubera** — To pay the bride-price Shrinivasa borrows immense wealth from the treasurer-god Kubera, a perpetual divine debt that devotees' Tirumala offerings repay _(actors: Shrinivasa, Kubera)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Venkatacala-Mahatmya)
- **The heroes reunited and dissolved into their source deities** — In his new divine body Yudhiṣṭhira beholds each hero returned to source: Bhīma to the Maruts, Arjuna among Indra's host (as Nara), Nakula and Sahadeva to the Aśvins, Draupadī as Śrī/Lakṣmī, Karṇa into Sūrya, Bhīṣma to the Vasus, Droṇa into Bṛhaspati, Abhimanyu to Soma, and Kṛṣṇa beheld in his supreme Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa form _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, Karṇa, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Abhimanyu, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.4-5)
- **The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste** — The prophesied king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, shows no reverence to Vedas or brahmanas, and reduces the twice-born to outcaste status — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy _(actors: Vishvasphurji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **The Vanished Deity and the Floating Dāru-brahma** — Nīla Mādhava disappears into the sand before the king arrives; a divine voice promises return as a fragrant log (Dāru-brahma) that washes ashore at Purī _(actors: Nīla Mādhava, Indradyumna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama Māhātmya))
- **Vyāsa raises the slain warriors from the Gaṅgā for one night** — At Gāndhārī's and Kuntī's plea, Vyāsa by ascetic power calls up all the slain warriors of both armies from the river for one reconciled night with the living; Dhṛtarāṣṭra is granted celestial sight to behold his hundred sons, and at dawn the dead re-enter the Gaṅgā _(actors: Vyāsa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the slain warriors)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Putradarshana))
- **Avatara of Dhumraketu** — Ganesha will descend as the smoke-colored horse-mounted Dhumraketu at the end of Kali Yuga to destroy the wicked mleccha hordes, a Ganapatya parallel to Kalki _(actors: Ganesha (Dhumraketu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda))
- **Barhadratha Line Ends** — Last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son _(actors: Puranjaya/Ripunjaya, Shunaka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.2-3)
- **Descent of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Closing-Age Teacher)** — In Gaudiya tradition the next descent after Krishna in this Mahayuga is Chaitanya Mahaprabhu within the present Kali Yuga, propagating the nama-sankirtana yuga-dharma _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.5.32; Chaitanya Charitamrita)
- **Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa Darśana to Janamejaya** — Viṣṇu as Kṛṣṇa the Pāṇḍava-envoy grants the cosmic-form darśana to king Janamejaya, commemorated at the Pāṇḍava Dūta temple of Kāñcī _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (divyadesam.com)
- **Śrīnivāsa's descent and the anthill austerity** — Viṣṇu follows Lakṣmī to earth as Śrīnivāsa and dwells in austerity on Veṅkaṭa hill, in some tellings nursed within an anthill _(actors: Śrīnivāsa (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Sambandar's Confrontation with the Jains at Madurai** — At the Meenakshi/Madurai shrine, Sambandar confronts the Jains in the legends focused on the Pandya capital _(actors: Sambandar, Jains)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **Second Boon — The Nāciketa Fire** — Naciketas asks the heavenward fire-sacrifice; Yama expounds the Nāciketa fire-altar, names it after the boy, and adds a necklace _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.12-19; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **The epic closes with its phala-śruti** — The book declares Vyāsa composed a six-million-verse poem distributed across the worlds, proclaims the merit of reciting the Mahābhārata, and gives the closing self-praise that what is here is found elsewhere and what is not here is nowhere, with benediction to Nārāyaṇa, Nara and Sarasvatī _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.5)
- **The five fall one by one on the slopes of Meru** — As they cross the high snow, Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, and Bhīma each fall in turn, Yudhiṣṭhira naming the single fault (partiality, pride in wisdom, vanity of beauty, arrogance in prowess, gluttony and boasting) that bars each from bodily ascent, never looking back _(actors: Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.2)
- **The Hidden Carpenter and the Unfinished Images** — Viśvakarmā (or Ananta-mahārāṇā) carves the log behind locked doors; the door is opened early, leaving Jagannātha armless and unfinished, and Brahmā consecrates the temple _(actors: Viśvakarmā / Ananta-mahārāṇā, Indradyumna, Guṇḍicā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **War-widows enter the Gaṅgā to rejoin their husbands** — Vyāsa tells the widows that any who wish to rejoin their dead husbands may enter the river; women who do so cast off their bodies in the Gaṅgā and ascend to their husbands' worlds _(actors: Vyāsa, the war-widows)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Putradarshana))
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī die in the forest fire** — After two more years of harsh tapas, a wildfire sweeps the wood; too weak to flee, the three elders choose not to escape and the blind king sits in yoga as the flames take all three; Nārada announces their deaths to Yudhiṣṭhira _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **Gokarna-Dhundhukari ghost-liberation (Bhagavata-Mahatmya)** — The allegory of Bhakti as a mother with sons Jnana and Vairagya, with the ghost Dhundhukari liberated by recitation of the Bhagavata _(actors: Gokarna, Dhundhukari, Bhakti, Jnana, Vairagya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Uttara Khanda, Bhagavata-Mahatmya))
- **King Indradyumna founds the Jagannātha cult at Puri** — King Indradyumna recovers the divine dāru-brahman image, which Viśvakarmā carves into the Jagannātha–Balabhadra–Subhadrā triad at Puruṣottama-kṣetra (Puri) _(actors: Indradyumna, Viśvakarmā, Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-māhātmya); Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Marriage of Śrīnivāsa and Padmāvatī** — Śrīnivāsa falls in love with and marries Padmāvatī (Alamēlu-maṅgā), lotus-born daughter of King Ākāśarāja and a form of Lakṣmī, enshrined at Tiruchanūr _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Padmāvatī, King Ākāśarāja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Nabakalebara — Periodic Re-embodiment** — The perishable wooden images are periodically replaced and the secret Brahma-padārtha life-essence transferred; historical rites span 1969–2015 _(actors: Jagannātha triad, Dayitāpati priests)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (temple tradition / sthala-purāṇa; academic record)
- **Nanda Dynasty — Exterminator of Kshatriyas** — Mahapadma Nanda, born of a shudra woman, founds the first non-kshatriya empire, styled 'exterminator of all kshatriyas' _(actors: Mahapadma Nanda, Mahanandi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.10-11)
- **Prophesied Descent of Kalki** — Vishnu is prophesied to descend as Kalki at the end of Kali Yuga to end the age of strife and restore Satya Yuga _(actors: Vishnu; Kalki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2)
- **Takṣaka Slays King Parīkṣit** — The serpent-chief Takṣaka, having been cursed-upon by Śṛṅgin's word against Parīkṣit, slays the king with his venom on the seventh day, triggering Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Takṣaka, Parīkṣit, Śṛṅgin)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **The dog reveals himself as Dharma and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends in the body** — Indra offers to carry Yudhiṣṭhira to Svarga but forbids the dog; Yudhiṣṭhira refuses to abandon the faithful creature, whereupon the dog reveals himself as Dharma (his divine father) who praises his compassion, and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends to heaven in his living mortal body, an unprecedented feat _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, the dog (Dharma))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.3)
- **Third Boon — The Secret of Death Requested** — Naciketas asks the great doubt of whether a man exists after death, the Upaniṣad's metaphysical innovation _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.20)
- **Andal Composes the Tiruppavai at Srivilliputhur** — Andal (Goda) is born at Srivilliputhur, birthplace also of Periyalvar, where the Tiruppavai originates _(actors: Andal, Periyalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham / Alvar hagiography)
- **Chanakya Uproots the Nandas** — A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) overthrows the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty _(actors: Chanakya/Kautilya, Chandragupta Maurya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.12)
- **Janamejaya's Sarpa-Satra (Snake-Sacrifice)** — Janamejaya vows to exterminate the serpent race and undertakes the sarpa-satra, whose oblations draw nāgas of every size from across the worlds into the flames _(actors: Janamejaya, nāgas, Takṣaka)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīka Parva)
- **Kaṇṇappa's Eye-Offering at Srikalahasti** — The hunter-saint Kannappa, worshipping the linga his untaught way, gouges out his own eyes to stop the linga's bleeding eye; Shiva seizes his hand, restores his eyes and grants liberation, proving devotion outranks ritual _(actors: Kannappa (Tinnan), Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Periya Purana (Kannappa Nayanar Puranam))
- **Kubera's wedding-loan to Śrīnivāsa** — To meet bridal expenses Śrīnivāsa borrows a vast sum from Kubera, vowing repayment with interest through all of Kali-yuga — the basis of the temple hundi donations _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Kubera)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Lakulisha prophecy, last of the 28 Yogeshvaras** — The Purana prophesies Maheshvara descending in Kali Yuga as the ascetic Lakulisha, 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples who found the Pashupata sect _(actors: Shiva (Lakulisha), Kushika, Garga, Mitra, Kaurushya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (ch. 53))
- **Sañjaya escapes the fire and departs for the Himālaya** — Before the fire closes in, Dhṛtarāṣṭra orders his faithful charioteer Sañjaya to save himself; bereft of his master, Sañjaya retires to the Himālaya to perform penance and is never heard of again _(actors: Sañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **The Ratha Yātrā Chariot Festival** — On Āṣāḍha dvitīyā the triad rides three giant chariots (Nandighoṣa, Tāḷadhvaja, Darpadalana) to the Guṇḍicā temple; the Gajapati king performs Chera Paṅharā _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā, Gajapati king)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa māhātmya layer; temple tradition)
- **Yama Tests Naciketas with Bribes** — Yama offers sons, cattle, gold, lands, long life and celestial maidens instead, but Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds to the third boon _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.21-29)
- **Birth of Nammalvar at Azhwarthirunagari** — Nammalvar (Maran/Satakopan), foremost of the Alvars who sang the most Divya Desams, is born at Tirukkurugur/Azhwarthirunagari _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Alvar hagiography)
- **Śrīnivāsa remains bodily on the hill** — Bound by marriage and debt, Śrīnivāsa stays on Tirumala rather than returning to Vaikuṇṭha, grounding the Kali-yuga refuge promise _(actors: Śrīnivāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Āstīka Halts the Snake-Sacrifice** — Vāsuki sends his nephew Āstīka, who praises the sacrifice so eloquently that Janamejaya grants a boon to cease it, sparing Takṣaka and the surviving nāgas and ending the enmity _(actors: Āstīka, Vāsuki, Janamejaya, Takṣaka)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīka Parva)
- **Vishvasphurji Abolishes Caste** — The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, scorns Vedas and brahmanas — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy _(actors: Vishvasphurji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1, Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Yama Teaches the Knowledge of the Self** — Yama discloses śreyas vs preyas, the unborn Self, OM, the chariot of the body, and yoga as steadiness of the senses _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.2-2.6)
- **Naciketas Attains Brahman** — Having received the knowledge of the Self and the whole rule of yoga from Death, Naciketas becomes free of passion and death and attains Brahman _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 2.6.18)
- **Vaiśampāyana First Recites the Mahābhārata** — At Janamejaya's sarpa-satra, Vaiśampāyana, pupil of Vyāsa, first recites the Mahābhārata to the king — the epic's outermost narrative frame _(actors: Vaiśampāyana, Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata)
- **Arjuna's Gandiva fails against the Abhira robbers** — Escorting the Yadava column, Arjuna is ambushed by Abhira bandits and finds his strength gone, unable to string Gandiva or summon his astras; the widows are carried off and the loss of his invincibility signals the divine age has closed _(actors: Arjuna, Abhira robbers, the Yadava widows)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.7-8)
- **The First Three Alvars Meet at Tirukkovilur** — The first three (Mudhal) Alvars — Poigai, Bhutha, and Pey — meet in a storm-narrowed corridor at Tirukkovilur, where the Iyarpa Prabandham begins _(actors: Poigai Alvar, Bhutha Alvar, Pey Alvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Alvar hagiography / Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **The Kali-yuga king-list prophecy** — Parashara prophesies the post-Parikshit dynasties of Magadha (Pradyotas, Shaishunagas, Nandas, Mauryas, Shungas, Kanvas, Andhras) and foretells the rise of mleccha and low-born kings _(actors: Parashara, Parikshit)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 4, ch. 24); cf. Bhagavata 12)
- **Venkateshvara's marriage to Padmavati and loan from Kubera** — The self-manifest Venkateshvara (Balaji/Srinivasa) of Tirumala marries Padmavati and takes a loan from Kubera, the founding legend of the Tirupati shrine _(actors: Venkateshvara, Padmavati, Kubera)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Vaishnava-khanda, Venkatachala-mahatmya))
- **Vishnu Stands on Pundalika's Brick at Pandharpur** — While serving his parents, the reformed son Pundalika tosses a brick for the arriving Vishnu to wait upon; pleased, the Lord stays standing on the brick as Vitthala _(actors: Pundalika, Vishnu/Krishna-Vitthala)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Skanda & Padma Purana Panduranga-mahatmyas)
- **Vyāsa recounts the 108 Śakti Pīṭhas** — Vyāsa recounts to Janamejaya 108 seats of the Goddess with their locations and the local form of the Devī at each — the most-cited Purāṇic pīṭha-list _(actors: Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha VII)
- **Disputed canonical status — the Vāyu/Śiva seat** — Vāyu is counted among the 18 Mahāpurāṇas by Matsya/Bhāgavata lists but replaced by the Śiva Purāṇa in others; al-Bīrūnī already recorded the two rival lists _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Purāṇic concordances [scholarly]; smriti-puranas survey)
- **Vajra installed as king at Indraprastha** — Arjuna reaches Kurukshetra with a remnant and installs Krishna's grandson Vajra as king at Indraprastha, preserving the Yadava line _(actors: Arjuna, Vajra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.8)
- **Vajranabha Re-founds Dvaraka Worship** — Krishna's lineage through Aniruddha and Vajra is credited with re-founding worship and raising the original Hari-griha shrine after the city's submergence _(actors: Vajranabha, Aniruddha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Skanda Purana, Dvaraka-mahatmya)
- **Astika halts the sarpa-satra and the Mahabharata is recited** — The young brahmana Astika stops Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, sparing Takshaka, and it is at this sattra that Vaishampayana first recites the Mahabharata _(actors: Astika, Janamejaya, Takshaka, Vaishampayana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Astika Parva)
- **The Great Departure and the test of the dog** — After Kṛṣṇa's death Yudhiṣṭhira crowns Parikṣit and journeys north; his companions fall one by one, and he refuses Indra's heaven rather than abandon a faithful dog who proves to be Dharma _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Dharma/Yama, a dog)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Mahāprasthānika Parva)
- **Vyāsa counsels the Pāṇḍavas to renounce the kingdom** — The grief-stricken Arjuna goes to Vyāsa, who explains all happened by destiny and the ripening of curses, and counsels that the heroes' age is over and the time has come for the Pāṇḍavas to renounce and depart _(actors: Vyāsa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.8-9)
- **Kali-Yuga prophecy (Bhaviṣya Parva)** — The Bhaviṣya Parva forecasts the degenerate age to come — the moral and social decline of Kali Yuga, beginning by tradition at Krishna's departure → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Bhaviṣya Parva)
- **Kalki's Epic Wars and Reign (Kalki Purana)** — Kalki marries Padma and Rama, wars against Koka and Vikoka, defeats the demon Kali personified, then reigns and ascends _(actors: Kalki, Padma, Rama, Koka, Vikoka, Kali (demon))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Kalki Purana)
- **The final test of heaven and hell** — Seeing Duryodhana in heaven and his loved ones in hell, Yudhiṣṭhira chooses to remain in Naraka with them; the illusion lifts, he sheds his body in the celestial Gaṅgā, and is reunited in true Svarga _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Dharma/Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Svargārohaṇa Parva)
- **Kali Yuga prophecy of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa** — The Viṣṇu Purāṇa closes its king-lists with a famed prophecy of the moral decline of Kali Yuga → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Book 4)
- **Bhima's Fall on the Great Departure** — On the final Himalayan march Bhima falls, his flaw named as gluttony and pride in his strength _(actors: Bhima, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva)
- **The Dharma Daivas Appear at Birmanna Pergade's House** — Four guardian spirits of Dharma test and are pleased by the Jain chieftain Birmanna Pergade's hospitality, then ask him in a dream to dedicate his home to their worship, founding Dharmasthala _(actors: Kalarahu, Kalarkayi, Kumarasvami, Kanyakumari, Birmanna Pergade)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Dharmasthala daiva legend)
- **Arjuna Returns Gandiva to the Waters** — After Krishna's death, his powers gone, Arjuna casts Gandiva back into Varuna's waters on the final journey and ascends north toward Svarga _(actors: Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva)
- **Birth of Hariharaputra (Shiva + Mohini)** — After the Samudra Manthana, Vishnu reassumes the Mohini form for Shiva, and from their union the divine child Sasta/Ayyappa is born, deliberately to produce the being able to slay the demoness Mahishi _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu-as-Mohini, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Brahmanda Purana, Bhutanatha Upakhyana; Bhagavata Purana 8; Keralan tradition)
- **Mahishi's boon of unslayability** — The buffalo-demoness Mahishi, sister of Mahishasura, does penance and Brahma grants that she can be killed only by a being born of both Vishnu and Shiva — the engine of Ayyappa's birth _(actors: Mahishi, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Pandalam/Keralan legend)
- **The infant Ayyappa left on the Pampa** — The divine child is left on the banks of the Pampa river with a golden bell at his neck, to be found and adopted as Manikandan by the childless King Rajashekhara of Pandalam _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, King Rajashekhara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan Pandalam legend)
- **The tiger's-milk plot against Manikandan** — Resentful of the favored foundling, the queen feigns an illness curable only by tigress's milk, sending Manikandan on a seemingly fatal forest errand _(actors: Manikandan, the queen, the Diwan)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan Pandalam legend)
- **Ayyappa slays Mahishi** — In the forest Manikandan confronts and kills the demoness Mahishi (often on the Azhutha river), fulfilling his cosmic mission; her death-dance is commemorated _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, Mahishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Janamejaya's Snake-Sacrifice** — Avenging his father Parikshit, killed by Takshaka, Janamejaya holds the sarpasatra, the occasion at which the Mahabharata is first recited by Vaishampayana _(actors: Janamejaya, Takshaka, Vaishampayana)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Ayyappa returns riding a tiger** — Manikandan returns to Pandalam astride a tiger (Indra and the devas in tiger-forms), revealing his divinity and fulfilling the milk-errand _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Kali Yuga begins (3102 BCE)** — The Age of Strife begins at Krishna's departure with dharma on a single leg; chanting the divine name becomes the prescribed yuga-dharma _(actors: Krishna, humanity)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Surya Siddhanta, Bhagavata Purana 12.2-3)
- **Founding of the Sabarimala shrine** — Ayyappa shoots an arrow and ordains a temple be built where it lands — at Sabari, where the Ramayana ascetic Sabari awaited Rama — then merges into the deity-form _(actors: Ayyappa, King Rajashekhara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Onset of Kali Yuga, Parikṣit restrains personified Kali** — Kali Yuga formally begins as Kṛṣṇa leaves the earth (traditionally 3102 BCE); Parikṣit confronts and restrains a personified Kali _(actors: Parikṣit, Kali)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.16-17)
- **Curse of Leela into demonic form** — The celestial woman Leela is cursed to buffalo/demonic form (becoming Mahishi) after refusing to return to the divine realm with sage Dattatreya, and is freed upon her death at Ayyappa's hands _(actors: Leela, Dattatreya, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan supplementary tradition)
- **Parikṣit cursed to die in seven days** — Parikṣit is cursed by the boy-brahmana Sṛṅgi to die in seven days by the snake Takṣaka, the dramatic engine for the rest of the Bhagavata _(actors: Parikṣit, Sṛṅgi, Takṣaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1)
- **Malikappurathamma's deferred marriage proposal** — The goddess Malikappurathamma wishes to marry Ayyappa, who replies he will wed her only when no first-time pilgrim comes to Sabarimala — forever deferring the marriage and preserving his celibacy _(actors: Malikappurathamma, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Suka teaches Parikṣit on the Ganga** — Sukadeva Gosvami speaks the bulk of the Bhagavata to King Parikṣit on the bank of the Ganga during the seven days before his death _(actors: Sukadeva, Parikṣit)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2-12)
- **The great departure of the Pāṇḍavas** — The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī walk toward Mount Meru and fall one by one; only Yudhiṣṭhira and a dog (Dharma in disguise) reach heaven's gate _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī, Dharma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Mahābhārata 17 (Mahāprasthānika Parva))
- **Ayyappa defeats the bandit Udayanan** — Aided by his companion Vavar and local forces, Ayyappa defeats the forest robber-chief Udayanan _(actors: Ayyappa, Vavar, Udayanan)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan temple/pilgrimage tradition)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira's heaven-test and ascension** — Yudhiṣṭhira is tested by an illusion of his kin in hell/heaven, then reconciled, and the heroes attain their celestial states _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Mahābhārata 18 (Svargārohaṇa Parva))
- **Ugrashravas recites the Mahabharata to the Naimisha sages** — The outermost frame of the Gita is Ugrashravas' recitation of the epic to the sages of the Naimisha forest, nesting Vaishampayana's and Sanjaya's reports within it _(actors: Ugrashravas, Naimisha sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/README.md) — (Mahabharata frame narrative)
- **Future-dynasty prophecy** — Suka foretells the post-Mahabharata kings (Magadha, Nanda, Maurya, Sunga, Andhra) down into Kali in the prophetic past tense _(actors: Sukadeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12)
- **Death of Parikshit by Takshaka** — King Parikshit fearlessly meets death by the serpent Takshaka's bite, closing the frame, followed by Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Parikshit, Takshaka, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.5-6)
- **Manu's law-code narrated to the sages** — The Manava-Dharmasastra (Laws of Manu) is narrated by Manu to the sages, codifying dharma, varna, and ashrama for the current age _(actors: Manu, sages)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/agamas-tantras-dharmashastras.md) — (Manusmṛti)
- **The Pandavas' Great Departure (Mahaprasthana)** — Hearing of Krishna's death, the Pandavas crown Parikshit and walk north toward the Himalayas, all dying on the way except Yudhishthira, who ascends to heaven with a dog who is Dharma in disguise _(actors: the Pandavas, Parikshit, Yudhishthira, Dharma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mahaprasthanika and Svargarohana Parvas)
- **Kalki avatara ends Kali Yuga** — Kali Yuga closes with the Kalki avatara, who destroys adharma and ushers in a new Satya Yuga, restarting the Mahayuga _(actors: Kalki)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2; Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Śeṣa incarnates as Patañjali** — Ādiśeṣa takes birth as the sage Patañjali, falling as a tiny serpent into the cupped hands of his mother Goṇikā, to witness Śiva's Tāṇḍava and honour him as first teacher of yoga _(actors: Śeṣa, Patañjali, Goṇikā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Vaiṣṇava & Yoga tradition; Patañjali hagiography)
- **Buddha avatar deludes the asuras** — Vishnu descends in ascetic Buddha form, in one reading to delude the asuras away from the Vedic path so the devas can defeat them, and in another to stop Vedic animal sacrifice out of compassion _(actors: Buddha (Vishnu), the asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24; Vishnu Purana 3.17-18; Gita Govinda)
- **Jīmūtavāhana offers his body to Garuḍa** — The compassionate Vidyādhara prince Jīmūtavāhana offers his own body to Garuḍa in place of a Nāga victim, halting Garuḍa's serpent-slaughter _(actors: Jīmūtavāhana, Garuḍa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara; Nāgānanda)
- **Naravāhanadatta consecrated emperor of the Vidyādharas** — The mortal-born prince Naravāhanadatta wins the vidyās and is consecrated Cakravartin emperor of the Vidyādharas across the Kathāsaritsāgara _(actors: Naravāhanadatta)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara)
- **Tulasī Vivāha — annual marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu** — The ceremonial marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu/Śālagrāma is performed each year from Prabodhinī Ekādaśī to Kārttika Pūrṇimā, ending Cāturmāsya and opening the wedding season _(actors: Tulsī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Tulasi in Hinduism (Wikipedia))
- **Vaishampayana recites the Anugita to Janamejaya** — The Anugita reaches the world as Vaishampayana's recitation to King Janamejaya at the snake-sacrifice, reporting the postwar exchange between Krishna and Arjuna _(actors: Vaishampayana, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata)
- **Caṇḍeśa made lord of the gaṇas' provisions** — In the Nāyanār tradition the boy-saint Caṇḍeśa strikes his own father to defend Śiva-worship and is made steward and lord of the gaṇas' provisions _(actors: Caṇḍeśa, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Śaiva Siddhānta)

## Kali Yuga — Documented History  ·  367 events

*The academic/historical timeline (flagged distinct from scripture).*

- **Adi Shankara Organizes the Greater Char Dham** — Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) is traditionally credited with organizing the four pan-India abodes (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram) into one pilgrimage to bind the subcontinent _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Wikipedia, Char Dham)
- **Adi Shankara Renounces as a Boy at Kaladi** — Born at Kaladi to an aged childless couple, the precocious Shankara renounces as a boy after a crocodile seizes his leg, forcing his mother's consent to sannyasa _(actors: Adi Shankara, Aryamba)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Madhaviya Shankara-Digvijaya)
- **Andal Discovered Beneath the Tulasi** — The Alvar Periyalvar finds the infant girl Kodai (Andal) under a tulasi plant in the Srivilliputhur temple garden and raises her in Krishna-devotion, her earth-birth underwriting her Bhu-devi identity _(actors: Periyalvar, Andal)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Andal — Wikipedia)
- **Basava rejects the sacred thread** — As a boy Basava rejects the Brahminical sacred thread (upanayana) in protest at birth-based hierarchy and leaves for Kudalasangama to study, taking Kudalasangamadeva as his form of Shiva _(actors: Basava)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Basava hagiography (traditional))
- **Birth and milk legend of Sambandar** — Born at Sirkazhi to a Brahmin couple, the toddler Sambandar is fed divine milk by Pārvatī from a golden cup and sings his first hymn, earning his name _(actors: Sambandar, Pārvatī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sambandar)
- **Birth of Śaṅkaradeva** — Śrīmanta Śaṅkaradeva, founder of Ekaśaraṇa Dharma, is born into a Bhuyan Kāyastha family at Bordowā/Batadrava in Nagaon, Assam (traditionally 1449) _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Birth of Nammalvar and the subduing of Shatha** — Born Maran to a non-Brahmin Vellalar family, the infant Nammalvar subdues Shatha (the wind afflicting newborns), earning the title Shathakopa, and never cries, eats or speaks _(actors: Nammalvar, Kari, Udaya Nankai)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Nammalvar hagiography (traditional))
