- **Composition of the Kakawin Ramayana** — The oldest major Southeast Asian Rama text is composed in Central Java c. 856-930 CE, modeled on the Sanskrit Bhattikavya rather than Valmiki directly _(actors: Anonymous Old Javanese poet (sometimes ascribed to Yogesvara))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/southeast-asian-ramayanas.md) — (Kakawin Ramayana)
- **Indus Valley / Harappan Civilization** — Mature urban Harappan civilization flourishes c. 2600-1900 BCE with planned cities, standardized weights, and an undeciphered script, with disputed claims linking it to Vedic culture _(actors: Harappan civilization)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India (Wikipedia); archaeology consensus)
- **Jagannath Rath Yatra (charter procession)** — Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra and Sudarshana Chakra are pulled in three towering chariots from the Puri temple to the Gundicha Temple and back, the annual chariot festival of the Char Dham _(actors: Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Wikipedia, Ratha Yatra (Puri); Britannica)
- **Kabir found as an infant on Lahartara Lake** — A Brahmana widow abandons the infant Kabir on Lahartara Lake in Varanasi, where the Muslim weaver couple Niru and Nima find and raise him, making him Hindu by blood and Muslim by upbringing _(actors: Kabir, Niru, Nima, Brahmana widow)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Kabir hagiography (folk))
- **Lagadha's Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa** — Oldest extant Indian astronomical text, a ritual luni-solar calendar tracking Sun and Moon against the nakṣatras, with no zodiac _(actors: Lagadha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa; histories of Indian astronomy)
- **Lakulīśa reforms the Pāśupata order** — The Gujarat sage Lakulīśa (~2nd c. CE), regarded as an incarnation of Śiva, reforms the Pāśupata movement and authors the foundational Pāśupata-sūtra, renaming it Lākula-Pāśupata _(actors: Lakulīśa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Pashupata Shaivism)
- **Mirabai's childhood vow to Krishna** — As a child before an image of Krishna, Mira declares 'He is my husband,' making her later earthly marriage a formality over a prior spiritual vow to Giridhar _(actors: Mirabai, Krishna)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography)
- **Naraharitīrtha pioneers Kannada devaranāma** — Earliest recognized progenitor of Haridāsa song within Madhva's paramparā, reputed pioneer of Kannada devaranāma; fl. late 13th–early 14th c _(actors: Naraharitīrtha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya; Wikipedia, Narahari Tirtha)
- **Nathamuni Recovers the Naalayira Divya Prabandham** — Nathamuni (c. 824-924 CE) recovers the lost 4,000 Alvar hymns by reciting Madhurakavi's verses until Nammalvar reveals the whole corpus, compiling and setting it to music as the Dravida Veda _(actors: Nathamuni, Nammalvar, Madhurakavi)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Nimbarka traps the sun in a neem tree** — To honor a sannyasi guest after sunset when ascetics may not eat, Nimbarka traps the setting sun (arka) in a neem (nimba) tree so its light lingers, earning his name _(actors: Nimbarka, a sannyasi guest)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Nimbarka hagiography (folk))
- **Patañjali compiles the Yoga Sūtras** — Patañjali composes/redacts the 196-sūtra foundational manual of classical Yoga (c. 2nd c. BCE - 5th c. CE), crystallising Sāṃkhya-with-Īśvara as the practical darśana of stilling the mind _(actors: Patañjali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-sutras-of-patanjali.md) — (Yoga Sūtras of Patañjali)
- **Ramananda founds the Ramanandi Sampradaya** — Ramananda pioneers the organization of north-Indian bhakti and founds the Ramanandi (Ramavat) ascetic order centred on Rama-Sita, accepting disciples regardless of caste, gender or creed and preaching in vernacular Hindi _(actors: Ramananda)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Bhaktamal tradition)
- **Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Sabha** — Raja Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Sabha at Calcutta on 20 August 1828, the rationalist monotheist precursor of the Brahmo Samaj and engine of the Bengal Renaissance _(actors: Ram Mohan Roy, Dwarkanath Tagore)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Brahmo Samaj history)
- **The Alvars Sing the 108 Divya Desams** — The twelve Alvar poet-saints (c. 5th-9th c. CE) sing Vishnu shrines in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham, the act of mangalasasanam canonizing the 108 Divya Desams _(actors: Twelve Alvars, Tirumangai Alvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **The Three Sangams convene at Madurai** — By legend three successive literary academies meet at Madurai under Pāṇḍya patronage over ~9,990 years, the first two lost to floods (Kumari Kandam), only the third surviving _(actors: Pāṇḍya kings, Tamil poets)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Iṟaiyaṉār Akapporuḷ commentary)
- **Tukārām born into Vārkarī devotion** — Tukārām, a Śūdra grocer-cultivator of Dehu, is born to Bolhobā and Kanakāī into a Viṭṭhal-devotee family, inheriting Vārkarī devotion _(actors: Tukārām, Bolhobā, Kanakāī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (Wikipedia, Tukaram; New World Encyclopedia)
- **Yamuna dies as Ramanuja arrives at Srirangam** — Ramanuja is designated successor of Yamunacharya, the theological forerunner of Srivaishnavism, but the two never meet — Yamuna dies just as Ramanuja arrives at Srirangam _(actors: Yamunacharya, Ramanuja)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Ramanuja hagiography)
- **Abolition of sati (1829)** — Ram Mohan Roy's campaign secures the 1829 abolition of sati, a landmark of rational reform under colonial modernity _(actors: Ram Mohan Roy)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Bengal Renaissance reform history)
- **Adi Shankara Founds the Four Amnaya Mathas** — Adi Shankara founds four cardinal monasteries (Jyotirmath, Sringeri, Govardhana at Puri, Dwarka Sharada Pitha), each guarding one Veda and one quarter of India _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Wikipedia, Char Dham)
- **Śaṅkaradeva's pan-Indian pilgrimage** — Orphaned and schooled under Mahendra Kandalī, Śaṅkaradeva undertakes a ~12-year pilgrimage to the tīrthas, then returns to propagate single-refuge Bhāgavata devotion _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva, Mahendra Kandalī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (vajiramandravi.com; testbook.com)
- **Basava becomes chief minister to Bijjala II** — Basava rises to treasurer and then chief minister of the Kalachuri king Bijjala II at Kalyana, using his state office to institutionalize the Sharana gatherings and fund the dasoha kitchens _(actors: Basava, Bijjala II)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Kalachuri political chronology)
- **Bhāskararāya systematizes Śrīvidyā** — Bhāskararāya Makhin (1690–1785) reconciles the diverse vidyās into one coherent Śrīvidyā philosophy, authoring 40+ works and founding a living lineage _(actors: Bhāskararāya Makhin)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md) — (Wikipedia, Shri Vidya)
- **Gauḍapāda composes the Māṇḍūkya-Kārikā** — Gauḍapāda, the parama-guru of Śaṅkara, composes the 215-verse Māṇḍūkya-Kārikā, the earliest systematic treatise of Advaita Vedānta with its ajāta-vāda doctrine _(actors: Gauḍapāda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mandukya-upanishad.md) — (Gauḍapāda, Māṇḍūkya-kārikā)
- **Indo-Aryan Migrations** — Indo-Aryan speakers migrate into the subcontinent c. 1900-1500 BCE bringing the Indo-European language that becomes Vedic Sanskrit (disputed against an Out-of-India model) _(actors: Indo-Aryans)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India (Wikipedia); genetic studies (Reich et al.))
- **Kaṇṇaki burns Madurai (Cilappatikāram)** — After her husband Kōvalaṉ is wrongly executed for theft, Kaṇṇaki proves his innocence and curses the city of Madurai, which burns down _(actors: Kaṇṇaki, Kōvalaṉ)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Cilappatikāram)
- **Kabir descends from Satlok as a body of light** — In the Kabir Panth's own account, Kabir descends from Satlok as a body of light and incarnates on a lotus in Lahartara Lake, witnessed by the rishi Ashtanand, marking him a divine avatara rather than a born human _(actors: Kabir, sage Ashtanand)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Kabir Panth tradition (folk))
- **Kaundinya's Pañcārtha-bhāṣya** — The commentator Kaundinya (4th–5th c.) writes the Pañcārtha-bhāṣya on the Pāśupata-sūtra, fixing the pati–paśu–pāśa triad inherited by all later Śaiva schools _(actors: Kaundinya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Pashupata Shaivism)
- **Marriage of Mirabai to Bhojraj of Mewar** — In 1516 Mira weds Bhojraj, crown prince of Mewar and son of Rana Sanga, marrying into the Sisodiya dynasty of Chittor _(actors: Mirabai, Bhojraj, Rana Sanga)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Rajput chronicle)
- **Nammalvar's sixteen years of silence under the tamarind** — Nammalvar sits in padmasana in a hollow of a tamarind tree at the Adinatha temple for sixteen years, eyes closed in absorption, neither speaking nor eating _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Nammalvar hagiography (traditional))
- **Nimbarka founds the Nimbarka Sampradaya** — Nimbarka founds the Kumara/Nimbarka Sampradaya, propounds Dvaitadvaita, elevates Radha to full divine status worshipped inseparably with Krishna as the Yugala, and authors the Vedanta-parijata-saurabha _(actors: Nimbarka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Vedanta-parijata-saurabha; Dashashloki)
- **Pey Alvar First Sees Lakshmi Beside Vishnu** — Pey Alvar, third of the Mudhal Alvars, is said to have first 'seen' Lakshmi beside Vishnu, recorded in his Munram Tiruvandhadhi _(actors: Pey Alvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Ramanuja breaks with Yadava Prakasha** — Ramanuja first studies Advaita under Yadava Prakasha at Kanchi but breaks with him over the kapyasam scriptural-interpretation dispute, then aligns with the Yamuna line _(actors: Ramanuja, Yadava Prakasha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Ramanuja biography)
- **Ravidas envisions Begampura** — The Chamar sant-poet Ravidas of Varanasi sings his nirguna devotion and articulates the utopia of Begampura, an egalitarian city 'without sorrow or tax,' a great social image of the bhakti movement _(actors: Ravidas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Guru Granth Sahib (Ravidas hymns))
- **Re-composition of the Ramakien under Rama I** — After Ayutthaya-era versions were lost in the 1767 Burmese sack, King Rama I re-composes the standard Thai national Rama epic (1782-1809) _(actors: King Rama I of the Chakri dynasty)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/southeast-asian-ramayanas.md) — (Ramakien)
- **Śrīpādarāja systematizes the Dāsa-kūṭa** — Mulbāgal pontiff (c. 1422–1480) shapes the suḷādi form and composes under aṅkita 'Raṅga Viṭṭhala', first major systematizer of Dāsa-kūṭa song _(actors: Śrīpādarāja (Lakṣmīnārāyaṇatīrtha))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya; Wikipedia, Sripadaraja)
- **Sambandar's Pandya reconversion contest** — Summoned by queen Maṅgaiyarkkaracī, Sambandar cures the Pandya king's fever, defeats the Jains in contests of fire and water, and reconverts the king and realm to Śaivism _(actors: Sambandar, Kūṉ Pāṇḍiyaṉ, Maṅgaiyarkkaracī, Kulacciṟai)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sambandar)
- **Shankara Initiated by Govinda Bhagavatpada** — Journeying north, Shankara meets and is initiated by his guru Govinda Bhagavatpada on the banks of the Narmada, inheriting the proto-Advaita teaching of Gaudapada _(actors: Adi Shankara, Govinda Bhagavatpada)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Wikipedia, Adi Shankara)
- **The famine and Tukārām's turn to devotion** — A c. 1629 famine kills Tukārām's first wife Rakhumābāī and a son and ruins his trade, the collapse that turns the failing grocer toward total Viṭṭhal-devotion _(actors: Tukārām, Rakhumābāī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (New World Encyclopedia; siddhayoga.org)
- **The Five Siddhāntas** — Five early-CE astronomical schools (Sūrya, Paitāmaha, Vāsiṣṭha, Romaka, Pauliśa) absorbing Greco-Babylonian geometry and the 12-sign zodiac into India _(actors: Anonymous Siddhānta authors)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Pañcasiddhāntikā; histories of Indian astronomy)
- **The Garland Legend (Sudikkodutta Nacciyar)** — Kodai secretly wears the temple garlands as the Lord's bride; when Periyalvar withholds the 'polluted' offering, Vishnu appears in his dream declaring he prefers the worn garlands, earning her the epithet Sudikkodutta Nacciyar _(actors: Andal, Periyalvar, Vishnu)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Andal — Wikipedia; Grokipedia)
- **The Moovar Sing the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams** — The Nayanar saint-poets Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar (6th-9th c. CE) compose the Tevaram, qualifying 275/276 Shiva temples as Paadal Petra Sthalams _(actors: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Tevaram / first seven Tirumurai)
- **Andal Composes the Tiruppavai** — Andal composes the 30-verse Tiruppavai, dramatizing the Margali pavai vow with herself as a gopi waking companions and the household of Krishna, the most-recited portion of the Prabandham _(actors: Andal)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Tiruppavai — Wikipedia)
- **Composition of the Rigveda** — The Rigveda, oldest layer of the four Vedas with hymns to Agni, Indra, Soma, Varuna and Ushas, is composed c. 1500-1200 BCE (traditionally held eternal and authorless) _(actors: Vedic rishis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Rigveda; Vedic period (Wikipedia))
- **Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj** — Swami Dayananda founds the Arya Samaj at Bombay on 10 April 1875, preaching return to the sole authority of the Vedas and pioneering the shuddhi reconversion rite, and authors the Satyarth Prakash _(actors: Dayananda Saraswati)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Satyarth Prakash; Arya Samaj history)
- **Deification of Kaṇṇaki as Paṭṭiṉi** — Kaṇṇaki is deified as the goddess of chastity Paṭṭiṉi/Kaṇṇaki Amman, and King Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ builds her temple, founding the Paṭṭiṉi cult _(actors: Kaṇṇaki, Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Cilappatikāram (Vañcikkāṇṭam))
- **Founding of the Anubhava Mantapa** — Basava founds the Anubhava Mantapa at Kalyana, a casteless 'first religious parliament' open to all and to women, presided over spiritually by Allama Prabhu on the Shunya-simhasana, becoming the crucible of the vachana corpus _(actors: Basava, Allama Prabhu, the Sharanas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Vachana sahitya)
- **Kabir's trick-initiation by Ramananda** — Kabir lies across the Panchganga ghat steps before dawn; Ramananda trips over him crying 'Ram! Ram!', and Kabir seizes that involuntary cry as his initiating mantra, proclaiming himself the saint's disciple _(actors: Kabir, Ramananda)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Popular hagiography (folk))
- **Madhurakavi breaks Nammalvar's silence** — Following a southern light to the tamarind tree, Madhurakavi poses a riddle and the boy's first-ever words answer it, declaring the soul's total dependence on God; Madhurakavi becomes his disciple on the spot _(actors: Madhurakavi Alvar, Nammalvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Tiruvaymoli tradition)
- **Nabakalebara (renewal of Jagannath's wooden bodies)** — Every 12-19 years, when an Adhika Ashadha falls, the wooden bodies of the Puri deities are ritually replaced and the Brahma-padartha soul-substance transferred in secret _(actors: Jagannath)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (traditional)
- **Pratisarga 'prophecy' of Adam, Noah, Moses** — The interpolated Pratisarga Parva narrates a Genesis-derived cycle of Ādhama and Havyavatī, Nyūha (Noah) and the flood, and Mūsā (Moses) — an 18th–19th-c. fabrication _(actors: Ādhama, Havyavatī, Nyūha, Mūsā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/bhavishya-purana.md) — (Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Pratisarga Parva) [interpolation])
- **Ramanuja Heads the Shri Sampradaya** — Ramanuja (trad. 1017-1137) is appointed head acharya of the Lakshmi-founded Shri Sampradaya, crystallizing it into the Vishishtadvaita school of qualified non-dualism _(actors: Ramanuja, Lakshmi)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Wikipedia, Ramanuja)
- **Ramanuja systematizes Vishishtadvaita and reorganizes Srirangam** — Ramanuja settles at Srirangam, reorganizes its Ranganatha temple worship, propounds prapatti as the supreme means to moksha, and writes the Shri Bhashya refuting Shankara sutra by sutra _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Shri Bhashya; Vedartha Samgraha; Gadya Trayam)
- **Rigveda Composed** — Oldest Veda layer composed c. 1500-1200 BCE (scholarly); tradition holds the Vedas eternal and authorless _(actors: Vedic rishis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Rigveda)
- **Sambandar raises Pūmpāvai from death** — Sambandar raises the merchant's daughter Pūmpāvai from death by his hymn and is given a pearl palanquin, parasol and cymbals by Śiva _(actors: Sambandar, Pūmpāvai, Śiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sambandar)
- **Shankara Recovers the Badrinath Image from the Alaknanda** — Adi Shankara is said to have recovered the self-manifest black shaligram image of Badrinarayan from the Alaknanda river, establishing the northern dham _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Skanda Purana, Badari-mahatmya)
- **Sūrya Siddhānta** — Cornerstone of Hindu mathematical astronomy revealed by Sūrya to Maya; planetary motions, Earth's sphericity, and the 4,320,000-year Mahāyuga synchronising all planets _(actors: Sūrya, Maya (frame); historical redactors)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Sūrya Siddhānta)
- **Staging of the Cihna Yātrā** — Śaṅkaradeva stages the Cihna Yātrā, the first theatrical/visual-art presentation of the movement and seed of aṅkīyā nāṭ drama _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Surdas composes the Sursagar** — The blind Braj-bhasha master Surdas, supreme of the Ashtachhap, composes the Sursagar 'Ocean of Sur,' a vast song-anthology on Krishna's childhood and youth _(actors: Surdas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Sursagar)
- **The Digvijaya (Conquest of the Directions)** — Shankara undertakes a pan-Indian debate-tour, defeating and converting rival schools, reordering monastic life and establishing his pithas _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Madhaviya Shankara-Digvijaya)
- **Tiruppan Alvar Carried into the Srirangam Sanctum** — The low-born Panar bard saint Tiruppan Alvar is carried into the Srirangam sanctum and composes the Amalanadipiran, a head-to-foot vision of Ranganatha, emblem of bhakti transcending caste _(actors: Tiruppan Alvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Tukārām's dream-initiation by Bābājī Caitanya** — Having no living guru, Tukārām receives dream-dīkṣā when a teacher named Bābājī Caitanya lays a hand on his head and gives the mantra 'Rām Kṛṣṇa Hari.' _(actors: Tukārām, Bābājī Caitanya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (VivekaVani; New World Encyclopedia)
- **Vallabha founds the Pushtimarg** — Vallabha founds the Pushtimarg 'Path of Grace' and systematizes Shuddhadvaita, teaching salvation by divine grace and sevA through Brahma-sambandha self-dedication to Krishna, and authors the Anubhashya and Subodhini _(actors: Vallabhacharya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Anubhashya; Subodhini; Shodasha-granthah)
- **Vasugupta receives the Śiva-Sūtras** — Śiva reveals the Śiva-Sūtras (77 aphorisms) to Vasugupta, inscribed on a rock at Mahādeva mountain, seeding Kashmir Śaivism and the Spanda doctrine _(actors: Śiva, Vasugupta)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (New World Encyclopedia, Kasmir Saivism; SUNY)
- **Vyāsatīrtha institutionalizes the Haridāsa movement** — Dvaita dialectician and Vijayanagara rāja-guru (c. 1460–1539), bridges Vyāsa-kūṭa and Dāsa-kūṭa, mentors Purandara and Kanaka; signature 'Sirī Kṛṣṇa' _(actors: Vyāsatīrtha (Vyāsarāja), Kṛṣṇadevarāya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya; Wikipedia, Vyasatirtha)
- **Widowing of Mirabai** — Bhojraj, wounded in battle c.1518, dies c.1521 before succeeding to the throne, leaving Mira widowed young and never reigning as queen _(actors: Mirabai, Bhojraj)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Rajput chronicle)
- **Xuanzang Records the Prayag Assembly under Harsha** — The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang records a great bathing-and-almsgiving assembly at Prayag convened by King Harsha in 644 CE, often cited as the earliest historical witness to the Kumbh _(actors: Xuanzang, King Harsha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Wikipedia; Sahapedia)
- **Abhinavagupta receives the Kaula transmission** — Abhinavagupta (c. 975–1025) receives the Kaula transmission from his guru Śambhunātha and fuses Krama's Kālī-core into a Kaula-Trika synthesis in the Tantrāloka _(actors: Abhinavagupta, Śambhunātha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md) — (Wikipedia, Kashmir Shaivism)
- **Andal Dreams Her Wedding to Vishnu (Varanam Ayiram)** — In the Varanam Ayiram decad of the Nacciyar Tirumoli, Andal dreams her marriage to Vishnu in vivid ritual detail, the textual core of her dream-wedding identity _(actors: Andal, Vishnu)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Nacciyar Tirumoli; Andal — Wikipedia)
- **Basava's reform program and the ishtalinga** — Basava abolishes caste in worship and table-fellowship, rejects temple-icon ritual and animal sacrifice, and gives every devotee regardless of birth or sex the ishtalinga to wear, making the body the temple _(actors: Basava)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Vachana sahitya; Lingayatism)
- **Battle of the 1760 Haridwar Kumbh** — At the 1760 Haridwar Kumbh, competition over bathing primacy erupts into a deadly battle between Shaiva Gosains and Vaishnava Bairagis, leaving hundreds dead _(actors: Shaiva Gosains, Vaishnava Bairagis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Wikipedia, Kumbh Mela)
- **Composition of Later Vedic Corpus and Upanishads** — The Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas plus Brahmanas, Aranyakas and principal Upanishads are composed c. 1200-500 BCE, shifting from sacrificial ritualism to Atman-Brahman metaphysics _(actors: Vedic sages)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Vedic corpus; Brihadaranyaka and Chandogya Upanishads)
- **Founding of Ekaśaraṇa Dharma** — Śaṅkaradeva founds the Ekaśaraṇa ('single refuge') monotheistic Kṛṣṇa/Nārāyaṇa devotion, structuring it around the cāri vastu (Nāma, Deva, Guru, Bhakat) _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Ekasarana Dharma)
- **Hirapur Chausaṭh Yoginī Temple Built** — The Bhauma-Kara queen Hīrādevī builds the small circular hypaethral Chausaṭh Yoginī temple at Hirapur c. 864 CE with 64 black-stone yoginī images and a central Kālī/Mahāmāyā shrine _(actors: Hīrādevī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (ASI; Wikipedia: Chausath Yogini Temple, Hirapur)
- **Kabir's double critique of Hindu and Islamic orthodoxy** — Kabir delivers his iconoclastic teaching attacking idol-worship, pilgrimage, caste and the sacred thread on the Hindu side and the muezzin's call, namaz, hajj and circumcision on the Muslim side, declaring independence from both religions _(actors: Kabir)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Bijak; Kabir verse)
- **Śālivāhana meets Īśā (Jesus)** — King Śālivāhana is said to encounter in the Himalayas a teacher calling himself Īśā-putra, born of a virgin — a late Christian interpolation _(actors: Śālivāhana, Īśā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/bhavishya-purana.md) — (Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Pratisarga Parva) [interpolation])
- **Madhva Founds the Udupi Seat and Dvaita School** — Madhva (1238-1317), held to be the third avatara of Vayu, heads the Brahma Sampradaya, founds the Udupi seat-cluster, and systematizes the realist Dvaita / Tattvavada doctrine _(actors: Madhva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Wikipedia, Madhvacharya)
- **Maṇimēkalai renounces the world and gains the alms-bowl** — Maṇimēkalai, daughter of Kōvalaṉ and Mādhavi, renounces the world for the Buddhist path and obtains the never-empty magic alms-bowl Amuta-curapi _(actors: Maṇimēkalai)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Maṇimēkalai)
- **Milarepa Flies to the Kailāsa Summit** — In the Bön/Buddhist legend the yogi Milarepa flies to the summit of Kailāsa on a sunbeam, winning the mountain for Buddhism through devotion rather than climbing _(actors: Milarepa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (Bon/Buddhist tradition)
- **Mirabai defies widow-propriety and caste** — Rejecting Rajput widow seclusion, Mira sings and dances publicly before Krishna's image and consorts with low-caste sadhus, the core scandal driving the persecution legends _(actors: Mirabai, sadhus)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography)
- **Mucalinda Shelters the Buddha** — The nāga Mucalinda coils seven times and spreads his hood to shelter the meditating Buddha from a seven-day storm _(actors: Mucalinda, Buddha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Buddhist canon)
- **Nammalvar composes the Tiruvaymoli and his four works** — Nammalvar composes his four Tamil works totaling 1,296 verses — the Tiruvaymoli, Tiruviruttam, Tiruvaciriyam and Periya Tiruvandhadhi — revered as the Tamil Veda equated with the four Vedas _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Tiruvaymoli; Nalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Narsinh Mehta composes Vaishnava Jana To** — The Adi Kavi of Gujarati, Narsinh Mehta, sings Krishna's rasa-lila and composes 'Vaishnava Jana To,' which became Gandhi's favorite bhajan and a near-anthem of the freedom movement _(actors: Narsinh Mehta)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Narsinh Mehta padas)
- **Purandara Dāsa codifies Carnatic pedagogy** — 'Father of Carnatic music' (c. 1484–1564) creates the graded piḷḷāri gītes and Māyāmāḷavagauḷa exercises and vast devaranāma under 'Purandara Viṭṭhala' _(actors: Purandara Dāsa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya; biographies of Purandara Dāsa)
- **Raja Jagat Singh installs Raghunath as Kullu's sovereign** — As penance for a curse, King Jagat Singh installed an idol of Raghunath (Rama) brought from Ayodhya as Kullu valley's true king and ruled as his regent, founding Kullu Dussehra _(actors: Jagat Singh, Raghunath/Rama)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Wikipedia, Kullu Dussehra)
- **Ramakrishna's multi-path realization at Dakshineswar** — The Dakshineswar Kali priest Ramakrishna attains experiential realization through multiple paths — Tantra, Vaishnava bhakti, Advaita, Islam and Christianity — grounding the doctrine that all religions lead to the same God _(actors: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Ramakrishna Mission history)
- **Ramanuja's exile to Melkote** — Fleeing Chola Shaiva-aligned persecution, Ramanuja takes refuge at Melkote in the Hoysala Karnataka country, founding institutions there before returning to Srirangam _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Ramanuja hagiography (traditional))
- **Āryabhaṭa and the Āryabhaṭīya (499 CE)** — Founding dated astronomical text giving π≈3.1416, sine tables, and the radical doctrine of Earth's axial rotation; midnight vs sunrise reckoning schools _(actors: Āryabhaṭa)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Āryabhaṭīya)
- **Sambandar merges into the jyoti at his wedding** — At his own marriage at Nallūr-Perumaṇam, Sambandar prays and merges into the divine effulgence, taking the entire wedding party into Śiva _(actors: Sambandar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sambandar)
- **Sambandar Turns the Pandya King Back to Shaivism** — The child-prodigy saint Tirugnana Sambandar, fed divine milk by Parvati, composes hymns that lead the Pandya king back to Shaivism from Jainism _(actors: Sambandar, Pandya king)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Tevaram)
- **Shankara Debates Mandana Mishra** — Shankara challenges the Mimamsa ritualist Mandana Mishra at Mahishmati with his wife Ubhaya Bharati as umpire; Shankara prevails and Mandana takes sannyasa as Sureshvaracharya _(actors: Adi Shankara, Mandana Mishra, Ubhaya Bharati)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (esamskriti; Wikipedia)
- **Somānanda founds the Pratyabhijñā school** — Early 10th c., Somānanda founds the Pratyabhijñā ('recognition') school with his Śiva-dṛṣṭi and teaches Utpaladeva _(actors: Somānanda, Utpaladeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (IEP, Kashmiri)
- **The drowned manuscripts miracle** — Ordered by Rāmeśvar Bhaṭṭ to destroy his poems, Tukārām sinks his manuscripts in the Indrāyaṇī and fasts 13 days, after which they float up intact, vindicating a Śūdra's right to scripture _(actors: Tukārām, Rāmeśvar Bhaṭṭ)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (mkvyoga.com; New World Encyclopedia)
- **Upanishads & Later Vedic Corpus** — Brahmanas, Aranyakas and principal Upanishads c. 1200-500 BCE shift focus to Atman-Brahman metaphysics _(actors: Vedic sages)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya Upanishads)
- **Vallabha discovers and serves Shrinathji** — Vallabha discovers and serves the self-manifest Shrinathji image — Krishna as a child lifting Mount Govardhana — on Govardhana hill in Braj, the central icon of the Pushtimarg _(actors: Vallabha, Shrinathji)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Pushtimarg tradition)
- **Appar's healing and reconversion to Śaivism** — After a Jain phase as Dharmasena, Appar is struck by incurable colic, returns to his sister Tilakavatiyār who applies sacred ash, is healed, and embraces Śaivism for life _(actors: Appar, Tilakavatiyār)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Appar)
- **Appar Survives the Shaiva Ordeals** — Appar, converted to Jainism then back to Shaivism, survives ordeals of poison, an elephant and the sea, and establishes the sacred-ash (Tiruniru) devotion _(actors: Appar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Appar — Wikipedia)
- **Bastar Dussehra instituted by the Bastar house** — The Bastar ruling house instituted a ~75-day Dussehra honouring the guardian-goddess Danteshwari and clan goddess Maoli as a tribal-royal compact, with no Ravana-burning _(actors: Danteshwari, Bastar rulers)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Outlook; Deccan Chronicle; Village Square)
- **Bhedaghat 81-Yoginī Temple Built** — The Kalachuri king Yuvarāja II builds the largest Yoginī temple at Bhedaghat in the early 11th century with 81 cells following the Mūla-cakra scheme of 9 Mātṛkās each leading 8 yoginīs _(actors: Yuvarāja II)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (Wikipedia: Chausath Yogini Temple, Bhedaghat)
- **Caitanya Grafts the Gaudiya Line onto Madhva** — Caitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534) and his Acintya-bheda-abheda theology are affiliated to the Brahma-Madhva line through Madhavendra Puri and Ishvara Puri, forming the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya Sampradaya _(actors: Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Madhavendra Puri, Ishvara Puri)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (iskconcommunications.org)
- **Composition of the Kīrtana-ghoṣā** — Śaṅkaradeva composes the Kīrtana-ghoṣā, his masterpiece of Assamese narrative Kṛṣṇa-verse for congregational singing and central scripture of Ekaśaraṇa _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Composition of the Tukārām Gāthā** — Tukārām composes the Tukārām Gāthā (c. 1632–1650), several thousand plain-Marathi abhaṅgas that become the culminating scripture of the Vārkarī canon _(actors: Tukārām)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (Wikipedia, Tukaram)
- **Death of Kabir at Maghar and the body of flowers** — Kabir deliberately dies at the inauspicious town of Maghar rather than Kashi; his quarreling Hindu and Muslim disciples lift the shroud to find the body vanished and only flowers, which they divide for cremation and burial _(actors: Kabir, Hindu and Muslim disciples)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Kabir hagiography (folk))
- **Death of Vallabha at Varanasi** — Vallabha attains tirobhava at Varanasi in 1531, traditionally by entering the Ganga at Hanuman-ghat and vanishing in a flame _(actors: Vallabhacharya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Pushtimarg tradition)
- **First National Ayurveda Day** — The Government of India designated Dhanteras as National Ayurveda Day, first observed 28 October 2016 _(actors: Government of India)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Ministry of AYUSH)
- **Founding of the Baranagore Math** — After Ramakrishna's death in 1886 his monastic disciples form the first Math at Baranagore, the seed of the Ramakrishna order _(actors: Ramakrishna's monastic disciples)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Ramakrishna Mission history)
- **Kanaka Dāsa, anti-caste poet-saint** — Kuruba warrior-poet-saint (c. 1509–1609), author of Mohanataraṅgiṇī and Haribhaktisāra, the Uḍupi Kanakana Kiṇḍi legend; signature 'Kāginele Ādikeśava' _(actors: Kanaka Dāsa (Ṯhimmappa Nāyaka))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya; Wikipedia, Kanaka Dasa)
- **Madhvācārya, third descent of Vāyu** — In Dvaita doctrine Vāyu descends a third time as Madhvācārya in the Kali Yuga to restore true dualist Vaiṣṇava Vedānta, completing the threefold avatāra after Hanumān and Bhīma _(actors: Madhvācārya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Madhva-vijaya of Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya; Mādhva exegesis of Ṛgveda 1.141)
- **Nammalvar's ascent to Vaikuntha** — After a brief life of about 35 years Nammalvar attains paramapada-prapti, ascending to Vaikuntha, commemorated annually as his apotheosis _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Nammalvar hagiography (traditional))
- **Panini's Ashtadhyayi** — Panini composes his Sanskrit grammar c. 5th-4th century BCE _(actors: Panini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Ashtadhyayi)
- **Panini's Ashtadhyayi Composed** — Panini composes the Ashtadhyayi, the foundational Sanskrit grammar, c. 5th-4th century BCE _(actors: Panini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Ashtadhyayi)
- **Prayagwal Priests Rebrand the Magh Mela as Kumbh** — In the mid-1800s the Prayagwal priests rebrand Prayag's annual Magh Mela as 'Kumbh' for socio-economic advantage, the name previously reserved for Haridwar _(actors: Prayagwal priests)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Maclean; Wikipedia, Prayag Kumbh Mela)
- **'Prophecy' of Mahāmada (Muhammad)** — A polemical late insertion casts Muhammad as a piśāca/demon-incarnation whose followers are called musalmān _(actors: Mahāmada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/bhavishya-purana.md) — (Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Pratisarga Parva) [interpolation])
- **Queen Māyā Conceives the Buddha at Anavatapta** — In Buddhist legend Queen Māyā conceives the Buddha at Mānasarovara (Anavatapta/Anotatta), the lake at the centre of the world _(actors: Queen Māyā, the Buddha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (Buddhist tradition)
- **Rājarāja I recovers and Nampi canonizes the Tirumurai** — The lost early Śaiva hymns are rediscovered by Chola king Rājarāja I in a sealed Chidambaram chamber and arranged into the canon by Nampi Āṇṭār Nampi _(actors: Rājarāja I, Nampi Āṇṭār Nampi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Tirumurai tradition)
- **Rāmprasād Sen opens Śākta-bhakti** — Rāmprasād Sen (c. 1718–1775), Bengal's founding Śākta poet-saint, first addresses Kālī with tender intimacy as Mother in his Rāmprasādī Kālī-songs, reframing the fierce Goddess _(actors: Rāmprasād Sen)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md) — (Wikipedia, Ramprasad Sen)
- **Shankara Enters King Amaruka's Corpse to Learn Kama** — When Ubhaya Bharati questions the celibate Shankara on the art of love, he enters the corpse of the dead King Amaruka by parakaya-pravesha to learn the subject and win the debate _(actors: Adi Shankara, Ubhaya Bharati, King Amaruka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Madhaviya Shankara-Digvijaya, Part 3)
- **Standardization of the Burmese Yama Zatdaw** — Myanmar's Rama epic is standardized under Konbaung-dynasty patronage in the 18th century, shaped by court contact with Thai Ayutthaya after 1767 _(actors: Konbaung dynasty patrons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/southeast-asian-ramayanas.md) — (Yama Zatdaw)
- **The cup of poison turned to nectar** — The Rana sends Mira a cup of poison disguised as prasad; she drinks it as Krishna's gift and is unharmed, the poison turning to nectar _(actors: Mirabai, Rana Vikramaditya, Krishna)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography (folk))
- **The Haralayya-Madhuvarasa inter-caste marriage crisis** — A marriage between the son of the untouchable Sharana Haralayya and the daughter of the Brahmin Sharana Madhuvarasa enrages the orthodox; Bijjala orders the fathers blinded and executed, triggering Sharana unrest _(actors: Haralayya, Madhuvarasa, Bijjala II)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Basava hagiography)
- **The Tenkalai-Vadakalai split** — The Shri Sampradaya fractures by the late 14th c. into the Vadakalai (Vedanta Deshika, monkey-analogy effortful grace) and Tenkalai (Manavala Mamunigal, cat-analogy causeless grace) sub-sects over how prapatti and grace operate _(actors: Vedanta Deshika, Manavala Mamunigal)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Rahasya-traya-sara; srivaishnava polemics)
- **The Twin Dream-Command to Bring Andal to Srirangam** — Ranganatha appears in dreams to both Periyalvar and the Srirangam priests, commanding that Andal be brought in bridal attire to be wed to him _(actors: Ranganatha, Periyalvar, Srirangam priests)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Andal — Grokipedia)
- **Tulsidas composes the Ramcharitmanas** — Tulsidas composes the Ramcharitmanas in seven kandas in 1574-77, begun at Ayodhya on Rama-Navami, a devotional Awadhi retelling of the Ramayana that becomes the basis of the Ramlila and the 'Bible of north India.' _(actors: Tulsidas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Ramcharitmanas)
- **Utpaladeva systematizes Pratyabhijñā** — Utpaladeva (c. 925–975) systematizes the recognition philosophy in the Īśvara-pratyabhijñā-kārikā _(actors: Utpaladeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Kashmir Shaivism)
- **Varāhamihira** — Sixth-century synthesiser whose Pañcasiddhāntikā summarises the five Siddhāntas and whose Bṛhat Saṃhitā and Bṛhat Jātaka anchor the saṃhitā and horā branches _(actors: Varāhamihira)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Pañcasiddhāntikā; Bṛhat Saṃhitā; Bṛhat Jātaka)
- **Abhinavagupta unifies the Kashmiri streams** — Abhinavagupta (c. 950–1016) reconciles the Āgama, Spanda and Pratyabhijñā streams into a unified non-dualism in the Tantrāloka and other works _(actors: Abhinavagupta)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Kashmir Shaivism)
- **Andal Merges into Ranganatha (Goda-Kalyanam)** — Borne to Srirangam as a bride, Andal ascends to Ranganatha's couch and merges bodily into the deity in a burst of light, a paradigm of jiva-Brahman union _(actors: Andal, Ranganatha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Andal — Wikipedia; JKYog)
- **Appar survives the ordeals under Mahendravarman I** — Appar survives a lime kiln, poison, a maddened elephant and being cast into the sea bound to a stone, convincing the Pallava king Mahendravarman I to reconvert to Śaivism _(actors: Appar, Mahendravarman I)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Appar)
- **Assassination of Bijjala and the Kalyana dispersal** — The marriage-crisis repression provokes Bijjala's assassination c.1167 and the violent scattering of the Kalyana Sharanas, who flee to Ulavi carrying the vachana manuscripts that preserve the movement _(actors: Sharanas, Bijjala II, Channabasava)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Kalachuri chronology)
- **Bhāskara I** — Earliest commentator on Āryabhaṭa, author of Mahābhāskarīya and a rational sine approximation, and an early user of positional decimal notation with zero _(actors: Bhāskara I)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Mahābhāskarīya; Laghubhāskarīya; Āryabhaṭīya-bhāṣya)
- **Bāmākhepā perfects Tantric sādhanā at Tārāpīṭha** — Bāmākhepā (1837–1911) perfects yoga and Tantric sādhanā in the Tārāpīṭha cremation ground, becomes its spiritual head and 'sweetens' the terrifying Tārā into an intimate Mother _(actors: Bāmākhepā, Kailāśpati Bābā)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md) — (Wikipedia, Bamakhepa)
- **Compilation of the Bijak** — The eastern Banaras branch compiles the Bijak ('seed/map of hidden treasure') in the 17th century as the holy scripture of the Kabir Panth, organizing Kabir's verse into Ramaini, Shabad and Sakhi _(actors: Kabir Panth, Banaras branch)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Bijak)
- **First Organized Prayag Kumbh (1870)** — The recognizably modern, administered Kumbh at Allahabad is held in 1870 under British supervision _(actors: British administration)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Wikipedia)
- **Islamization of the Hikayat Seri Rama** — The Malay prose Rama story is reframed within an Islamic cosmological frame (Allah, prophet-hierarchy) roughly 1300-1700 CE, one of the oldest Malay literary works _(actors: Malay hikayat tradition)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/southeast-asian-ramayanas.md) — (Hikayat Seri Rama)
- **Jnaneshwar composes the Jnaneshwari and takes living samadhi** — The Varkari founding luminary Jnaneshwar composes the Jnaneshwari Marathi paraphrase of the Bhagavad Gita in 1290, then dies at 21 by living sanjivana samadhi at Alandi _(actors: Jnaneshwar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Jnaneshwari; Amritanubhava)
- **Karaikkal Ammaiyar Becomes a Ghoul-Attendant at Shiva's Dance** — The earliest Nayanar renounces her beauty to become a skeletal pey (ghoul) attendant at Shiva's dance, composing some 143 verses _(actors: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, Shiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Tirumurai Book 11)
- **Later Dāsa-kūṭa revival** — 18th-c. revival under Vijaya Dāsa, Gopāla Dāsa, and Jagannātha Dāsa (Harikathāmṛtasāra), extending the Haridāsa corpus _(actors: Vijaya Dāsa, Gopāla Dāsa, Jagannātha Dāsa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Haridāsa-sāhitya)
- **Madhva rejects Advaita and founds Dvaita** — Initiated young under the Advaitin Acyutapreksha, Madhva rejects Advaita and launches Tattvavada (Dvaita), teaching the pancha-bheda five eternal distinctions and authoring the 37 Sarvamula granthas _(actors: Madhva, Acyutapreksha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Brahma Sutra Bhashya; Anuvyakhyana; Sarvamula granthas)
- **Mahavira and Buddha** — Mahavira (Jainism) and Gautama Buddha flourish c. 6th-5th c. BCE, challenging Vedic ritual and caste _(actors: Mahavira, Gautama Buddha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Jain & Buddhist tradition)
- **Mitaoli Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple Built** — The 64-celled circular Ekattarso Mahadeva yoginī temple is built at Mitaoli c. 1323 CE, often cited as inspiration for the Indian Parliament's circular plan → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (ASI)
- **Nathamuni recovers the lost Divya Prabandham** — Nathamuni recites Madhurakavi's eleven verses 12,000 times at Alvartirunagari until Nammalvar appears in yogic vision and reveals the entire 4,000 hymns with their music and esoteric meaning, which he institutes as the Dravida Veda _(actors: Nathamuni, Nammalvar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Nammalvar hagiography (traditional))
- **Nāthamuni recovers the Divya Prabandham** — By legend Nāthamuni recovers the lost 4,000 Āḻvār verses through yogic meditation on Nammāḻvār, compiling the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham _(actors: Nāthamuni, Nammāḻvār)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham tradition)
- **Prabhupada Founds ISKCON as 32nd Link** — Prabhupada founds ISKCON (1966), reckoning himself the 32nd link in the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya parampara counted from Krishna _(actors: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (HareKrishnaMandir.org)
- **'Prophecies' of Mughals, Timur, and the British** — The Pratisarga Parva 'foretells' the Mughals, Timur, Akbar, Nādir Shāh, the English, Calcutta, and Queen Victoria — fabricated retrojections dating the layer to the 18th–19th c _(actors: Mughals, Timur, Akbar, Queen Victoria)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/bhavishya-purana.md) — (Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Pratisarga Parva) [interpolation])
- **Rise of the Sixteen Mahajanapadas** — Sixteen kingdoms and oligarchies arise c. 600-321 BCE with cities, coinage and the ascendancy of Magadha during the second urbanization _(actors: Mahajanapadas; Magadha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India (Wikipedia))
- **Sekkizhar Composes the Periya Puranam** — Sekkizhar composes the Periya Puranam (12th c., the 12th Tirumurai), the hagiography of all 63 Nayanars narrating their temple-visits as miracle events _(actors: Sekkizhar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **Shankara Establishes the Four Amnaya Pithas** — Shankara installs four cardinal mathas (Shringeri, Puri, Dvaraka, Jyotirmatha), each with a Veda, mahavakya and first head, and reorganizes renunciants into the Dashanami order _(actors: Adi Shankara, Sureshvara, Padmapada, Hastamalaka, Totaka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Hindupost; Sringeri Math)
- **The basket with the serpent** — Mira is sent a covered basket said to hold a venomous snake but on opening it finds a garland of flowers or a Krishna image, the snake transformed _(actors: Mirabai, the in-laws, Krishna)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography (folk))
- **The borgeet fire and the 34 survivors** — A fire destroys Śaṅkaradeva's 240 borgeet manuscripts; only ~34 are recovered from memory, after which, grieved, he stops composing and asks Madhavadeva to continue the genre _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva, Madhavadeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (assaminfo.com; atributetosankaradeva.org)
- **Thrissur Pooram founded by Sakthan Thampuran** — Around 1796 Raja Rama Varma 'Sakthan Thampuran' of Cochin organized ten temples around Vadakkunnathan into the unified Thrissur Pooram after smaller temples were barred from the Aarattupuzha Pooram _(actors: Sakthan Thampuran)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Wikipedia, Thrissur Pooram)
- **Tukārām's bodily ascent to Vaikuṇṭha** — At his end (1649/1650) Tukārām tells Avalī he is going to Vaikuṇṭha and is taken bodily in a radiant chariot before a crowd, leaving no corpse _(actors: Tukārām, Avalī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (mkvyoga.com; New World Encyclopedia)
- **Vikramaditya's Reign and the Vikrama Samvat Epoch** — The legendary cakravartin Vikramaditya reigns at Ujjayini with his court of nine gems including Kalidasa, and the Vikrama Samvat era (57 BCE) is founded counting from his reign _(actors: Vikramaditya, Kalidasa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ujjain-avantika.md) — (Simhasana-dvatrimshika tradition)
- **Vitthalanatha forms the Ashtachhap** — Vallabha's son Vitthalanatha completes his father's works, organizes temple seva and forms the Ashtachhap, the eight poet-saints (four his, four Vallabha's) whose Braj-bhasha songs become the sect's liturgical music _(actors: Vitthalanatha, Surdas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Ashtachhap corpus)
- **Vivekananda's Chicago address** — Vivekananda delivers the 'Sisters and Brothers of America' address at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in September 1893, introducing Vedanta and Yoga to the West _(actors: Swami Vivekananda)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Ramakrishna Mission history)
- **Yatōktakāri Obeys Tirumaḻicai Āḻvār** — The reclining Viṣṇu at Tiru-Veḷḷakkuḷam rises and leaves (then returns) at the command of Tirumaḻicai Āḻvār, becoming Yatōktakāri, 'he who did exactly as told' _(actors: Viṣṇu (Yatōktakāri), Tirumaḻicai Āḻvār)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (divyadesam.com)
- **Bhartrhari Renounces the Ujjain Throne** — The poet-king Bhartrhari, disillusioned by the tale of the immortality-fruit passed between king, queen and lover, renounces the Ujjain throne to become a yogin and compose the Shatakatraya _(actors: Bhartrhari, Vikramaditya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ujjain-avantika.md) — (folk tradition)
- **Brahmagupta and the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta (628 CE)** — First text to treat zero and negatives as numbers; carried the decimal system to Baghdad as the Zīj al-Sindhind; rejected Āryabhaṭa's rotating Earth _(actors: Brahmagupta)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta; Khaṇḍakhādyaka)
- **Cēkkiḻār composes the Periya Purāṇam** — In 1135 CE Cēkkiḻār composes the Periya Purāṇam, the hagiography of all 63 Nāyaṉārs, under Chola Kulottuṅga II _(actors: Cēkkiḻār, Kulottuṅga II)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/tamil-canon-sangam-and-bhakti.md) — (Periya Purāṇam)
- **Death of Basava at Kudalasangama** — Having withdrawn to Kudalasangama amid the crisis, Basava dies there, traditionally described as merging into the linga _(actors: Basava)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Basava hagiography)
- **Enactment of Nammalvar's Vaikuntha-ascent at Srirangam** — During the Adhyayana Utsava at Srirangam the full Tiruvaymoli is recited and Nammalvar's image is taken through the Paramapada Vasal into the sanctum, dramatically staging his liberation before the assembled devotees _(actors: Nammalvar, Srirangam devotees)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Tiruvaymoli; Srirangam liturgy)
- **Founding/glorification of the Koṇārka Sun Temple** — The Brahma Purāṇa describes the great Sun Temple of Koṇārka (built 1241 CE) and its pilgrimage merit, a key dating anchor → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa [late text])
- **Founding of the pādukā-pālkhī procession** — In 1685 Tukārām's youngest son Nārāyaṇ Mahārāj begins the pādukā-pālkhī custom, carrying the saint's sandals in a palanquin from Dehu to Pandharpur _(actors: Nārāyaṇ Mahārāj, Tukārām)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tukaram.md) — (Wikipedia, Pandharpur Wari)
- **Kabir's verses entered into the Adi Granth** — Guru Arjan Dev compiles the Adi Granth in 1604 at Kartarpur, incorporating Kabir's verses and making him the largest non-Sikh bhagat contributor to Sikh scripture _(actors: Guru Arjan Dev, Kabir)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Adi Granth / Guru Granth Sahib)
- **Kailāsanāthar Temple Built by Rājasiṃha** — The Pallava king Rājasiṃha (Narasiṃhavarman II) builds the Kailāsanāthar temple c. 685–705 CE, the oldest standing temple in Kāñcī and foundational to the Dravidian style _(actors: Rājasiṃha (Narasiṃhavarman II), Mahendravarman III)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (Wikipedia, Kailasanathar Temple)
- **Kannappar Offers His Own Eyes to Shiva** — The tribal hunter Nayanar Kannappar offers his own eyes to a Shiva linga, becoming the archetype of devotion over ritual purity _(actors: Kannappar, Shiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Nayanars — Wikipedia)
- **Krishnadevaraya Composes the Amuktamalyada** — The Telugu poet-king Krishnadevaraya retells Andal's life in the Amuktamalyada ('she who gives a worn garland'), an emperor's literary tribute _(actors: Krishnadevaraya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Amuktamalyada — Grokipedia)
- **Madhva obtains the Udupi Krishna icon and founds the Krishna Matha** — Madhva miraculously obtains a Krishna murti encased in gopichandana from a ship off the Karnataka coast and enshrines it at Udupi, establishing the Krishna Matha and the Ashta Matha with their Paryaya worship rotation _(actors: Madhva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Madhva hagiography (traditional))
- **Meykaṇḍar composes the Śivajñāna-bodham** — In the 13th c. Meykaṇḍar authors the twelve-sūtra Śivajñāna-bodham, founding systematic Tamil Śaiva Siddhānta and the Meykaṇḍar Sampradāya _(actors: Meykaṇḍar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Meykandar)
- **Namdev co-founds the Varkari kirtana tradition** — The tailor sant Namdev of Pandharpur, Jnaneshwar's contemporary, co-founds the Varkari kirtana tradition and travels to the Punjab, his hymns entering the Guru Granth Sahib _(actors: Namdev)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Namdev abhangas; Guru Granth Sahib)
- **Relocation of Shrinathji to Nathdwara** — In 1672, fleeing Aurangzeb, the Shrinathji image is moved from Govardhana to Nathdwara in Rajasthan, which becomes the chief Pushtimarg shrine _(actors: Pushtimarg followers)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Pushtimarg tradition)
- **Rise of Mahavira and the Buddha** — Mahavira (Jainism) and Gautama Buddha flourish c. 6th-5th century BCE, their critique of Vedic ritual and caste reshaping the religious field Hinduism later defines itself against _(actors: Mahavira; Gautama Buddha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India (Wikipedia))
- **Shankara Disappears at Kedarnath** — After his works and tour, Shankara dies at age 32, traditionally disappearing at Kedarnath in the Himalayas _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Wikipedia, Adi Shankara)
- **Sundarar and the slave-deed legend** — At his wedding Śiva, disguised as an old Brahmin, produces a deed proving Sundarar's family were his hereditary bond-slaves; Sundarar accepts the call, abandons the wedding and begins his hymns chiding Śiva _(actors: Sundarar, Śiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sundarar)
- **The bed of iron spikes becomes flowers** — Sent a bed of iron spikes to kill her, Mira lies down and it becomes a bed of flowers _(actors: Mirabai, the Rana, Krishna)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography (folk))
- **Tyāgarāja and the kṛti as nāma-saṅkīrtana** — Carnatic Trinity composer (1767–1847), 700+ Telugu kṛtis, Pañcaratna kṛtis, frames music as singing the Name; signature 'Tyāgarāja' _(actors: Tyāgarāja)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Biographies of the Carnatic composers)
- **Vallabha Founds Pushtimarg** — Vallabhacharya (1479-1531) revives Shuddhadvaita and founds Pushtimarg, Krishna-worship as the child Shrinathji of Govardhana, seated at Nathdwara _(actors: Vallabha)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Britannica, Vallabha; Wikipedia)
- **Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission** — Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, fusing renunciation with social service under the maxim of serving the living being as God _(actors: Swami Vivekananda)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Ramakrishna Mission history)
- **Weaving of the Bṛndāvanī Vastra** — Around 1554 Śaṅkaradeva has a ~40-yard tapestry woven depicting Kṛṣṇa's Vṛndāvana līlā, a rare material relic of the movement _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Allama Prabhu's awakening at the cave temple** — After his dancer wife Kamalate's death plunges him into grief and wandering, the siddha Animishayya gives Allama a linga and instruction in a cave temple, igniting his enlightenment and his signature 'Guheshvara.' _(actors: Allama Prabhu, Kamalate, Animishayya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Allama Prabhu hagiography)
- **Aurobindo withdraws to Pondicherry and founds his Ashram** — Aurobindo withdraws from the freedom struggle to Pondicherry in 1910, develops Integral Yoga aiming at the descent of the Supermind, and co-founds the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in 1926 with the Mother _(actors: Sri Aurobindo, Mirra Alfassa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (The Life Divine; Savitri)
- **Bābā Kīnārām founds the Aghorī order** — The Vārāṇasī ascetic Bābā Kīnārām founds the named Aghorī order (the sole surviving Kāpālika-descended line) with its seat at Krīṃ-Kuṇḍ, dying in the latter 18th c _(actors: Bābā Kīnārām)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Aghori)
- **Caitanya Mahāprabhu's Years at Purī** — Caitanya (1486–1534 CE) spent his last ~18 years at Purī absorbed in Jagannātha worship, making it a supreme Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tīrtha _(actors: Caitanya Mahāprabhu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Caitanya-caritāmṛta; Caitanya-bhāgavata)
- **Chaitanya's initiation and ecstatic turn at Gaya** — Travelling to Gaya c.1508-09 for his father's shraddha, the scholar Nimai is initiated by the ascetic Ishvara Puri into the Gopala mantra and overtaken by ecstatic Krishna-bhava _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Ishvara Puri)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Chaitanya-charitamrita; Chaitanya-bhagavata)
- **Ādi Śaṅkara Consecrates the Śrī-Cakra before Kāmākṣī** — Ādi Śaṅkara pacifies the fierce Kāmākṣī by consecrating a Śrī-Cakra before her in the cavity under the central shrine, seating her in yogic calm and founding a living Śrī-Vidyā seat _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara, Kāmākṣī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (kamakoti.org; Kamakshi tradition)
- **Ādi Śaṅkara Installs Chaṇḍī Devī Image** — Ādi Śaṅkarācārya is said to install the main image of Chaṇḍī Devī on Nīl Parvat in the 8th century _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkarācārya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (tourmyindia; Wikipedia)
- **Founding of the Kabir Panth** — After Kabir's death the Sant-mat sect crystallizes in the 17th-18th c. revering him as Satguru and divine incarnation, splitting into the Kabir Chaura and Dharmadasi/Chhattisgarh branches _(actors: Kabir's followers, Dharmadas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Anurag Sagar; Sukh Nidhan (late Panthi texts))
- **Heliodorus Pillar Erected** — The Greek devotee Heliodorus erects a Garuḍa-stambha to Vāsudeva at Besnagar c. 113 BCE, the earliest dated physical witness to Garuḍa-Vaiṣṇava cult _(actors: Heliodorus)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Heliodorus pillar inscription)
- **Kali-yuga dynastic chronicle (Maurya–Gupta)** — Future-tense king-lists of Bārhadratha, Pradyota, Śiśunāga, Nanda, Maurya, Śuṅga, Kāṇva, Andhra/Sātavāhana and Gupta dynasties — datable historical memory recast as prophecy _(actors: Mauryas, Śuṅgas, Sātavāhanas, Guptas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa/Matsya/Viṣṇu Purāṇas [scholarly])
- **Lalla** — Eighth-century author of the Śiṣyadhīvṛddhida-tantra, a major post-Brahmagupta siddhānta on planetary theory and eclipse correction _(actors: Lalla)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Śiṣyadhīvṛddhida-tantra)
- **Madhva proclaims himself the third Vayu-avatara** — Madhva proclaims himself the third incarnation of Vayu after Hanuman and Bhima, sent to restore right doctrine, and brands Advaita 'crypto-Buddhism.' _(actors: Madhva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Madhva works)
- **Mirabai merges into the Krishna image at Dwarka** — In old age Mira travels to Dwarka and, when Mewar emissaries come to summon her home, embraces the Ranchhor-ray image and merges bodily into the Krishna-murti, leaving only her garment _(actors: Mirabai, Dwarkadhish)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Mirabai hagiography (folk))
- **Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar's Sanskrit kṛtis** — Trinity composer (1775–1835), grand slow Sanskrit kṛtis, Navagraha and Kamalāmbā Navāvaraṇa cycles, nottu-svara; signature 'Guruguha' _(actors: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Biographies of the Carnatic composers)
- **Nandanar Enters the Chidambaram Sanctum** — The untouchable Pulaiyar labourer-saint Nandanar enters the Chidambaram sanctum, becoming an emblem of bhakti dissolving caste barriers _(actors: Nandanar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Nayanars — Wikipedia)
- **Nimbarka Pioneers Joint Radha-Krishna Worship** — Nimbarka, head of the Kumara Sampradaya and an amsha of the Sudarshana cakra, settles at Vrindavana and pioneers the joint worship of Radha-Krishna under the Dvaitadvaita school _(actors: Nimbarka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Wikipedia, Nimbarka Sampradaya)
- **Redaction of the Mahabharata** — The Mahabharata is redacted c. 400 BCE-400 CE (traditionally composed by Vyasa at the Dvapara/Kali cusp recording events of ~3102 BCE) _(actors: Vyasa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Mahabharata)
- **Redaction of the Ramayana** — Valmiki Ramayana core composed c. 500 BCE-200 CE (scholarly); tradition places events in Treta Yuga _(actors: Valmiki (traditional))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Ramayana)
- **Sundarar blinded and his sight restored** — Married to Paravai and Caṅkili, Sundarar breaks his oath and is struck blind, gradually regaining sight through penitent hymns; Śiva acts as go-between to reconcile him with Paravai _(actors: Sundarar, Paravai, Caṅkili, Śiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sundarar)
- **The 2013 Kedarnath Flash Floods** — Catastrophic June 2013 flash floods devastate the Kedarnath valley while the temple itself survives → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Wikipedia, Chota Char Dham)
- **The Belaguri debate and conversion of Madhavadeva** — Once a Śākta sacrificer, Madhavadeva is converted to single-refuge bhakti by Śaṅkaradeva at the famous Belaguri debate (maṇi-kāñcana saṃyoga), adding Guru as a cāri-vastu principle _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva, Madhavadeva, Gayāpāṇi/Rāmadāsa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Madhavdev, Ekasarana Dharma)
- **Tukaram's manuscripts float back from the Indrayani** — The Shudra grocer-sant Tukaram of Dehu, emotional apex of the Varkari tradition, sees his abhanga manuscripts drowned in the Indrayani river float back intact, and is traditionally taken bodily to Vaikuntha at his death _(actors: Tukaram)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Tukaram Gatha)
- **Ujjaini Mahakali temple founded (Bonalu charter)** — In 1813 a Hyderabad battalion at Ujjain vowed to install Mahakali's idol if she lifted a plague back home; on deliverance they founded the Ujjaini Mahakali temple, origin of the Bonalu cycle _(actors: Mahakali, Hyderabad battalion)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Wikipedia, Bonalu; Pragyata)
- **Vishnupad Temple Rebuilt by Ahalyābāī Holkar** — The Maratha queen Ahalyābāī Holkar of Indore rebuilds the octagonal Vishnupad temple enclosing Viṣṇu's footprint in its present form in 1787 CE _(actors: Ahalyābāī Holkar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gaya-pitru-tirtha.md) — (Wikipedia, Vishnupad Temple)
- **Worship as Kūttāṇṭavar and the Kūvākam festival** — Aravān is enshrined in Tamil Nadu as Kūttāṇṭavar (a severed-head icon); the eighteen-day Kūvākam (Koovagam) festival re-enacts the marriage, sacrifice, and widowhood, and is the great gathering of the Aravāṇi/Thirunaṅgai community _(actors: Aravān (Kūttāṇṭavar), Aravāṇi/Thirunaṅgai community)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Kūttāṇṭavar temple tradition (Kūvākam, Villupuram, Tamil Nadu))
- **Śaṅkaradeva's death at Bheladuar** — Śaṅkaradeva dies (traditionally 1568) at Bheladuar in Cooch Behar under Koch king Naranārāyaṇa's patronage _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva, Naranārāyaṇa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Allama Prabhu merges with the linga at Kadalivana** — Allama Prabhu is said to have become one with the linga at Kadalivana near Srisailam _(actors: Allama Prabhu)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Allama Prabhu hagiography (traditional))
- **Baladeva Vidyabhushana Wins the Galta Debate** — Baladeva Vidyabhushana composes the Govinda-bhashya and Prameya-ratnavali (18th c.) to win the Gaudiyas a recognized seat at the Galta (Jaipur) debate, bridging them to Madhva _(actors: Baladeva Vidyabhushana)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (iskconcommunications.org)
- **Basava founds the Liṅgāyat tradition** — Basava (c. 1105–1167), treasurer under Kalachuri king Bijjala II, organizes the Liṅgāyat/Vīraśaiva bhakti movement rejecting caste, ritual sacrifice and priestly mediation _(actors: Basava, Bijjala II)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Basava)
- **Bhāskara II and the Siddhānta Śiromaṇi (1150 CE)** — Summit of classical astronomy (Līlāvatī, Bījagaṇita, etc.); anticipates differential calculus with instantaneous planetary velocity and the cakravāla solution of Pell's equation _(actors: Bhāskara II (Bhāskarācārya))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (Siddhānta Śiromaṇi)
- **Buddha's Enlightenment at Bodh Gayā** — Gautama Buddha attains enlightenment under the Bodhi tree beside the Phalgu at Bodh Gayā, the Buddhist pole of the Gayā district _(actors: Gautama Buddha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gaya-pitru-tirtha.md) — (Wikipedia, Bodh Gaya; Britannica)
- **Cekkilar Versifies the Periya Puranam** — Cekkilar (c. 1135 CE) versifies the hagiographies of the 63 Nayanars in the Periya Puranam, added as Book 12 to complete the Tirumurai canon _(actors: Cekkilar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/alvars-and-nayanars.md) — (Periya Puranam; Tirumurai)
- **Chaitanya launches sankirtana at Navadvipa** — Chaitanya launches nightly congregational sankirtana of the Hare Krishna maha-mantra with Nityananda and Advaita Acharya at Shrivasa's courtyard, inaugurating mass Gaudiya devotion _(actors: Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita Acharya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Chaitanya-charitamrita)
- **Ādi Śaṅkara Founds the Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha** — By the Kāñcī matha's tradition, Ādi Śaṅkara founds the Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha at Kāñcī and attains his final siddhi there _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (kamakoti.org)
- **Maurya Empire & Ashoka** — First pan-Indian empire c. 322-185 BCE; Ashoka patronizes Buddhism and issues rock/pillar edicts _(actors: Chandragupta, Bindusara, Ashoka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India)
- **Mirabai and Jiva Gosvami at Vrindavana** — Told that the ascetic Jiva Gosvami would not meet a woman, Mira retorts that Krishna is the only true male in Vrindavana and all else are gopis, whereupon the abashed scholar comes out to meet her _(actors: Mirabai, Jiva Gosvami)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mirabai.md) — (Gaudiya transmission (folk))
- **Onam — Mahābali's Annual Return** — Kerala folk-tradition holds that the golden-age king Māveli (Mahābali) returns to visit his people once a year, celebrated as the Onam harvest festival _(actors: Mahābali (Māveli), Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vamana-bali.md) — (Kerala Onam festival tradition)
- **Ramana Maharshi's death-experience and Self-realization** — At sixteen in 1896 Ramana undergoes a spontaneous death-experience resolving into permanent Self-realization, then settles for life at Tiruvannamalai teaching atma-vichara, 'Who am I?' _(actors: Ramana Maharshi)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/modern-teachers-and-reform.md) — (Ramana Maharshi biography)
- **Ramanuja Learns the Charama Sloka at Tirukkoshtiyur** — At Tirukkoshtiyur, Ramanuja learns the secret charama sloka from his teacher _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Sri Vaishnava hagiography)
- **Redaction of the Valmiki Ramayana** — The Ramayana's core text is composed c. 500 BCE-200 CE (traditionally narrating Treta Yuga events far earlier) _(actors: Valmiki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Ramayana)
- **Rise of the Haridasa movement** — The Kannada bhakti-musical Haridasa wing of Madhva's school carries Dvaita to the common people through devaranamas and dasa-sahitya, with Purandaradasa hailed grandfather of Carnatic music _(actors: Purandaradasa, Vyasatirtha, Kanakadasa)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ramanuja-and-madhva.md) — (Dasa-sahitya; devaranamas)
- **Shankaradeva founds Ekasarana Dharma** — The Assamese polymath Shankaradeva founds Ekasarana Dharma, a single-refuge monotheistic Krishna-devotion, and creates the Kirtana-ghosha, the borgeet song-genre, ankiya nat plays, and the sattra and namghar institutional network _(actors: Shankaradeva, Madhavadeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/north-bhakti-sants.md) — (Kirtana-ghosha)
- **Sundarar composes the Tiruttoṇḍa Tohai** — Sundarar composes the Tiruttoṇḍa Tohai naming the foremost Śiva-devotees, the seed-list from which the canonical 63 Nāyaṉārs were fixed _(actors: Sundarar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sundarar; Nayanars)
- **Tagore's Songs of Kabir** — Rabindranath Tagore publishes Songs of Kabir in 1915, making Kabir a global figure of universalist mysticism _(actors: Rabindranath Tagore)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kabir.md) — (Tagore, Songs of Kabir (1915))
- **The Pañcasakhā and Odia Bhakti** — The five Odia poet-devotees (Balarāma, Jagannātha, Yaśovanta, Ananta, Acyutānanda Dāsa) centered Utkala Vaiṣṇavism on Jagannātha; Jagannātha Dāsa's Odia Bhāgavata became household scripture _(actors: Pañcasakhā poets)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Odia Vaiṣṇava tradition; scholarship)
- **Tulsidas Begins the Ramcaritmanas at Ayodhya (1574)** — Gosvami Tulsidas begins composing the Ramcaritmanas at Ayodhya in 1574 CE, recasting Valmiki's Sanskrit epic into Avadhi for the people _(actors: Tulsidas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Wikipedia; tradition)
- **Viśvanātha Temple Rebuilt by Ahilyābāī Holkar** — After repeated medieval demolitions the Kāśī Viśvanātha (Gyanvapi) temple is rebuilt by Ahilyābāī Holkar in 1780 _(actors: Ahilyābāī Holkar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Kashi-khanda; Shiva Purana)
- **Āḻvār consecration of Tiruvēṅkaṭam as Divya Deśam** — The Āḻvārs (Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai) hymn Tirumala as Tiruvēṅkaṭam in the Divya Prabandham, making it one of the most-sung 108 Divya Deśams and a horizon of prapatti _(actors: Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham)
- **Worship as Khāṭū Śyām Jī / Śyām Bābā** — The self-manifested head is enshrined at Khāṭū, Rajasthan; worshipped as Khāṭū Śyām Jī, Śyām Bābā, Hāre kā Sahārā, with the annual Phālguna fair _(actors: Khāṭū Śyām Jī devotees, Khāṭū shrine (Sīkar, Rajasthan))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Khāṭū Śyām sthala-tradition [folk] [regional])
- **Śyāma Śāstri, the Devī-upāsaka composer** — Eldest of the Trinity (1762–1827), archaka of Baṅgāru Kāmākṣī, Navaratnamālikā and rhythmically intricate svarajatis; signature 'Śyāmakṛṣṇa' _(actors: Śyāma Śāstri)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/haridasa-and-carnatic-bhakti.md) — (Biographies of the Carnatic composers)
- **Akka Mahadevi renounces clothing for Shiva** — After the Jain king Kaushika breaks his pact never to violate her devotion, Akka Mahadevi leaves him, renounces all possessions and clothing covering herself only with her hair, and walks to Kalyana _(actors: Akka Mahadevi, King Kaushika)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Akka Mahadevi hagiography)
- **Chaitanya takes sannyasa at Katwa** — In 1510 Chaitanya takes sannyasa at Katwa from Keshava Bharati, receiving the name Krishna Chaitanya _(actors: Chaitanya, Keshava Bharati)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nimbarka-vallabha-chaitanya.md) — (Chaitanya-charitamrita)
- **Discovery of the Varadvinayak Idol from the Lake (1690)** — The Varada-Vinayaka murti is reportedly found immersed in an adjoining lake at Mahad in 1690 CE, leading to the temple's construction in 1725 _(actors: Ramji Mahadev Biwalkar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ashtavinayaka.md) — (temple history)
- **Eastern Gaṅga Temple Construction** — The surviving 12th-c. Kaliṅga-style temple was built under Eastern Gaṅga kings Anantavarman Coḍagaṅga and Anaṅgabhīma III (c. 1135–1230 CE) over an older, likely Sabara-origin cult _(actors: Anantavarman Coḍagaṅga, Anaṅgabhīma III)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (epigraphic / academic history)
- **Establishment of the Anubhava Maṇṭapa** — Basava establishes the Anubhava Maṇṭapa at Basavakalyāṇ, the 'first religious parliament,' where śaraṇas of all backgrounds debate and produce the vachana corpus _(actors: Basava, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahādevī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shaiva-schools.md) — (Wikipedia, Anubhava Mantapa)
- **Founding of the Maurya Empire** — The Maurya Empire (c. 322-185 BCE), first pan-Indian empire, is founded by Chandragupta; Ashoka patronizes Buddhism and issues rock and pillar edicts _(actors: Chandragupta; Bindusara; Ashoka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (History of India (Wikipedia))
- **Madhavadeva composes the Nāma-ghoṣā** — Madhavadeva composes the Nāma-ghoṣā ('book of the Name'/Hajāri-ghoṣā), consolidating the faith after the founder's death and producing a peak of Assamese literature _(actors: Madhavadeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Madhavdev)
- **Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma and the Kerala school** — Founder of the Kerala school, credited with infinite-series expansions for π, sine and cosine anticipating European calculus by ~250 years _(actors: Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/siddhantic-astronomy-and-astronomers.md) — (histories of Indian astronomy; Yuktibhāṣā (transmission))
