- **Indra Splits Open Vala to Free the Cattle and Dawns** — Indra breaks open the Vala cave to release the imprisoned cattle and dawns, a recurring Vedic myth of liberating light and order _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda)
- **Śiva descends as Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava** — Śiva manifests as a fierce mounted solar-warrior form (Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava) and rides to Jejuri/Mailāra to confront the demons _(actors: Śiva as Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava, the gods as his army)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Mallāri Māhātmya; Marathi folk tradition)
- **Śiva states the guṇa-classification of Purāṇas to Pārvatī** — Śiva teaches Pārvatī the sāttvic/rājasic/tāmasic grouping of the eighteen Purāṇas, each tied to a deity and destination _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/README.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa 236.18–21)
- **Śiva teaches the guṇa-classification to Pārvatī** — Śiva instructs Pārvatī, grouping the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas into sāttvic, rājasic and tāmasic classes by presiding deity and destination _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa 236.18–21)
- **Jaya and Vijaya's three demonic births across the yugas** — The cursed pair are born as Hiraṇyākṣa/Hiraṇyakaśipu (Satya), Rāvaṇa/Kumbhakarṇa (Tretā), and Śiśupāla/Dantavakra (Dvāpara), each slain by Viṣṇu's avatāras _(actors: Jaya, Vijaya, Viṣṇu's avatāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1, 10.74, 10.78)
- **Kahoda Drowned by Bandin** — Ashtavakra's father Kahoda is defeated in debate by Bandin at King Janaka's sacrifice and drowned per the contest's rule _(actors: Kahoda, Bandin, Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashtavakra.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva CXXXII)
- **Kubera's former-life merit as Gunanidhi** — In a folk variant, the thief Gunanidhi, robbing a Shiva temple, inadvertently keeps a lamp burning before the linga, earning merit that reincarnates him as the wealth-god and friend of Shiva _(actors: Kubera (Gunanidhi), Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kubera.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Lakshmi Departs Vaikuntha for Earth** — Offended that her abode was kicked by Bhrgu, Lakshmi leaves Vaikuntha for earth, triggering Vishnu's descent after her as Shrinivasa _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Venkatacala-Mahatmya)
- **Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean and asuras rout the devas** — Stripped of fortune, the three worlds wither, Lakshmi re-enters the Kshira-Sagara, and Bali's asuras rout the weakened devas, who flee Svarga _(actors: Lakshmi, Bali, the asuras, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5-8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Mahalakshmi slays Mahishasura** — As the rajasika aspect, the Goddess slays the buffalo-demon Mahishasura in the middle carita _(actors: Mahalakshmi, Mahishasura)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 2-4)
- **Mohini tests Rukmangada and Vishnu bears the family to Vaikuntha** — Brahma fashions the enchantress Mohini to break Rukmangada's vow; she forces him to choose between his fast and beheading his son Dharmangada, but as the sword falls Vishnu intervenes, reveals the test, and bears the family to Vaikuntha _(actors: Mohini, Rukmangada, Dharmangada, Sandhyavali, Vishnu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/narada-purana.md) — (Narada Purana (Rukmangada-carita))
- **Mārkaṇḍeya's First Narmadā Parikramā** — Sage Markandeya, held to be the first parikramavasi, circumambulates the Narmada and each of her tributaries, founding the most extensive form of the river-circuit vow _(actors: Markandeya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/narmada-parikrama.md) — (Narmada Parikrama tradition)
- **Nara-Nārāyaṇa Teach at Badarī** — The twin sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa impart ekāntika devotion to the sage Nārada at their hermitage at Badarī _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narayaniya.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva (Narayaniya))
- **Parvati Gives Murugan the Vel** — Parvati/Shakti gives Murugan her crystallised power as the lance Vel, the Shakti-vel that becomes the network's central object of worship _(actors: Parvati, Murugan)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/arupadai-veedu-murugan.md) — (Tirumurukarruppatai; Kanda Puranam)
- **Rati's penance wins Kama's rebirth** — Rati performs penance and the gods intercede; Shiva grants that Kama will be reborn, visible to Rati alone or bodily in the next age _(actors: Rati, Shiva, Kama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Shiva Purana; Matsya Purana)
- **Sarasvati curses Ganga to flow on earth** — In the Shakta account, after a jealous quarrel among Vishnu's three consorts, Sarasvati curses Ganga to flow on earth as a river _(actors: Sarasvati, Ganga, Vishnu, Lakshmi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Savitri chooses Satyavan and Narada's death-prophecy** — Savitri chooses the forest-prince Satyavan, son of the blind dethroned king Dyumatsena; the sage Narada declares Satyavan destined to die in exactly one year, but Savitri refuses to recant _(actors: Savitri, Satyavan, Dyumatsena, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 292-293)
- **Shiva beheads the boy guardian** — The boy posted at the door bars Shiva from entering Parvati's chamber, fights the ganas, and is decapitated by Shiva's trident _(actors: Shiva, Ganesha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Six-fold birth of Skanda (Shanmukha)** — Shiva's too-potent seed, relayed through Agni, Ganga and a reed-thicket, becomes six infants nursed by the six Krittikas and fused by Parvati into the six-faced Kartikeya _(actors: Shiva, Agni, Ganga, Krittikas, Parvati, Kartikeya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Maheshvara/Kedara-khanda); cf. Mahabharata, Kumarasambhava)
- **Sāvitrī chooses Satyavān despite Nārada's death-prophecy** — Sāvitrī chooses the forest-prince Satyavān; Nārada foretells he will die in one year, but she refuses to recant _(actors: Sāvitrī, Satyavān, Nārada, Dyumatsena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 292–293)
- **The soul's crossing of the Vaitarani river** — The preta crosses the dreadful river of blood and pus only by merit and a cow gifted (vaitarani-dana) by the family, which becomes its boat _(actors: the preta (soul), family of the deceased)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/garuda-purana.md) — (Garuda Purana (Preta-khanda))
- **The Tārakāmaya War** — The heavens split into war over Tārā, with devas demanding her return against Soma, Śukra, and Śiva, until Brahmā intervenes and forces Tārā's return _(actors: Bṛhaspati, Indra, Soma, Śukra, Śiva, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Padma Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Threefold birth of the self** — Aitareya teaches the self's three births — conception, gestation, and rebirth in one's offspring — with the ātman entering the body through the crown _(actors: Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad 2.1)
- **Tvaṣṭṛ creates Vṛtra in revenge** — Enraged at his son's murder, Tvaṣṭṛ bars Indra from the soma sacrifice and performs a fire-rite to generate the avenger Vṛtra, but a mispronunciation dooms Vṛtra to die by Indra's hand _(actors: Tvaṣṭṛ, Vṛtra, Indra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishvakarma-and-tvashtar.md) — (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.4.12; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9)
- **Vishnu's footprint enshrined at Vishnupada Temple** — The Vishnupada Temple at Gaya enshrines the basalt footprint of Vishnu, the foot that subdued Gayasura, marking the principal site of Gaya pinda-dana _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/shraddha-and-pitr-rites.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **Vrika Questions Narada** — The asura Vrika, son of Shakuni, meets the wandering Narada and asks which of the three chief gods is most quickly pleased _(actors: Vrika, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.13-16)
- **Yayāti rescues Devayānī and weds her** — Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into a well; King Yayāti pulls her out, weds her, with Śarmiṣṭhā given as her serving-maid _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 76–82; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Aṅgāraka (Mars) Healed of Leprosy** — Mars, afflicted with leprosy, worships Vaidyanatha-Shiva at Vaitheeswaran Koil and is healed, fixing the temple as the Mars node and divine-physician shrine _(actors: Angaraka, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Sthala-purana)
- **Ashtavakra Defeats Bandin in Debate** — The boy Ashtavakra out-argues the unbeaten Bandin in a counting debate, completing the verse on thirteen; Bandin reveals he is Varuna's son and the drowned brahmanas rise alive _(actors: Ashtavakra, Bandin, Janaka, Kahoda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashtavakra.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva CXXXIV)
- **Birth of Budha (Mercury)** — Tārā returns pregnant and, pressed by Brahmā, confesses Soma is the father; the radiant child is named Budha, the planet Mercury _(actors: Tārā, Soma, Budha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata 9; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Dakṣa-yajña, Satī's self-immolation, and Vīrabhadra's destruction of the rite** — Dakṣa Prajāpati holds a great sacrifice without inviting Śiva; Satī self-immolates and Śiva's emanation Vīrabhadra destroys the sacrifice — the archetypal sacrifice gone wrong _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva, Virabhadra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/yajnas-and-vedic-rituals.md) — (Puranas; Mahabharata)
- **Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches in silence** — Śiva as the south-facing supreme guru expounds jñāna and yoga wordlessly through cinmudrā to the four aged Kumāras _(actors: Śiva (Dakṣiṇāmūrti), the four Kumāras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti Stotra)
- **Daksha curses Candra with wasting disease** — Daksha curses Candra with kshaya-roga (wasting disease) so his brilliance dwindles away, in response to the wives' complaint _(actors: Daksha, Candra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/nakshatras.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.6)
- **Drying and Disappearance of the Sarasvatī** — The once-mighty Sarasvati dries and goes underground (the vinashana), re-emerging unseen at sacred confluences such as the Triveni Sangam _(actors: Sarasvati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Mahabharata)
- **Durvasa Hurls the Kritya Fire-Demon** — Enraged that the king 'ate' before serving him, Durvasa tears a lock from his hair and creates a blazing female fire-demon, the Kritya, to attack Ambarisha _(actors: Durvasa, the Kritya, Ambarisha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.4.45-48)
- **Duṣyanta denies Śakuntalā; the celestial voice names Bharata** — Duṣyanta publicly disowns Śakuntalā and son until a sky-voice affirms the child, who is named Bharata and crowned heir _(actors: Duṣyanta, Śakuntalā, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Emanation of the Daśa Mahāvidyā from Satī** — The ten Mahāvidyā goddesses emanate from Satī (or Pārvatī) when she blocks Śiva's exit in a quarrel, surrounding him with ten terrifying forms _(actors: Satī, Śiva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/shakta-and-tantra-lineages.md) — (Wikipedia, Mahavidya)
- **Founding of Pushkara as Brahma's tirtha** — Brahma's sacrifice founds Pushkara (Ajmer) as his chief shrine, with the Savitri/Gayatri episode explaining Brahma's near-absence of temples _(actors: Brahma, Savitri, Gayatri)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Srishti Khanda))
- **Gajendra-Moksha at Tirukkavithalam** — Vishnu as Gajendra Varadan saves the elephant-king Gajendra from the crocodile, the Gajendra-moksha legend localized at Tirukkavithalam _(actors: Vishnu, Gajendra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Bhagavata Purana tradition / sthala-purana)
- **Ganesha restored with an elephant head** — To console the grieving Parvati, Shiva fixes an elephant's head onto the boy's body, reviving him as Gajanana and granting him first worship among gods _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Indra slays Namuci by a foam-trick** — Indra kills the demon Namuci, who could be slain by neither wet nor dry nor day nor night, using a trick of foam _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/indra.md) — (Rigveda)
- **Indra slays the Vṛtras with Dadhyañc's bones** — Dadhyañc's horse-head is recovered from the lake Śaryaṇāvat near Kurukṣetra, and Indra, using the bones of that head, slays ninety-nine Vṛtras — the Vedic germ of the spine-vajra story _(actors: Indra, Dadhyañc)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.84.13; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14.1.1)
- **Ishvara Gita spoken by Shiva** — After Vishnu and Shiva embrace, Shiva expounds Atman, Brahman, Prakriti, Maya, yoga and moksha through a Shaiva non-dualist lens — a Bhagavad Gita with Shiva as spokesman _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu, the rishis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (Ishvara Gita, Uttara-vibhaga))
- **Śiva Lifts Kāśī on His Trident at Pralaya** — At each universal dissolution Śiva lifts Kashi up on his trident to keep it safe, setting it back when creation resumes, so the city alone survives every pralaya _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Judgment of the soul by Yama and Citragupta** — At Yama's city the scribe Citragupta reads the ledger of deeds and Yama assigns heaven, a hell, or rebirth _(actors: Yama, Citragupta, the soul)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/garuda-purana.md) — (Garuda Purana (Preta-khanda))
- **Kakudmi and Revati visit Brahmaloka** — King Kakudmi (Raivata), finding no suitor worthy of his daughter Revati, travels with her to Brahma's realm to ask Brahma directly for a husband, arriving while Brahma is absorbed in a Gandharva performance _(actors: Kakudmi/Raivata, Revati, Brahma, Gandharvas Haha and Huhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.3.27-36; Vishnu Purana 4.1)
- **Kalpa, manvantara and yuga arithmetic** — Exposition of the fourteen Manus, the mahāyuga/manvantara/kalpa numbers and the four yugas — a base witness for the timeline's chronology _(actors: the fourteen Manus)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Kshipra Breaks Mahadev into 84 Pieces** — In one legend the river Shipra breaks Mahadev into 84 pieces to slay the demon Dushana, each piece becoming one of the Chaurasi Mahadev shrines _(actors: Shiva-Mahadev, Kshipra, Dushana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ujjain-avantika.md) — (Avantya-khanda mahatmya)
- **Madalasa's Atma-jnana lullaby and her sons' renunciation** — Queen Madalasa, a jivanmukta, sings non-dual Vedanta to each infant son, and her first three sons renounce the world straightaway _(actors: Madalasa, King Ritadhvaja, Vikranta, Subahu, Shatrumardana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana (chs. 16-44))
- **Mahasarasvati slays Shumbha-Nishumbha** — As the sattvika aspect, the Goddess slays Shumbha and Nishumbha and emanates Kali/Chandika in the third carita _(actors: Mahasarasvati, Shumbha, Nishumbha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 5-13)
- **Marriage of Savitri and Satyavan in the forest** — Ashvapati gives Savitri to Satyavan in the hermitage; she dons bark-cloth and serves her blind father-in-law Dyumatsena as a devoted ascetic-wife _(actors: Savitri, Satyavan, Ashvapati, Dyumatsena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 293)
- **Mohinī beguiles Śiva, begetting Ayyappa** — Mohinī later beguiles Śiva, their union begetting Ayyappa (Hari-Hara-putra), and also deludes the demon Bhasmāsura _(actors: Mohinī (Viṣṇu), Śiva, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Murugan Slays Surapadman and Weds Deivanai** — At the Arupadai Veedu abodes Murugan slays the demon Surapadman (who falls at Tiruchendur) and marries Deivanai at Thiruparankundram _(actors: Murugan, Surapadman, Deivanai)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Thirumurugatrupadai)
- **Nārada's Journey to Śvetadvīpa** — Nārada journeys north past Mount Meru to the White Island to behold the universal form of the Lord and the perfected single-minded white devotees _(actors: Nārada, the white ekāntins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narayaniya.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva (Narayaniya))
- **Prāṇa overcomes the demons (Pavamāna prayer)** — The vital breath (prāṇa) overcomes the demons' evil, the context of the 'asato mā sadgamaya' prayer leading from untruth to truth, darkness to light, death to immortality _(actors: prāṇa, the demons)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.3.28)
- **Pratardana dialogue with Indra** — Indra teaches Pratardana that he is prāṇa, the conscious self, life and immortality, declaring life-breath and cognition inseparable _(actors: Indra, Pratardana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 3)
- **Pārvatī Creates Gaṇeśa at Gaurī Kuṇḍa** — At Gaurī Kuṇḍa below Dolma La, Pārvatī fashions a son from the paste of her body to guard her bath; Śiva strikes off his head and replaces it, the boy becoming Gaṇeśa _(actors: Pārvatī, Śiva, Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (sthala-purana; Ganesha birth-myth)
- **Rudra Creates and Rolls Up the Worlds** — The one Rudra, allowing no second, holds all worlds with his ruling powers, creates beings, and at the end of time rolls them up (samcukoca) into himself _(actors: Rudra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/svetashvatara-upanishad.md) — (Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.2)
- **Sati immolates herself at the Daksha-yajna** — Sati, married to Shiva against her father Daksha's contempt and humiliated at his sacrifice, immolates herself in yogic fire _(actors: Sati, Daksha, Shiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Sati-khanda))
- **Satī's Navel Falls at Kāñcī** — In the Satī dismemberment myth the goddess's navel falls at Kāñcī, anchoring Kāmākṣī as a Śakti Pīṭha and the 'navel of the goddess' _(actors: Satī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (Devi-Bhagavata / Shakti-pitha lists)
- **Satī's self-immolation and the Dakṣa-yajña** — Dakṣa stages an insulting sacrifice; Satī immolates herself, rupturing Dakṣa and Śiva, after which Pārvatī later performs austerity to win Śiva _(actors: Satī, Dakṣa, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Satyavān dies and Sāvitrī follows Yama** — On the foretold day Satyavān dies; Yama comes in person to take his soul and Sāvitrī follows Death southward _(actors: Satyavān, Yama, Sāvitrī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 294–295)
- **Slaughter of the Exposed Kalakeyas** — With the ocean drained, the gods slaughter the exposed Kalakeya asuras, already weakened by the wrath of the brahmins _(actors: the Devas, the Kalakeyas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
- **Slaying of Mahiṣāsura** — After a shape-shifting duel the Goddess pins the buffalo-demon Mahiṣāsura and beheads him as the true demon emerges from the buffalo's mouth, earning the name Mahiṣāsura-mardinī _(actors: Durgā (Mahiṣāsura-mardinī), Mahiṣāsura)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devī Māhātmya ch.2-4)
- **Slaying of Malla and Maṇi** — The god slays Malla (hence Mallāri); the dying Maṇi gifts his white horse and wins the boon of joined worship and animal offerings _(actors: Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava, Maṇi, Malla)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Mallāri Māhātmya; Jejuri/Kannada Mailāra folk variants)
- **Slaying of Surapadma at Tiruchendur** — After a six-day fast Murugan fells the asura Surapadma in the seaside battle at Tiruchendur, the climactic victory of the Skanda war-cycle _(actors: Murugan, Surapadma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/arupadai-veedu-murugan.md) — (Kanda Puranam; Surasamharam legend)
- **Taraka-vadha by Skanda** — Anointed Devasenapati, Skanda leads the devas and slays Tarakasura (and in expanded cycles Surapadma, Simhamukha and Pralamba), restoring cosmic order _(actors: Skanda, Tarakasura, Surapadma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Maheshvara-khanda); Tamil Kandapuranam)
- **The race around the parents** — In a race against Kārtikeya for a divine fruit, Gaṇeśa circumambulates his parents declaring them his whole world and wins, sending the slighted Kārtikeya south _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Kārtikeya, Śiva, Pārvatī, Nārada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa)
- **The Spider and the Elephant at Thiruvanaikaval** — Two cursed Shiva-ganas reborn as a spider and an elephant worship the jambu-linga; their rivalry kills both, and Shiva frees them from the curse, the spider reborn as the Chola king Koccengat _(actors: Malyavan, Pushpadanta (spider and elephant), Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Jambukeswarar mahatmya)
- **The Vedavyāsa office and the 28th Vyāsa** — A Veda-Vyāsa is appointed each Dvāpara to re-arrange the Veda; Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana is the 28th of the cycle, with Aśvatthāmā named as the coming 29th _(actors: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, the twenty-eight Vyāsas, Aśvatthāmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4)
- **The Vritra-gita: Vritra accepts his destiny** — The defeated asura-king Vritra, taught by Shukracharya, expounds calm renunciation and devotion to Vishnu _(actors: Vritra, Shukracharya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lesser-gitas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Santi Parva ~12.279-281)
- **Tyranny from Śūnyaka and desolation of the worlds** — Bhaṇḍāsura rules from the City of the Void with brothers Viṣukra and Viṣaṅga, draining the cosmos of love and fertility; Nārada counsels the devas to invoke Parāśakti _(actors: Bhaṇḍāsura, Viṣukra, Viṣaṅga, the devas, Nārada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lalita-bhandasura.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Lalitopākhyāna))
- **Uddālaka teaches Śvetaketu 'Tat tvam asi'** — To humble his conceited son Śvetaketu, Uddālaka Āruṇi teaches the Sad-vidyā through nine parables, each closing with 'Tat tvam asi' — that thou art _(actors: Uddālaka Āruṇi, Śvetaketu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1–6.16)
- **Śukra curses Yayāti with premature old age** — Discovering the broken oath, Śukra curses Yayāti to instant decrepitude, granting the loophole that he may trade his age for another's youth _(actors: Yayāti, Śukrācārya, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 85; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Vāg-Devatās recite the Lalitā-Sahasranāma** — The Vāg-Devatās recite the thousand-name hymn to Lalitā to Hayagrīva, encoding the Śrī-Cakra and Śrī-Vidyā mantra doctrine _(actors: Vāg-Devatās, Hayagrīva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmanda-purana.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Lalitopākhyāna))
- **Vishnu counsels the churning truce** — The devas approach Vishnu at the Kshira-Sagara, who counsels a temporary truce with the asuras to churn the ocean for amrita, promising the devas will ultimately keep it _(actors: Vishnu, Brahma, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.6; Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Vishnudutas Rescue Ajamila from the Yamadutas** — Hearing the holy name, four Vishnudutas descend and forcibly stop the three Yamadutas from binding and removing Ajamila's soul, then debate the jurisdiction of Yama _(actors: Vishnudutas, Yamadutas, Ajamila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.1.34-6.2.49)
- **Vishnu's Three Strides (Trivikrama)** — Vishnu measures out the three worlds — earth, mid-air, and heaven — in three strides, establishing the cosmos as living-space for gods and men and setting his 'highest step' as the abode of bliss _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 1.22; 1.154)
- **Vishnu Worships Ganesha to Subdue Madhu and Kaitabha at Siddhatek** — At creation's edge Vishnu cannot subdue the asuras Madhu and Kaitabha until he worships Ganesha at Siddhatek and obtains siddhi, then prevails _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Ganesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ashtavinayaka.md) — (Ganesha Purana; cf. Devi-Mahatmya)
- **Visnu accepts the curse and offers two roads** — Visnu bows to the Kumaras, accepts the irrevocable curse, and offers his servants seven devotee-births or three enemy-births back to him _(actors: Visnu, Jaya, Vijaya, Sanaka-kumaras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.16; 7.1)
- **Viṣṇu Leaves His Footprint at Har-ki-Pauri** — Viṣṇu appears at Har-ki-Pauri in the Vedic age and leaves his footprints in the stone of the ghāṭ, kept perpetually touched by the Gaṅgā _(actors: Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia, Har Ki Pauri)
- **Vrika's Flesh-Offering Penance at Kedara** — At Kedaranatha Vrika feeds the sacrificial fire with pieces of his own flesh for seven days until Shiva emerges from the fire to stay his self-beheading _(actors: Vrika, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.17-19)
- **Yajña on Gayāsura's Body** — Asked for a boon, Gayāsura offers his own body as the altar; he lies head-to-north and Brahmā and the devas perform the great sacrifice upon him, making his body the holiest ground _(actors: Gayāsura, Brahmā, devas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gaya-pitru-tirtha.md) — (Vayu Purana, Gaya-mahatmya)
- **Ajamila's Repentance and Liberation at Haridvara** — Restored and transformed by faith, Ajamila renounces his home, performs bhakti-yoga at Haridvara, and at his second death is borne by the Vishnudutas to Vaikuntha _(actors: Ajamila, Vishnudutas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.2.25-46)
- **Ashtavakra Made Straight in the River** — The restored Kahoda bids Ashtavakra bathe in the river Samanga, and his eight bends are made straight _(actors: Ashtavakra, Kahoda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashtavakra.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva CXXXIV)
- **Aṣṭāvakra debates the celestial woman on women's independence** — The sage Aṣṭāvakra, sent to test marriage, debates a celestial woman (Diśā) on whether a woman is independent or always under guardianship, expounding strī-dharma _(actors: Aṣṭāvakra, Diśā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/13-anushasana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 13.19-21)
- **Bharata becomes Cakravartin and eponym of Bhāratavarṣa** — Bharata grows into a universal sovereign whose name is given to the dynasty and to the subcontinent Bhāratavarṣa _(actors: Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Birth of Kauśikī and Kālikā** — From Pārvatī's bodily sheath emerges the radiant Ambikā/Kauśikī to fight Śumbha-Niśumbha, while her darkened remainder becomes Kālikā _(actors: Pārvatī, Kauśikī/Ambikā, Kālikā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devī Māhātmya ch.5)
- **Boy-Sage Śveta Saved from Yama** — The boy-sage Sveta, fated to die at sixteen, is saved from Yama by Shiva at Thiruvenkadu, where Shiva subdues death itself _(actors: Sveta, Shiva, Yama)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Sthala-purana)
- **Brahma's revelation of elapsed time** — Brahma laughs and explains that twenty-seven chaturyugas (roughly 116 million human years) have passed on Earth during their brief wait, so the proposed bridegrooms and their dynasties are long dead — an early literary depiction of time dilation _(actors: Brahma, Kakudmi, Revati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.3)
- **Chandra's Curse Tempered at Somnath** — The Moon-god Chandra, cursed by Daksha to wane for neglecting his wives, worships Shiva at Prabhas Patan, and Shiva tempers the curse into periodic waxing and waning, founding the Somnath jyotirlinga _(actors: Chandra (Soma), Daksha, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana; Skanda Purana (Prabhasa Khanda))
- **Child Murugan Teaches Om to Shiva at Swamimalai** — At Swamimalai the child Murugan teaches the meaning of the Pranava (Om) to his father Shiva, becoming Swaminatha _(actors: Murugan, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Arupadai Veedu tradition)
- **Dadhīci drinks the gods' weapons** — Tired of guarding the divine weapons deposited with him, Dadhīci dissolves them in water and drinks them, absorbing their power into his bones so his skeleton alone can yield the supreme weapon _(actors: Dadhīci, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.10)
- **Dadhichi sacrifices his bones for the vajra** — When a Vritra can only be killed by a sage's bones, the ascetic Dadhichi yields his body, and Vishvakarma forges the Vajrayudha from his spine for Indra _(actors: Dadhichi, Vishvakarma, Indra, Vritra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/indra.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Mahabharata)
- **Ghora Āṅgirasa instructs Kṛṣṇa Devakīputra** — The sage Ghora Āṅgirasa instructs Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī — one of the earliest textual mentions of Kṛṣṇa — figuring life as a soma-sacrifice _(actors: Ghora Āṅgirasa, Kṛṣṇa Devakīputra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.17)
- **Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada, and Narasimha (Vishnu P.)** — The asura king Hiranyakashipu persecutes his Vishnu-devoted son Prahlada, prompting Vishnu to erupt as the man-lion Narasimha and slay the boon-protected tyrant _(actors: Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada, Narasimha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1); cf. Bhagavata 7)
- **Indra eclipses Varuṇa as king of the gods** — Across the later Vedic layers the warrior storm-god Indra rises and displaces Varuṇa as effective king of the gods, his slaying of Vṛtra overtaking Varuṇa's law-sovereignty _(actors: Indra, Varuṇa, Vṛtra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/varuna.md) — (Ṛgveda 7.82-85)
- **Indra's sabotage of the hundredth Aśvamedha** — Because a hundred horse sacrifices entitle the performer to Indra's throne, Indra habitually sabotages the hundredth Aśvamedha to protect his sovereignty _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/yajnas-and-vedic-rituals.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 13; Mahabharata)
- **Instruction of King Alarka by Dattatreya** — Alarka, his kingdom threatened to provoke his awakening, follows his mother's ring-counsel to the avadhuta Dattatreya and receives the realization of the Self, finally renouncing _(actors: Alarka, Madalasa, Dattatreya, Subahu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana (chs. 39-43))
- **Jaya and Vijaya choose three demonic births** — Unable to bear long separation, the two choose to be born three times as Visnu's enemies, each life ended by his hand, to return home swiftly _(actors: Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1)
- **Mahiṣāsura-vadha (Śākta variant)** — The gods pool their tejas into the lion-riding Durgā/Caṇḍikā, who is armed by each deity and slays the buffalo-demon Mahiṣa _(actors: Durgā/Caṇḍikā, Mahiṣāsura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha V)
- **Maya the asura-architect and the burning of Tripura** — The asura craftsman Maya builds the three flying cities and a life-restoring nectar step-well; Vishnu drains the well to stop the demons' resurrection and Shiva destroys Tripura with a single fiery arrow _(actors: Maya, Vishnu (Janardana), Shiva, the Pramatha hosts, the asuras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana)
- **Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's penance** — Indra sends Menakā against the rishi Viśvāmitra; aided by Vāyu and Kāmadeva she seduces him, and from their union is born Śakuntalā _(actors: Menakā, Viśvāmitra, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya's vision of the pralaya** — The deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya survives the dissolution, beholds the infant Viṣṇu on a banyan leaf upon the cosmic waters, is swallowed, and sees the universe inside the Lord's body _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Naṭarāja's Ānanda Tāṇḍava** — Śiva as Lord of Dance performs the cosmic dance of bliss at Cidambaram, enacting the five acts (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, grace) and crushing the dwarf Apasmāra _(actors: Śiva (Naṭarāja), Apasmāra, Kālī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Cidambaram Naṭarāja tradition, Tirumantiram, Śaiva Siddhānta)
- **Naṭarāja's Ānanda Tāṇḍava — the cosmic dance of bliss** — Śiva as Lord of Dance performs the dance of bliss at Cidambaram, enacting the five cosmic acts (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, grace) and crushing the dwarf of ignorance Apasmāra _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Cidambaram Naṭarāja tradition; Śaiva Siddhānta; Tirumular's Tirumantiram)
- **Naciketas's three boons and Yama's teaching** — The boy Naciketas, sent to Yama's realm, wins three boons and Yama reluctantly teaches him the immortal Self that is never born and never dies _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad)
- **Origin of bhaṇḍāra (turmeric) worship** — In victory the god and army are showered in turmeric, founding the defining bhaṇḍāra offering and the cry 'Yelkoṭ! Jai Mālhār!' _(actors: Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava, devotees)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Marathi folk tradition [folk/regional])
- **Pūru gives his youth; sons cursed and the dynasty splits** — The four elder sons refuse and are cursed; youngest Pūru gives his youth and is crowned heir, forking the Lunar line into Yādava and Paurava branches _(actors: Yayāti, Yadu, Pūru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 85–88; Bhāgavata 9.18–19)
- **Sapindikarana (preta becomes pitr)** — The recurring decisive death-rite in which, on the 12th day, the single preta-pinda is merged into the three ancestral pindas, converting the hungry ghost into a settled ancestor and bumping the great-great-grandfather into the remote ancestors _(actors: the deceased (preta), descendants, three pitrs)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/shraddha-and-pitr-rites.md) — (Garuda Purana, Pretakhanda; grhya-sutras)
- **Savitri's Triratra vow and Satyavan's death** — Savitri undertakes a three-night standing fast, accompanies Satyavan into the forest on the fatal day, and he is stricken and dies with his head in her lap as Yama comes in person to take his soul _(actors: Savitri, Satyavan, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 293-295)
- **Shani's glance burns off Ganesha's head** — In a variant, Shani's destructive glance burns off the infant Ganesha's head and Vishnu brings a young elephant's head to replace it _(actors: Shani, Ganesha, Vishnu, Parvati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purana)
- **Shibi gives his eyes to a blind beggar (Sibi Jataka)** — In the Buddhist Sibi Jataka, Sakka disguised as a blind brahmana begs an eye and Shibi gives both, then has them restored by an Act of Truth _(actors: Shibi, Sakka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shibi.md) — (Sibi Jataka no. 499; Jatakamala 2)
- **Shiva Grants the Death-Touch Boon** — Shiva, bound by his word, grants Vrika the boon that whomever he touches on the head with his hand will die _(actors: Shiva, Vrika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.20-22)
- **Shiva manifests as the fire-column at Arunachala** — At Arunachala/Tiruvannamalai Shiva manifests as the infinite column of fire (teja-linga), the etiology of the Karttikai-Dipam festival _(actors: Shiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Arunachala-khanda))
- **Shiva Teaches Akhilāṇḍeśvarī Shiva-jñāna** — Shiva imparts Shiva-jnana to the fierce goddess Akhilandeshvari at Thiruvanaikaval, where she stands facing east as disciple and the linga faces west as guru _(actors: Shiva, Akhilandeshvari)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Temple tradition)
- **Skanda slays Surapadman (Tamil recension)** — In the Tamil Kandapuranam, Skanda destroys the demon Surapadman across six war-camps and marries Valli _(actors: Skanda, Surapadman, Valli)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana.md) — (Tamil Kandapuranam (ascribed to Shankari-samhita))
- **Surapadma Split into Peacock and Cock** — The dying Surapadma turns into a mango tree which the Vel splits in two; one half becomes Murugan's peacock vahana and the other the cock of his banner, redeeming the asura into service _(actors: Murugan, Surapadma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/arupadai-veedu-murugan.md) — (Kanda Puranam; Surasamharam legend)
- **Sāvitrī wins five boons and Satyavān's life from Yama** — By her dharma-wisdom Sāvitrī extracts five boons, trapping Yama with the boon of sons by Satyavān, forcing him to restore Satyavān to life _(actors: Sāvitrī, Yama, Satyavān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 296–297)
- **Teaching of Nārada at Badarī (Naranārāyaṇīya frame)** — The twin sages impart the ekāntika dharma to Nārada at Badarī, the inner narrative frame of the Nārāyaṇīya that transmits to Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Nārada, Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Nārāyaṇīya / Śānti Parva)
- **The Hamsa-gita: Brahma as swan instructs the Sadhyas** — Brahma in the form of a swan answers the Sadhyas on the highest good, teaching forbearance and self-mastery _(actors: Brahma, the Sadhyas, Vyasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lesser-gitas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Santi Parva ~12.288-299)
- **The Mahāyāga and the rise of Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī** — From the fire-pit (cit-kuṇḍa) of the devas' great sacrifice arises Lalitā Tripurasundarī, four-armed with noose, goad, sugarcane bow and five flower-arrows _(actors: the devas, Lalitā Tripurasundarī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lalita-bhandasura.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Lalitopākhyāna); Lalitā Sahasranāma)
- **The moon's curse on Gaṇeśa Caturthī** — Mocked by Candra after his belly bursts from modakas, Gaṇeśa decrees that whoever views the moon on his festival day will be falsely accused _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Candra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Gaṇeśa Purāṇa)
- **The Sudarshana Destroys the Kritya and Pursues Durvasa** — The Sudarshana-cakra instantly incinerates the Kritya, then turns on its sender Durvasa, chasing him across the three worlds as Brahma and Shiva confess they cannot save him _(actors: Sudarshana-cakra, Durvasa, Brahma, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.4.50-61)
- **The waxing-and-waning compromise** — Unable to revoke his word, Daksha modulates the curse so the Moon wanes for half the month and waxes back for the other half, originating the dark and bright fortnights _(actors: Daksha, Candra, the gods)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/nakshatras.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Tulasī deceived; the śālagrāma curse** — To enable Śaṅkhacūḍa's slaying, Viṣṇu deceives the chaste Tulasī by taking her husband's form; the enraged Tulasī curses Viṣṇu into the śālagrāma stone and is herself transformed into the tulasī plant and the Gaṇḍakī river _(actors: Tulasī, Viṣṇu, Śaṅkhacūḍa, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Prakṛti-khaṇḍa))
- **Vishnu incarnates as Kurma to bear Mount Mandara** — Mount Mandara is uprooted as churning-rod and Vasuki wound as the rope; when the mountain sinks Vishnu incarnates as the tortoise Kurma and supports it on his shell _(actors: Vishnu/Kurma, Vasuki, devas, asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.6-8.7; Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Vishvakarma trims the Sun** — To relieve Sanjna who could not bear Surya's blaze, Vishvakarma shaves off an eighth of the Sun's radiance, the shavings forged into Vishnu's chakra, Shiva's trident, and other divine weapons _(actors: Vishvakarma, Surya, Sanjna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Matsya Purana)
- **Viṣṇu Pins Gayāsura with the Dharmaśilā** — When Gayāsura's body keeps quaking, Viṣṇu places a great stone slab on him and presses it with his foot, leaving the Viṣṇupada footprint _(actors: Viṣṇu, Gayāsura, devas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gaya-pitru-tirtha.md) — (Vayu Purana; Agni Purana)
- **Vyasa Gita taught by Vyasa** — Vyasa teaches knowledge of Shiva through combined devotion and prescribed works, the duties of the ashramas, and the path to liberation _(actors: Vyasa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (Vyasa Gita, Uttara-vibhaga chs. 12-33))
- **Yājñavalkya cursed and the Yajurveda split** — Cursed by his teacher Vaiśampāyana, Yājñavalkya vomits the old Kṛṣṇa Yajus (taken up as partridges), then the Sun-god as a horse teaches him the fresh Śukla Yajurveda — the origin myth of the White/Black split _(actors: Yājñavalkya, Vaiśampāyana, Sūrya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.5)
- **Yājñavalkya–Maitreyī dialogue** — About to renounce, Yājñavalkya teaches his wife Maitreyī that immortality comes not from wealth but from knowing the Ātman, for whose sake all is dear _(actors: Yājñavalkya, Maitreyī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4 (repeated 4.5))
- **Yuga-dharma and the decline of the ages** — Detailed account of how dharma contracts from Satya to Kali, with the lengths and degeneration of varṇa, lifespan and virtue across the four yugas _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Agastya Digests the Asura Vatapi** — Agastya eats the goat-disguised cannibal asura Vatapi served by Ilvala and says 'Vatapi jiryatam,' digesting and dissolving the demon before he can be summoned back _(actors: Agastya, Vatapi, Ilvala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
- **Andhaka-vadha — impalement of the blind demon** — Andhaka, monstrous son of Hiranyaksha, lusts after Parvati and is impaled on Shiva's trident until his pride burns away, then converted into a devotee and gana-chief _(actors: Shiva, Andhaka, Parvati, Hiranyaksha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana)
- **Ashtavakra's Marriage Test for Suprabha** — To wed Suprabha, the grown Ashtavakra passes the northern temptation set by the rishi Vadanya, refusing a queen's seduction _(actors: Ashtavakra, Suprabha, Vadanya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashtavakra.md) — (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
- **Bharata, the deer, and Jada-Bharata** — King Bharata renounces his kingdom but becomes attached to a fawn, is reborn a deer and then as the idiot-seeming sage Jada-Bharata, who instructs the king of Sauvira in non-dualist wisdom _(actors: Bharata, Jada-Bharata, king of Sauvira)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 2); cf. Bhagavata 5)
- **Bhṛgu–Varuṇa inquiry into Brahman** — Varuṇa guides his son Bhṛgu through successive realizations deriving Brahman as food ascending to bliss in the Taittirīya teaching _(actors: Bhṛgu, Varuṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad (Bhṛgu-vallī))
- **Boon of Gayā the Eternal Pitṛ-Tīrtha** — Viṣṇu and the gods grant that the demon's name mark the spot forever and that any ancestral rite performed there liberate the dead, turning the demon's self-sacrifice into sacred geography _(actors: Viṣṇu, Gayāsura, devas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gaya-pitru-tirtha.md) — (Vayu Purana, Gaya-mahatmya)
- **Candra's penance to Shiva at Prabhasa** — Candra worships Shiva at Somnath/Prabhasa to be cured, and Shiva wears the saved crescent as Candrashekhara _(actors: Candra, Shiva)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/nakshatras.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Conception of Skanda/Kārtikeya** — Śiva's too-fiery seed is carried by Agni and Gaṅgā and deposited in the Saravaṇa reeds, conceived to produce a son able to slay Tārakāsura _(actors: Śiva, Agni, Gaṅgā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 224-232, Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Dadhīci gives his bones for the vajra** — When Viṣṇu reveals that only a weapon forged from Dadhīci's thunder-laden bones can slay Vṛtra, the sage consents to give his life and quits his body in samādhi so his spine can be taken _(actors: Dadhīci, Indra, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9–10)
- **Dakshas curse causes the moon's waning** — Candra favors Rohini and neglects his other 26 nakshatra-wives; Daksha curses him to waste away, and Shiva redeems him to wax and wane eternally _(actors: Candra, Daksha, Rohini, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Skanda/Padma Purana)
- **Dhūmralocana burnt to ash** — The Goddess reduces Śumbha's general Dhūmralocana to ashes with a single huṃkāra and her lion mauls his army _(actors: Devī, Dhūmralocana, Śumbha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devī Māhātmya ch.6)
- **Dismemberment of the asura Bala into the nine gems** — The great asura Bala (Vala) is sacrificed by the gods and his scattered body-parts become the nine precious gems (blood→ruby, teeth→pearl, etc.), the origin myth of the navaratna _(actors: the gods, the asura Bala/Vala)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/garuda-purana.md) — (Garuda Purana (gem section); Agni Purana; Buddha-bhatta's Ratna-pariksha)
- **Ganesha Grants Boons to Sage Gritsamada at Mahad** — Sage Gritsamada worships Ganesha at Mahad after a curse and is granted boons, enshrining the deity as Varada-Vinayaka, the boon-giver _(actors: Gritsamada, Ganesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ashtavinayaka.md) — (Ganesha Purana tradition)
- **Gautama brings the Godavari (Gautamī Gaṅgā) to the Deccan** — After a contrived cow-killing sin engineered by jealous ṛṣis, the sage Gautama brings the Gaṅgā down to the Deccan as the Godavari to expiate it _(actors: Gautama, Gaṅgā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya))
- **Gayāsura and the Gayā-māhātmya** — The pious asura Gayāsura is pinned to the earth so his sanctified ground becomes the supreme pitṛ-tīrtha where a single piṇḍa-offering liberates one's forebears _(actors: Gayāsura, Viṣṇu, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa (Gayā-māhātmya); cf. Agni/Garuḍa/Brahma Purāṇas)
- **Hālāhala / Nīlakaṇṭha** — During the ocean-churning Śiva drinks the all-destroying Hālāhala poison to save creation; Pārvatī holds his throat, lodging it there and turning his throat blue _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Vāsuki, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7, Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Indra slays Vṛtra mounted on Airāvata** — Airāvata is the mount on which Indra slays the dragon Vṛtra, cementing the elephant's rain-and-war role _(actors: Indra, Airāvata, Vṛtra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata; Ṛgvedic Vṛtra cycle)
- **Jānaśruti seeks the sage Raikva** — The proud king Jānaśruti, hearing flamingoes praise the cart-man sage Raikva, seeks him out and is taught the saṃvarga-vidyā of air and breath as the absorbers _(actors: Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa, Raikva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.1–4.3)
- **Kacha infiltrates Śukra to steal the Sañjīvanī** — The devas send Bṛhaspati's son Kacha to become Śukra's disciple and secretly learn the life-restoring mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā that the asuras alone possess _(actors: Kacha, Śukra, Devayānī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Matsya Purāṇa; Agni Purāṇa)
- **Katyayani born to slay Mahishasura** — The Goddess is born in sage Katyayana's hermitage specifically as the fierce warrior-form Katyayani to slay Mahishasura _(actors: Katyayani, Katyayana, Mahishasura)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Mahatmya; Devi Kavaca; Bhagavata Purana 10)
- **Mahishasura conquers heaven** — After a hundred-year war the buffalo-demon Mahishasura defeats Indra, usurps the three worlds, and expels the gods from svarga _(actors: Mahishasura, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 2)
- **Marriage of Lalitā to Kāmeśvara and enthronement in Śrīpura** — Śiva as Kāmeśvara weds Lalitā; the pair are enthroned on the Pañca-brahmāsana in the jeweled city Śrīpura, cosmographic form of the Śrīcakra _(actors: Lalitā, Kāmeśvara (Śiva), Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśāna, Sadāśiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lalita-bhandasura.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; Lalitā Sahasranāma)
- **Marriage to Mhāḷsā** — Khaṇḍobā weds Mhāḷsā, a Brahmin merchant's daughter identified with Pārvatī, representing the settled agrarian-Brahmin pole of the cult _(actors: Khaṇḍobā, Mhāḷsā (Pārvatī))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Mallāri Māhātmya; Marathi tradition)
- **Murugan's Marriage to Deivanai at Tirupparankundram** — After his victory Murugan weds Deivanai, Indra's foster-daughter, at Tirupparankundram, taking the dharmic deva-bride _(actors: Murugan, Deivanai)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/arupadai-veedu-murugan.md) — (Tirumurukarruppatai; Kanda Puranam)
- **Prajāpati's da-da-da teaching** — Prajāpati's single syllable 'da' is heard by gods, humans and demons as the threefold instruction to control oneself, give, and be compassionate _(actors: Prajāpati, gods, humans, demons)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 5.2)
- **Rambhā cursed to stone by Viśvāmitra** — Sent against Viśvāmitra, Rambhā fails and is cursed to become stone for ten thousand years _(actors: Rambhā, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Sati's body becomes the Shakti Pithas** — In the variant where Shiva carries Sati's corpse and Vishnu's discus dismembers it, her scattered body-parts fall to earth and become the Shakti Pithas _(actors: Shiva, Sati, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Sati-khanda))
- **Satī's Heart and Navel Fall at Māyāpurī** — When Viṣṇu dismembers Satī's corpse to end Śiva's grief-dance, her heart and navel fall at Māyāpurī (Haridwar), anchoring it among the Śakti Pīṭhas _(actors: Satī, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia, Maya Devi Temple; Shakti Pitha tradition)
- **Savitri's dialectical duel and five boons from Yama** — Following Yama southward and reciting dharma aphorisms, Savitri wins boons restoring Dyumatsena's sight and kingdom, a hundred sons for Ashvapati, and a hundred sons by Satyavan, trapping Yama into restoring Satyavan's life _(actors: Savitri, Yama, Satyavan, Dyumatsena, Ashvapati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 296-297)
- **Shiva and Parvati Follow Skanda to Srisailam** — After Kartikeya leaves in pique over Ganesha's marriage, Shiva and Parvati follow him to the hill and reside there as Mallikarjuna, establishing the Mallikarjuna jyotirlinga _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Kartikeya, Ganesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Skanda Purana; Shiva Purana)
- **Shiva drinks the Halahala poison and becomes Nilakantha** — The world-poison Halahala/Kalakuta surfaces first, threatening creation; Shiva drinks it and Parvati stays it in his throat, which turns blue, giving him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Vishnu Purana; Shiva Purana)
- **Shiva Flees to Vaikuntha** — Vrika turns to test the boon on Shiva's own head, and the terrified god flees across the universe to Vishnu's Vaikuntha _(actors: Vrika, Shiva, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.23-25)
- **Slaying of Andhakasura by Bhairava** — The blind demon Andhaka is defeated, the slaying associated with Bhairava, culminating in Andhaka's redemption as a gana _(actors: Bhairava (Shiva), Andhakasura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Slaying of Śumbha, Niśumbha, and Raktabīja** — The Goddess emanates the fair Kauśikī, leaving dark Kālikā behind, and destroys Śumbha and Niśumbha with their generals Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa (→Cāmuṇḍā) and Raktabīja, whose blood-drops Kālī drinks _(actors: Kauśikī, Kālikā, Śumbha, Niśumbha, Raktabīja, Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha V)
- **Sāvitrī wins Satyavān back from Yama** — Sāvitrī follows Yama as he carries off her husband Satyavān's soul and wins him back by her wit and virtue, in an expanded Sāvitrī–Yama discourse on dharma and the soul _(actors: Sāvitrī, Satyavān, Yama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Prakṛti-khaṇḍa))
- **The Bull of Dharma loses a leg each yuga** — Dharma personified as a bull loses one leg each yuga, virtue diminishing from four quarters to one across Satya, Treta, Dvapara, and Kali, restored to four at the next Satya _(actors: Dharma (the bull))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.16-17; Mahabharata Vana Parva 149)
- **The dance-contest against Kālī** — Śiva wins a dance-duel against Kālī by raising his leg in the ūrdhva-tāṇḍava pose, which Kālī, bound by modesty, cannot match and concedes _(actors: Śiva, Kālī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Tamil Śaiva sthala-purāṇa; Cidambaram māhātmya)
- **The three-wives quarrel and Vishnu's redistribution of consorts** — Jealous Sarasvati curses Lakshmi to become the Tulasi plant and a river; Ganga curses Sarasvati to become a river bearing people's sins; Vishnu ends the strife by keeping Lakshmi, sending Ganga to Shiva and Sarasvati to Brahma _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Ganga)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana; Brahmavaivarta Purana)
- **Umā–Maheśvara dialogue on women's duties** — Śiva, questioned by Umā (Pārvatī), expounds the ideal conduct of a wife: devotion, sweet speech, and treating the husband as god _(actors: Śiva, Umā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/13-anushasana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 13.146)
- **Vishnu Declares Himself Subject to His Devotees** — Fleeing to Vaikuntha, Durvasa is told by Vishnu that He cannot recall the discus or act against His devotee, uttering 'aham bhakta-paradhino,' and is sent to beg Ambarisha's pardon _(actors: Vishnu, Durvasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.4.62-68)
- **Yama Confesses Vishnu's Supremacy** — When the baffled Yamadutas report their defeat, Yamaraja reveals there is a Supreme Lord above him, names the twelve mahajanas, and commands his servants never to approach devotees of the Name _(actors: Yamaraja, the Yamadutas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.3)
- **Yayāti's renunciation after a thousand years of indulgence** — After a millennium of pleasure Yayāti realizes desire only grows, returns Pūru's youth, and retires to the forest attaining heaven _(actors: Yayāti, Pūru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 88; Bhāgavata 9.19)
- **Yogis See the Self-Power of the Deva** — Practitioners of dhyana-yoga, through meditation, perceive the hidden self-power (devatma-shakti) of God veiled by its own qualities, identifying the personal Lord as the first cause _(actors: meditating sages, the Deva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/svetashvatara-upanishad.md) — (Shvetashvatara Upanishad 1.3)
- **Agastya Destroys Ilvala** — Enraged that his brother is digested, Ilvala is reduced to ashes by the fire from Agastya's glance, and the sage departs with the riches he sought _(actors: Agastya, Ilvala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
- **Agni Purified by Worshipping Shiva at Kanjanur** — The fire-god Agni worships Shiva at Kanjanur to be purified, giving the temple its name Agnishvarar _(actors: Agni, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Sthala-purana)
- **Ambarisha's Prayer Spares Durvasa** — After a year of pursuit Durvasa falls at the king's feet; Ambarisha prays the Sudarshana-stuti, the discus relents, and the king feeds Durvasa before breaking his own fast _(actors: Ambarisha, Durvasa, Sudarshana-cakra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.5.1-20)
- **Bhrāmarī Devī slays Aruṇāsura** — When the demon Aruṇa, immune to harm from any two-footed creature, threatens the gods, the Goddess takes the form of Bhrāmarī and swarms of six-legged bees and wasps tear his army apart _(actors: Bhrāmarī Devī, Aruṇāsura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha X)
- **Birth of Durga from combined tejas** — The enraged gods emit tejas that coalesces into the eighteen-armed Goddess Durga/Chandika, each body-part formed from a specific god's light _(actors: Durga, Vishnu, Shiva, Brahma, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 2)
- **Candra abducts Tara and the Tarakamaya war** — Candra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, triggering the Tarakamaya war until Brahma intervenes; from the union Budha is born, founding the Lunar line _(actors: Candra, Tara, Brihaspati, Budha, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Vishnu Purana)
- **Chandra cursed by Ganesha** — Chandra mocks Ganesha's broken-tusk form and is cursed so that whoever sees the Moon on Ganesha Chaturthi is falsely accused _(actors: Chandra, Ganesha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Puranic/folk)
- **Daksha's sacrifice destroyed; Shiva weds Uma** — The Vamana Purana narrates Sati's self-immolation at Daksha's sacrifice, Shiva's wrecking of the yajna, and his later marriage to Parvati/Uma _(actors: Sati, Daksha, Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana)
- **Daksha-yajna wrecked by Virabhadra** — Daksha's sacrifice slights Shiva and is wrecked by Virabhadra and Bhadrakali — Bhaga's eye and Pushan's teeth are struck — until Shiva is honored and order restored _(actors: Daksha, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Shiva, Bhaga, Pushan)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana)
- **Division of the Veda by the 28 Vyasas** — The Veda is recurringly redacted by a Vyasa in each Dvapara, situating Krishna-Dvaipayana as the 28th, one per mahayuga across the manvantara _(actors: the 28 Vyasas, Krishna-Dvaipayana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 3))
- **Ganesha Recovers the Chintamani Jewel at Theur** — After the greedy prince Guna steals sage Kapila's wish-fulfilling Chintamani jewel, Ganesha slays Guna and recovers it, becoming Chintamani Vinayaka _(actors: Guna, Kapila, Ganesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ashtavinayaka.md) — (Ganesha Purana tradition)
- **Ganesha Slays Sindhu at Morgaon** — Ganesha as the peacock-rider Mayureshwar slays the demon Sindhu, founding the adi node of the Ashtavinayaka at Morgaon _(actors: Ganesha, Sindhu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/temple-networks-and-circuits.md) — (Ashtavinayaka sthala-purana)
- **Indra incurs Brahmahatya and hides** — Because the Puranic Vritra/Vishvarupa is a brahmana, killing him incurs Brahmahatya; crushed by the sin, Indra shrinks into a lotus stalk and vanishes, leaving Svarga kingless _(actors: Indra, Vishvarupa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/indra.md) — (Bhagavata; Mahabharata, Udyoga/Shanti Parva)
- **Śiva slays Tripura and Andhaka** — The Śiva Purāṇa records Śiva's slaying of the Tripura demons and of Andhaka _(actors: Śiva, Andhaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Śiva Whispers the Tāraka-Mantra at Death** — At the moment of death within Kashi, Śiva whispers the ferry-mantra into the dying's ear, cutting the knot of karma and granting immediate liberation regardless of prior deeds _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Kacha killed thrice and revived; the belly reversal** — The asuras murder Kacha three times, finally feeding his ashes to Śukra in wine; Śukra teaches the Sañjīvanī from inside his own belly, Kacha bursts out killing the guru and then revives him _(actors: Kacha, Śukra, Devayānī, the asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **King Bhaṅgāśvana becomes a woman** — A king transformed into a woman bears children as both sexes and, asked to choose, keeps the female form, declaring a mother's love and a woman's pleasure greater _(actors: Bhaṅgāśvana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/13-anushasana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 13.12)
- **Kālī slays Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa** — Kālī springs from Caṇḍikā's brow and beheads the generals Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, earning the name Cāmuṇḍā _(actors: Kālī (Cāmuṇḍā), Caṇḍikā, Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devī Māhātmya ch.7)
- **Krittika nurses suckle Kartikeya/Skanda** — The six Pleiad-nurses of the Krittika nakshatra suckle the war-god Karttikeya/Skanda, the origin of his name _(actors: The six Krittikas, Skanda/Kartikeya)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/nakshatras.md) — (Puranic)
- **Murugan's Marriage to Valli at Tiruttani** — At Tiruttani Murugan woos and weds Valli, the hunter-girl of the kurinci hills, the indigenous Tamil love-marriage counterpart to Deivanai _(actors: Murugan, Valli)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/arupadai-veedu-murugan.md) — (Tirumurukarruppatai; Kanda Puranam; Paripadal)
- **Mustering of the Goddess's army of śaktis** — Lalitā fields Vārāhī/Daṇḍanāthā as commander, Śyāmalā/Mantriṇī (Mātaṅgī) as prime minister, child-goddess Bālā, the Nityās, yoginīs and śaktis born of her own body _(actors: Lalitā, Vārāhī (Daṇḍanāthā), Śyāmalā (Mantriṇī/Mātaṅgī), Bālā, the Nityās and yoginīs)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lalita-bhandasura.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Lalitopākhyāna); Lalitā Sahasranāma)
- **Nara–Nārāyaṇa in the Bhāgavata avatāra rosters** — The Bhāgavata Purāṇa lists Nara-Nārāyaṇa among Viṣṇu's līlā-avatāras as the tapas-and-dharma exemplifying descent, outside the fixed canonical Daśāvatāra _(actors: Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa, Nara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.4; SB 1.3)
- **Oppiliappan Served Food Without Salt** — The founding legend of Tiruvinnagar where Vishnu as Oppiliappan vows to accept food served without salt, marking the marriage to Bhumi Devi _(actors: Vishnu (Oppiliappan), Bhumi Devi)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (sthala-purana)
- **Origin of the four Shaktis from Shiva** — Four Goddess-energies (Shaktis) arise from Shiva, a Shakta theophany folded into the Shaiva cosmology _(actors: Shiva, the four Shaktis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Parvati's rebirth and tapas** — Sati is reborn as Parvati, daughter of Himavan, and wins the ascetic Shiva through severe penance _(actors: Parvati, Himavan, Shiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Parvati-khanda))
- **Purāṇic geography — seven dvīpas and Meru** — Systematic geography of Jambūdvīpa, the concentric continents and oceans, Mount Meru as world-axis, the varṣas of Bhārata and the motion of the heavenly bodies _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Satī's Self-Immolation at Māyāpurī** — In a local telling Satī performs her yogic self-immolation at Māyāpurī, sitting in dhyāna and consuming her body by inner fire (linked to Daksha's spoiled sacrifice at Kankhal) _(actors: Satī, Daksha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia / temple tradition)
- **Satyakāma Jābāla's truthful lineage** — The boy Satyakāma honestly reports his unknown parentage; teacher Gautama accepts him as a true brāhmaṇa, and the elements and birds teach him the quarters of Brahman _(actors: Satyakāma Jābāla, Jabālā, Gautama Hāridrumata)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.4–4.9)
- **Satyavan revived and every boon fulfilled** — Yama looses the noose granting Satyavan four hundred years; Satyavan revives, Dyumatsena's sight and throne are restored as the usurper dies, and both Savitri and Ashvapati gain a hundred sons _(actors: Satyavan, Savitri, Dyumatsena, Ashvapati, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/savitri-satyavan.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 297)
- **Shiva Slays Dushana as Mahakala at Ujjain** — Shiva emerges as Mahakala to slay the demon Dushana who tormented the devout brahmin Vridhi and the pious king, founding the Mahakaleshwar jyotirlinga at Ujjain _(actors: Shiva (Mahakala), Dushana, Vridhi)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Siddhidatri grants Shiva his powers** — The Navadurga form Siddhidatri is said to have given Shiva his occult powers, making him Ardhanarishvara _(actors: Siddhidatri, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Kavaca; Devi-Bhagavata Purana)
- **Six-fold birth of Kārtikeya** — The seed becomes six infants in the reeds suckled by the six Kṛttikās; Pārvatī's embrace fuses them into the six-faced, twelve-armed Ṣaṇmukha _(actors: Kārtikeya (Skanda), the Kṛttikās, Pārvatī, Agni, Svāhā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Skanda Purāṇa, Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Tat tvam asi — Uddālaka teaches Śvetaketu** — Uddālaka Āruṇi instructs his son Śvetaketu nine times that 'That thou art,' teaching the identity of the self with universal Being _(actors: Uddālaka Āruṇi, Śvetaketu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7)
- **The Ashtavakra Gita Spoken to Janaka** — Ashtavakra instructs King Janaka in radical Advaita non-dualism, with Janaka voicing his own awakening mid-dialogue _(actors: Ashtavakra, Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashtavakra.md) — (Ashtavakra Gita)
- **The co-wife quarrel of Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī** — Viṣṇu's three consorts quarrel and curse one another, explaining why Gaṅgā descends to earth and Sarasvatī becomes a river _(actors: Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Prakṛti-khaṇḍa))
- **The Spider, Serpent and Elephant at Srikalahasti** — A spider, a serpent and an elephant each worship the Vayu-linga in their own way until their daily worship clashes; all three attain moksha and their names fuse into Sri-Kala-Hasti _(actors: spider, serpent, elephant, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Srikalahasti mahatmya)
- **Vishnu Tricks Vrika into Self-Destruction** — Vishnu, as a brahmana boy, plants doubt in Vrika and dares him to test the boon on himself, so Vrika lays his hand on his own head and his skull shatters _(actors: Vishnu, Vrika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.26-37)
- **Viśvakarman forges the vajra from Dadhīci's spine** — The divine architect Viśvakarman fashions the adamantine thunderbolt (vajra) and other weapons from Dadhīci's bones, hammering the vajra specifically from his backbone _(actors: Viśvakarman, Dadhīci)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.10)
- **Winning of Bāṇāī the Dhangar wife** — Khaṇḍobā in pastoral guise herds sheep to win Bāṇāī, a Dhangar shepherd woman; the two-wife structure unites agrarian and pastoral communities _(actors: Khaṇḍobā, Bāṇāī, Dhangars, Mhāḷsā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Marathi folk tradition; ovī oral epics [folk/regional])
- **Yama's Boon to His Sister Yamuna at Yamunotri** — Yama grants his sister Yamuna the boon that bathing in or touching her water grants a painless death, the significance of the Yamunotri shrine _(actors: Yama, Yamuna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (regional mahatmya)
- **Yayāti falls from heaven and is saved by his grandsons** — Cast out of svarga for pride, Yayāti is restored by the merit of his daughter Mādhavī's four royal-sage sons _(actors: Yayāti, Indra, Mādhavī, Aṣṭaka, Śibi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva 120–122)
- **Yājñavalkya defeats the sages at Janaka's court** — At King Janaka's great sacrifice Yājñavalkya claims the prize cattle and defeats challenger after challenger (Aśvala, Ārtabhāga, Bhujyu, Uṣasta, Kahola, Gārgī, Uddālaka) on Brahman and the Self _(actors: Yājñavalkya, Janaka, Gārgī, Uddālaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.1–3.9)
- **Abhijit descends and contests Rohini for seniority** — In the Mahabharata, the star Abhijit slips down from the sky contesting with Rohini for seniority, narrated to Skanda/Indra as why an extra (28th) nakshatra was needed; it becomes the nakshatra of victory _(actors: Abhijit, Rohini, Skanda/Indra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/nakshatras.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva III)
- **Ambarisha Attains the Lord's Abode** — Having demonstrated bhagavata-dharma perfectly, Ambarisha in old age divides his kingdom among his sons, retires to the forest, and attains the abode of Vishnu _(actors: Ambarisha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.5.25-28)
- **Attukal Amma identified with Kannagi** — The Attukal Bhagavathy charter identifies the goddess with Kannagi of the Silappatikaram, who burned Madurai in vengeance, grounding the women-only Attukal Pongala offering _(actors: Attukal Amma, Kannagi)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Silappatikaram; Kerala folklore)
- **Bhasmasura Destroyed by Mohini's Dance** — In the folk version, the ash-demon Bhasmasura wins the incinerate-by-touch boon, turns on Shiva, and Vishnu as Mohini dances him into laying his hand on his own head, reducing him to ashes _(actors: Bhasmasura, Shiva, Mohini)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Regional/folk tradition)
- **Bṛhaspati proclaims ahiṃsā the highest dharma** — Bṛhaspati delivers the celebrated declaration that non-violence is the highest dharma, self-control, gift, and austerity, counselling universal compassion _(actors: Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/13-anushasana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 13.117)
- **Bhrigu kicks Vishnu's chest (the Bhrigu-test)** — The Prajapati Bhrigu kicks Vishnu's chest to decide the supreme god, earning the foot-mark Shrivatsa _(actors: Bhrigu, Vishnu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.89; Mahabharata; Padma Purana)
- **Birth and beheading of Gaṇeśa (Śani-gaze version)** — Pārvatī obtains a son by the Puṇyaka-vrata; Śani's inauspicious gaze severs the infant's head, and Viṣṇu fetches a young elephant's head (Airāvata's calf) to restore him _(actors: Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa, Śani, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Gaṇeśa-khaṇḍa))
- **Burning of Kama (Kama-dahana)** — Kamadeva, sent to rekindle desire in the ascetic Shiva, is burned to ash by Shiva's third eye and later restored bodiless as Ananga _(actors: Shiva, Kamadeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Parvati-khanda))
- **Chaṇḍī Slays Śumbha and Niśumbha** — The goddess Chaṇḍī/Chaṇḍikā slays the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha and their generals Chaṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the deed enshrined at Chaṇḍī Devī on Nīl Parvat _(actors: Chaṇḍī, Śumbha, Niśumbha, Chaṇḍa, Muṇḍa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Devi Mahatmya)
- **Creation of Lopamudra** — Fearing his ancestors hang in limbo for want of offspring, Agastya assembles the most beautiful limbs of all creatures and infuses the child into the queen of Vidarbha, born as Lopamudra _(actors: Agastya, Lopamudra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
- **Cross-tradition identity as Mailāra/Mallanna/Khaṇḍerāo** — The deity is recognized across the Deccan as a single god under regional names (Mailāralinga, Mallanna, Khaṇḍerāo), with Kannada Mailāra as the older stratum _(actors: Khaṇḍobā/Mailāra/Mallanna, Goṛava and Vāghyā-Muraḷī devotees)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/khandoba-martanda-bhairava.md) — (Kannada Mailāra and Telugu Mallanna traditions [folk/regional]; modern scholarship)
- **Devī slays Mahiṣāsura and Śumbha–Niśumbha** — The Devī Māhātmya narrates the Goddess Durgā slaying the buffalo-demon Mahiṣāsura and the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha _(actors: Devī/Durgā, Mahiṣāsura, Śumbha, Niśumbha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa (Devī Māhātmya))
- **Durga assembled from the devas' tejas** — The supreme warrior Durga is assembled from the combined radiant energy of all the devas to slay Mahishasura _(actors: Durga, the devas, Mahishasura)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Devi Mahatmya)
- **Gajendra seized by the crocodile** — Gajendra, an elephant-king (cursed former king Indradyumna), is seized by the leg by a crocodile (the cursed gandharva Hūhū) while gathering lotuses on Mount Trikūṭa _(actors: Gajendra, the crocodile/Hūhū)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.2–8.4)
- **Ganesha wins the race around the parents** — Set a race to circle the world for a divine fruit, Ganesha circumambulates his parents declaring they are his whole world, winning over Kartikeya _(actors: Ganesha, Kartikeya, Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Skanda Purana)
- **Indra slays Triśiras and Vṛtra (Śākta reframing)** — Indra slays the three-headed Triśiras (Viśvarūpa) and the dragon Vṛtra, then purifies the resulting brahmahatyā guilt through Goddess-worship _(actors: Indra, Triśiras, Vṛtra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha VI)
- **Indra slays Vṛtra with the Dadhīci-vajra** — Armed with the vajra forged from Dadhīci's spine, Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra, releasing the cosmic waters and restoring world order; in the Bhāgavata Vṛtra dies a willing devotee and attains liberation _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.11–13)
- **King Suratha and merchant Samadhi worship the Devi** — The dethroned king Suratha and the merchant Samadhi worship the Goddess under the sage Medhas; Suratha is destined to be reborn as the future 8th Savarni Manu _(actors: Suratha, Samadhi, Medhas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana (Devi Mahatmya frame))
- **Kālī springs from Durgā's brow and slays Raktabīja** — In the battle with Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa, and Raktabīja, Kālī springs from Durgā's forehead and drinks Raktabīja's cloning blood to win _(actors: Kālī, Durgā, Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa, Raktabīja)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Devī Māhātmya ch. 7-8)
- **Lakshmi re-emerges and weds Vishnu** — The goddess of fortune rises radiant from the ocean and of her own choice garlands and weds Vishnu, restoring sri to the cosmos _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **March on Śūnyaka in the Śrīcakra chariots** — Lalitā rides the nine-tiered Cakra-rāja-ratha, with Mantriṇī on Geya-cakra and Vārāhī on Kiri-cakra, advancing on Bhaṇḍāsura's city _(actors: Lalitā, Mantriṇī, Vārāhī, the śakti host)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lalita-bhandasura.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Lalitopākhyāna))
- **Markandeya witnesses the pralaya** — The deathless Markandeya survives a dissolution, floating on the cosmic waters and seeing the infant Vishnu on the banyan leaf _(actors: Markandeya, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Puranas)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya's Penance Tested by Kāmadeva** — Fearing the sage's austerity, Indra sends Kāmadeva, spring and apsarases to break his penance, but Mārkaṇḍeya remains unmoved _(actors: Indra, Kāmadeva, Vasanta, Apsarās, Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.8)
- **Nahusha usurps Svarga and is cursed** — During Indra's absence the mortal king Nahusha is crowned regent, lusts after Shachi, and kicks sage Agastya, who curses him to fall as a serpent; Indra is then restored _(actors: Nahusha, Shachi, Agastya, Indra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/indra.md) — (Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva)
